New `src/ui/press.ts`: three press kinds (primary = scale 0.97 + darker volt, surface = fill/border lift, quiet = opacity), 120ms ease-out in / 90ms ease-in out, transform+opacity+colour only, `useReducedMotion` drops the scale but keeps the colour (reduced motion means less movement, not less feedback). Applied to 24 controls across Now, Goals, Settings, Recap. | Read the live inline style mid-press: LOG SET `transform: scale(0.97); background-color: rgb(178,222,0)` at 120ms cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), releasing to 90ms ease-in; PROGRESS `opacity: 0.5`; -45 fill rgb(22,28,34) + border rgb(46,56,65); all three return exactly to idle. 860 tests green. NB getComputedStyle read at t=0 of the transition reports the START value — measure the inline style, or wait past the duration. | next: route transitions — Now to Goals is an instant cut with no motion at all

- **R113 — the rail band, and five more from the batch. 860 tests green.** **The band that kept cutting its chips off.** Third time. It was pinned to `L.railHeight + 10`, a number the model computed and the stylesheet had to match EXACTLY, and neither the band's own margin nor its padding nor its rule were in that arithmetic — so the chips ran past the bottom and came out shaved. The fixed height is gone: the band sizes to its content, which cannot be wrong, and `railHeight` stays in the model purely as the RESERVE the fit math budgets (now +22, and it only has to be generous, never exact). Measured after: band 79px, chips clearing the rule by 13px. **The + asks before it logs.** Copying the last set outright was fast and wrong — the commonest reason to add a set to a lift further up the session is that it was DIFFERENT, so a silent copy recorded something that never happened. It opens the set sheet on those numbers as a starting point. **FINISH is no longer one-way**: `reopenSession` clears the end time and nothing else, so the workout you just finished can be corrected as ONE session instead of being split in two by a new one. **Progress has a history** — the last eight workouts, newest first, each with its lifts and top sets. Sorted by the last SET's time, not `startedAt`: a restored backup or any fixed-clock fixture gives sessions the same start and the order falls back to map iteration. Two of my own test assumptions were wrong and the model was right — the top set is by e1RM (145x8 beats 155x5 on Epley), and the title has to agree with `sessionDay` rather than a literal. **"Don't ask which machine"** — a checkbox in the equipment sheet where the cost is paid, the same switch in Settings because a preference reachable only through the sheet you are trying to stop seeing cannot be undone, and a second tap on MACHINE turns the question back on. **Not started: the extra split plans and the custom plan builder.** The ones worth adding (bro split, Arnold) do not derive from push/pull/legs the way upper/lower and full body do, so they need plan-days defined by MUSCLE GROUP — which `muscles.ts` now makes possible — plus a builder and a place to store it. That is the right shape and it is a chunk, not a patch, so it is left clean rather than half-done in the first-run flow.
- **R112 — the reason line is gone from the Now screen. 843 tests green.** R111 gave the day rail a second line under the heading explaining why the suggested lift was suggested. It was too much text on the one path §4 keeps bare: the rail already answers "what next" by putting that chip first, and a sentence about the ranking is a thing to READ in the middle of a set. Removed, and the band went back to 76px. The reason itself survives as the chip's accessible name — "Tricep Extension, suggested next: finishes what your compound started" — where it costs no pixels and is still there for anyone who cannot see the order. `RAIL_WHY` is kept as a zero rather than deleted, because the lesson it was carrying is worth keeping: the band is a FIXED height, and the one time something was drawn inside it without being counted, it cut 2px off the bottom of the very chip it was describing.
- **R111 — a twelve-item request batch, worked end to end. 843 tests green.** **Goals.** The filter row was clipping mid-chip at 390px — five chips need 405px and the row had 342, so PULL's count sheared in half at the edge and LEGS and DONE sat off-screen with no visible way to reach them. It wraps now instead of scrolling sideways, which also removes the need to drag it at all. REMOVE became WIPE with a confirm, plus WIPE ALL that asks three times with escalating copy, and BOTH are undoable — `removeGoals` returns what it took so the undo hands the same goals back, `createdAt` and all, which is what keeps the progress bar where it was. The target no longer resets when the rep count changes: it was recomputed from `suggestTarget` on every tap of the FOR (REPS) row, so dialling 315 and then changing your mind about the reps turned it back into 185. **Now.** Tapping a logged set EDITS it (weight, reps, and a free-text note for RIR, tempo, which machine) instead of arming it for destruction — removal moved the set to the end of the session with a new time, so fixing a middle set silently reordered the workout. A + beside UNDO repeats that lift's last set without leaving the lift you are on. Typed reps go to three digits, not two. Schema is at v4 for the note column. **Recommendations, with the research behind them.** New `domain/muscles.ts` maps the library to prime movers and encodes what the literature actually says about order: compounds before isolations for the same muscle (pre-exhaustion costs the compound 10-30% of its load for no measured benefit), shared prime movers are what not to stack back to back (bench, incline and overhead press all run on chest, anterior delt and triceps), and order matters far less than volume (effect size 0.03 across 11 studies) — which is why it suggests with a stated reason rather than restricting. After a bench press the rail now opens on TRICEP EXTENSION with "finishes what your compound started", exactly as asked. Two tuning passes were needed and both were the model teaching me something: the overlap penalty was punishing the triceps isolation for the very overlap that makes it correct, and once fixed the bonus was strong enough to beat a compound on a FRESH muscle, which inverts compound-first. Sources are in `RECOMMENDATION_SOURCES` so the advice can be checked. **Settings, as a real screen.** §9 banned one; the product owner overruled it. Split, units with a real lb↔kg conversion shown rather than described, language (full Spanish, `missingKeys` proves the table is complete), jump amounts. Weights are never converted on write — the stored number is the fact. **Layout.** The NEXT ON band was cutting its own chips by 2px because I added the reason line inside a FIXED-height band without telling the height model; CLEAR and FINISH were shoved against the right edge with 200px of nothing beside them and now centre on the column like every other row; and the type scale is one file instead of five sizes doing the job of body text and three doing section labels.
- **R110 — walked the whole goal chain end to end, and it holds. 797 tests green.** Seeded 36 goals, chose LEG DAY, logged a squat, switched to Romanian Deadlift from the rail, and put 260 × 8 against a 222 × 3 target. Every surface said the right thing in the right order: the Now line read "97 to 222 × 3" then flipped to a volt "goal hit: 222 × 3"; the recap came out carrying BOTH the personal record (260 × 8, +135 lb) AND "Romanian Deadlift: 222 × 3. Done." on the row under it, which is exactly what R101 was for — before it, a session with a PR dropped the goal entirely. Goals chips moved OPEN 31→30, LEGS 5→4, DONE 5→6. No defects found, which after fourteen rounds of changes is the result worth having. HANDOFF.md brought up to date in the same pass — counts, and a section covering R96–R109 for whoever picks this up next.
- **R109 — the card's top row grew a third thing, so it got the truncation guard before it needed it. 797 tests green.** R108 put CHANGE next to REMOVE, which turns a two-element row into a three-element one. Measured across all 31 cards with the library's longest name, "Machine Chest Press": no overlap, but only 76px of slack on a 430px column — which is 23px on a 375px phone and NEGATIVE for any movement the user invents with a longer name, and inventing movements is a feature. `flexShrink: 1` plus `numberOfLines={1}` on the name, `flexShrink: 0` on the controls, so the name ellipsizes rather than shoving the buttons off the card. Same lesson as the exercise name on the Now screen, applied before the report rather than after it. Also pinned the R108 rule that an achieved goal has no CHANGE control — a test that reads the guard sits BEFORE the control it hides, since a conditional in the wrong place still compiles and still renders.
- **R108 — a goal can be amended without throwing away what it has earned. 795 tests green.** There was no edit: changing a target or pushing a deadline out meant REMOVE and set a new one, and that quietly reset the thing the progress bar is measured from. `start` is what the lift could do WHEN THE GOAL WAS SET, so a recreated goal reads as zero progress however much of the distance is already covered — someone 40 lb into a 60 lb climb who moves their deadline out by a month would watch the bar drop to empty and the pace judgement go silent. CHANGE keeps the id and `createdAt`; the lift is fixed and stated rather than chosen, because a goal is a target ON a lift and moving it would take the baseline to another movement's history. An achieved goal has no CHANGE control at all — editing it would rewrite the target it was met against. **Two checks had to learn about editing:** every edit is a duplicate of itself, and an edit made at the cap is one goal too many, so `validateNewGoal` takes the id being amended and drops it from `existing` first. **And the running app caught what the tests could not.** The sheet opened on the 222 that was set, one tap of "+45" saved **185** — the stepper was counting from a fresh 140 lb suggestion the moment it was touched, so one press of PLUS was a 37 lb reduction, with nothing on screen saying which number it was adding to. Pulled the rule out into `targetBase()` so it is a tested function rather than an expression buried in JSX. Verified end to end: 222 → 267, the card reads "142 lb from a 267" and "68 days left · behind pace" — the pace flipping to behind is itself the proof the baseline survived, since a recreated goal would have gone silent instead.
- **R107 — the cost of R104, paid back. 787 tests green.** Putting the goal on the Now screen means `state()` reads `repo.goals()`, and `state()` runs on every render — which during rest is once a SECOND for the whole timer. `goals()` was a fresh SQLite query every time, unlike `allSets()`, which has been memoised since the day a five-year history made `state()` cost 47ms. Same treatment: one array, one flag, dropped by `saveGoal`, `deleteGoal` and `eraseAll`, frozen because callers keep it. On the Goals screen it also removes one query per card per render, and the cap is a hundred. **Every test here is a write followed by a read**, because staleness is the only thing a cache can get wrong: a new goal visible immediately (the empty read must not stick), an updated one reading back updated, a deleted one gone, `eraseAll` clearing it, and the array frozen so one screen's sort cannot reorder what another is reading. Plus one asserting the second read is the SAME array — without it the whole suite would pass with no cache at all.
- **R106 — took the decision R105 left open: the goal hit gets the volt. 781 tests green.** §15 allows one accent and it was already spent on LOG SET and the hero, so this was a real choice rather than a default. Made it in favour: a grey "goal hit" is a whisper where a normal voice is warranted, and at 15px beside a 159px hero it is a different size class — it draws the eye without competing for it. A gap still to close stays grey, because that is information rather than news. **The refactor it needed is the interesting part.** Colouring half a line means a nested `Text`, so the state now carries `lastTime` as `{head, tail, hit}` instead of one string. `lastTimeLine()` survives as the composed string — it is what the model tests assert on — and the ten places that read the STATE field compose through one `lineOf()` helper, so there is still exactly one definition of what the line says. Nesting is also where `numberOfLines` quietly stops applying, so there is a test that the row is still capped at one and that the parent still has the definite width ellipsis needs. Verified on the running app: parent grey rgb(124,135,146), child volt rgb(204,255,0), `nowrap` and `ellipsis` both intact on a 390px box.
- **R105 — the set that hits a goal now says so, in the moment. 779 tests green.** Hitting a target you chose months ago is the most postable thing that happens in this app, and on the logging screen it passed in complete silence: the line just stopped saying anything, next session. The recap tells the story afterwards; this says it while you are still standing there. Same line, same row — "Last time  125 × 8 · goal hit: 222 × 3" — so it costs no vertical space, no tap and no interruption. **The rule that keeps it honest: only in the session that did it.** The check is the same history with THIS session's sets removed — the state the user walked in with — so a goal met last month stays quiet. Without that, the line would read "goal hit" every time you touched the lift for the rest of the year, which is exactly the crying wolf §8 forbids of the PR badge. Walked it on the seeded app: Romanian Deadlift showed "97 to 222 × 3", logging 305 flipped the same line to "goal hit: 222 × 3", and the Goals chips went OPEN 31→30, LEGS 5→4, DONE 5→6. Four surfaces — the logging line, the goal card, the filter counts and the recap — agreeing about one event. **Next:** the "goal hit" clause is grey like the rest of the line. §15 allows one volt accent and it is spent on LOG SET and the hero, so colouring it means splitting the line into nested Text and deciding whether this beats the hero for attention. Worth a decision rather than a default.
- **R104 — the goal now shows on the screen where the lift is actually being trained. 774 tests green.** Goals lived on their own screen and on the recap, so while you were under the bar the app said nothing about the target you had set for that exact lift — the one moment the number can change what you do next. It reads "Last time  125 × 8   ·   97 to 222 × 3" now. **It rides the last-time line rather than taking a row of its own**, which is the whole design constraint: §4's logging path must not scroll, R94 and R95 were both fights over vertical space, and a new row would have bought this at the cost of the day rail on a short phone. Measured at 218px natural width in a 390px column, so it fits a 320px phone with room; `numberOfLines={1}` plus `alignSelf: 'stretch'` (numberOfLines can only ellipsize against a DEFINITE width — the same trap the exercise name hit) means a long one truncates the goal before the last-time numbers, which is the right order. **Two decisions worth keeping.** The rep count is printed — a gap to "185" means nothing without it, since a 20 lb gap at five reps is not a 20 lb gap at ten, and the user may well be doing eights right now. And an ACHIEVED goal prints nothing: it would otherwise sit on that line for every future session of the lift, and the trophy already has a home. The number comes from `goalProgress`, the same function the goal card and the Progress row use, so three screens cannot disagree about how far away a target is — verified against the seeded fixture, where Goals says "97 lb from a 222 romanian deadlift" and Now says "97 to 222 × 3".
- **R103 — swept the defect class R102 tripped over: 24 tests that could silently stop testing. 769 tests green.** The source-reading layout tests slice out the block they care about with a bare `indexOf`, and `slice(-1)` does not throw — it returns the LAST CHARACTER of the file, or the empty string with two anchors. Every `assert.match` against that fails and every `assert.doesNotMatch` PASSES, so a moved anchor either invents a confident wrong diagnosis or quietly asserts nothing at all. 24 sites across 12 files were exposed; one of them had already bitten, last round. All of them now go through `test/helpers/source.ts` — `region` / `upTo` / `around` — which name the missing anchor in the failure. `region` also looks for the CLOSING anchor after the opening one, which the hand-rolled version at `recap-layout.test.ts:187` had to do by nesting a second `indexOf` inside the first, and which the others simply got wrong in a way that returns an empty region. **Two tests guard the guard:** one asserting each helper throws on a missing anchor (and demonstrating, in an assertion, that the old form returns `'a'` instead), and a standing sweep over all 40 test files that fails on the twenty-fifth bare `slice(indexOf(...))` — written by someone who will never have read any of this. That sweep also checks its own regex still matches the thing it is meant to catch, because a lint test that has stopped matching is the same silent failure one level up.
- **R102 — walked the whole app from an empty database, after six rounds of changing it. 759 tests green.** Everything since R96 was built and judged against a 36-goal fixture; none of it had been seen by a new user. Cleared storage and walked §13's kill test end to end: Goals cold (no filter bar, correct — under five goals every chip would hide a card already on screen), the add sheet intact through the fragment restructure (28 movements, a 135 lb suggestion, no YOUR LIFTS heading with nothing trained), Progress cold, then a first-ever session — three sets, FINISH — producing a complete recap with the SESSION ONE slab, "45 × 8", THE ONE TO BEAT, the lift list and SHARE. **One real defect, caused by R96:** pinning the add button to the bottom edge left the sentence explaining an empty Goals screen at y93 and the only control that acts on it at y1127, with a thousand pixels of nothing between — the two halves of an empty state have to read as one thing. Centred while the list is empty. **And a test that had quietly stopped testing anything:** two layout assertions anchor on `SOURCE.indexOf('<ScrollView contentContainerStyle={s.body}')`, which I broke by making that prop an array. `indexOf` returns -1, `slice(-1)` silently hands back the last character rather than throwing, and the test reported "the add button is inside the scrolling list again" — a confident, specific, completely wrong diagnosis. It now asserts the anchor was found before trusting the slice.
- **R101 — the goals never reached the thing that leaves the app. 758 tests green.** Rendered the recap to a real PNG and looked at it. The claim slab takes the best true claim in order — PR beats first-session beats standing goal — and that order is right, but it means a lifter who is PROGRESSING sets PRs, so the goal branch never fires for them and their goals never reach the artifact at all. §5 says goals earn their place by feeding the output; "only on the sessions where nothing happened" is not feeding it. The goal line now has its own row under the lift list. **The trade had to be got right, and my first attempt got it backwards:** reserving the row unconditionally cost TWO rows on an ordinary five-lift session — the pitch has a 56px floor, so the shortened band fell one row short and the card came out as three lifts and "+2 more". The lifts are what the user actually did. Both layouts are measured now and the goal line is drawn only when it costs the list nothing; on a heavy session it simply does not appear. Six pixel-level tests on the rendered canvas, including one that counts list rows with and without the goal line and asserts they match. **Then the same defect turned up one layer up, in the SHARE TEXT** — and there the comment above the code described the correct behaviour ("it survives a PR day… it follows the work rather than leading it") while the condition read `!payload.pr &&`, which drops the goal precisely on the days the comment was about. Nothing tested it in that direction. Fixed, with a test that the goal FOLLOWS the record rather than leading it. **Worth keeping:** the card defect was invisible to every test and to the app — it took rendering the image and looking at it, and the e2e proof had never once passed a `goalLine` in, so the branch it was meant to prove had never been drawn. `link/dist` needed rebuilding too; the suite catches that, which is why it exists.
- **R100 — caught my own regression from R97, and a chip that was lying. 750 tests green.** **(a) The regression.** R97 took lifts that already have a goal out of the add sheet, which was right — but it excluded ACHIEVED goals too, and that put back at the picker exactly what R39 had removed from the validator. Hitting a 225 squat and wanting 275 is the single most likely next thing a user does; before R39 the app said "you already have a goal for this lift", and after my change the lift simply VANISHED from the sheet — quieter, and no more helpful. `activeGoals`, not `goals`: one LIVE goal per lift, everywhere. The domain layer had this right the whole time (`canAddGoal`, `validateNewGoal` and the cap all count live goals only); the new UI layer was the one that forgot. Confirmed on the running app: the sheet now offers exactly the five lifts whose goals are met, each with a fresh suggested target. **(b) The chip said ALL and meant OPEN.** It excludes met goals — so on a screen holding 36, the chip read "ALL 31" while DONE read 5. Renamed through the type, not just the label: `GoalFilter` is `'open' | SplitDay | 'done'` now, so OPEN and DONE are the pair of states they actually are, with the split days sitting under OPEN as subsets of it. **Worth writing down:** the defect was in the layer I had just added, and the layer underneath it had been correct for sixty rounds. A new surface over settled rules is a chance to contradict them quietly — the validator would still have refused the goal, so nothing would have thrown; the lift would just never have been offered.
- **R99 — the Goals screen remembers what it was showing, for exactly as long as it should. 749 tests green.** Goals is a place you leave and come back to inside one workout — check the pull numbers, go log a set, come back — and at a hundred goals, re-filtering every time is the screen refusing to remember what you just told it. The filter and sort now survive navigation. **Deliberately in memory, not in the database:** a filter that survives a restart is a MODE — open the app a week later, see eleven goals, and the fact that thirty-one exist is something you have to notice a highlighted chip to work out. In a module variable it lasts exactly as long as the reason for it does, and a cold start is always the whole list; there is a test that re-imports the module to prove it. **One guard came with it:** the remembered filter falls back to ALL whenever it holds nothing. A zero chip cannot be tapped, so the only ways to land on an empty filter are removing the last goal it held or arriving with one this screen remembered — and in both cases an empty screen is the wrong answer to "show me my goals". Verified by filtering to PULL / SOONEST, leaving via DONE, and coming back through the Now screen's GOALS link: both still set. **Next:** with a hundred slots, setting a goal per lift is a hundred trips through the sheet — the cap is fillable in principle and punishing in practice. Worth deciding whether bulk creation earns its complexity or whether the sheet just needs to be faster.
- **R98 — raising the cap made two screens quadratic, and nothing said so. 746 tests green.** Benchmarked what a hundred goals actually costs: `rankGoals` was **48ms per render** at 100 goals against 20,000 sets — a dropped frame or several on a phone, on a screen that recomputes on every add and delete. `goalProgress` reads the history twice per goal and `bestAt` FILTERED the whole list to apply its cutoff, so every goal allocated a fresh copy of every set the user has ever logged. Bucketing by exercise once, plus a single-pass `bestAt`: **0.9ms**, 53x. Safe only because every read `goalProgress` makes was already scoped to that goal's own exercise — pinned by a test that runs the old undivided computation and asserts the numbers are identical, and by one proving a 500 lb leg press cannot leak into a squat goal. **The same shape was next door on Progress**, and worse in a subtle way: rows kept alive purely because they carry a goal (`spared`) grow with the GOAL count, so the cap change made that screen's cost scale with something the USER controls. Three full scans per row, thirty-odd rows. Same fix, plus `rankExercises` was being run twice per render for no reason. Both now have a guard test with a frame budget rather than a benchmark, tight enough that the per-row scan cannot come back unnoticed. **The lesson worth keeping:** a product decision to move a number from 12 to 100 is a performance change, and nothing in 741 passing tests or in the running app was going to mention it — the seeded screen felt fine because five weeks of history is 180 sets, not five years of it.
- **R97 — two defects the hundred-goal cap exposed, both found by walking a full screen. 741 tests green.** **(a) The add sheet offered lifts it was going to refuse.** One goal per exercise is enforced at the write, but `goalLifts` never excluded the ones already taken — with 36 goals set, most chips in the sheet ended at "You already have a goal for this lift", discovered only after choosing a target, a rep count and a deadline, on the tap that was meant to commit. The DEFAULT selection was one of them. §4 says never ask a question it could answer; taken lifts are now out of both lists, and when nothing is left the sheet says so and points at the two things that would free a slot instead of rendering a form whose only outcome is a refusal. **(b) A card that said "Not trained yet · 130 days left · behind pace"** — in one sentence. Both halves were true under DIFFERENT definitions of trained: `trainedSince` counts any set on the lift, `current` counts only sets at the goal's rep count, and a lifter rowing 8s against a ×10 goal satisfies the first and not the second. The judgement then had nothing behind it, because `fraction` derives from `current` — "behind pace" was a reading of an absence. Pace is now judged on what the card can show, so the two lines cannot disagree; the case the rule was written for (qualified before the goal, stalled since) still reads behind pace, and still has a line beside it. Verified across all 31 live cards on the seeded screen: zero contradictions. **The seeder grew a `many-goals` mode** for this — 36 goals across every split day, five already met — because neither defect is reachable from the two goals a walk through the app produces, and neither was visible to 733 passing tests. **Next:** the filter resets to ALL on every visit. Also worth a look: with a hundred slots, setting a goal per lift is a hundred trips through the sheet — the cap is fillable in principle and punishing in practice.
- **R96 — a hundred goal slots, and a screen that can hold them. 733 tests green.** `MAX_GOALS` is 100 exactly — not 112, the old cap is gone rather than added to. A hundred cards is a different screen from twelve, so the cap bought a filter bar (`ui/goal-filters.ts`, 11 tests): ALL / PUSH / PULL / LEGS / DONE with live counts, and a sort that cycles CLOSEST → SOONEST → NEWEST. Three decisions worth keeping. **(a) DONE is a filter, not a sort** — a met goal is a trophy, not a target, and every other filter excludes them, so "PUSH" means "push goals I am still chasing". **(b) Ties break on the lift name**, because a hundred-item list that reshuffles under the finger is worse than one in a mediocre order. **(c) The counts come from the same function that filters**, so a chip can never promise a number the list does not deliver — and a zero chip declines the tap. **Two things the running app caught that the tests could not.** The chip row and the sort button overlapped: a flex item will not shrink below its own content width, so at 407px of chips in a 382px bar the sort control was drawn straight over the DONE chip — caret at x719, DONE's label at x764 — and ran 12px past the column. `minWidth: 0` on the scroller and `flexShrink: 0` on the button. And `+ ADD A GOAL` was the last row of the scroll: with 31 live goals that is 4,408px down, a control that exists and cannot be reached. It is pinned below the list now, with a rule above it so it does not read as one more card. **The cap tests had to be rewritten, and the reason is a real finding:** the library ships 28 movements and one goal per exercise is enforced, so the effective cap is the number of movements the user has — filling a hundred slots means inventing lifts. `capSlate()` does exactly that, and `seed-history.ts many-goals` plants 36 across every split day so the bar could be judged against a full screen rather than two cards. **Next:** the filter bar only appears above four goals, which is right, but nothing yet remembers the filter across a visit — come back to the screen and it is ALL again. Worth deciding whether that is a bug or the point.
- **R95 - the bottom really was overlapping, and the zoom was my fault. 717 tests green.** Four reports in one go. **(a) "super zoomed in"** - self-inflicted: I had forced a 390px emulated viewport for testing, so the pane scaled it up. Reset to native, and the real pane turned out to be 800x450 - wide and short, which is also the "not phone shaped, very square" complaint and why the column had been so tight all along. **(b) The rail moved** to sit directly under NEXT / SET n instead of above the footer: that header is the one place already answering "what now", while CLEAR and FINISH are where the eye goes to END a workout. **(c) The overlap was real and the screenshot showed it** - flush against the set list, which is a SCROLLER whose top row is routinely half-cut, the rail made "Chest Fly" look like two things drawn on top of each other. It has its own band now with a rule under it, and the first list row starts 9px clear. **(d) A bodyweight hero said "BW" with "LB" beside it**, which claims the set weighed nothing in pounds; it says BODYWEIGHT now, smaller, because it is a word rather than a two-letter unit. **The structural fix underneath all of it:** the column used to drop the day RAIL below 568 so CLEAR and FINISH could not be pushed off. That cost a feature to a constraint scrolling answers properly, so the column now scrolls when the fixed parts genuinely cannot fit - and §4's no-scroll rule is preserved exactly where it means something, since `scrolls` is false for every phone that ships. The threshold carries the model's measured 46px of conservatism rather than a guessed one.
- **R94 - two more things that did not fit, one of them the same bug one level down. 713 tests green.** Swept all four screens at 375x568 (clean) and at 281x460, which turned up two. **(a) The reps row overflowed sideways**: `repsRow` is `justifyContent: 'center'` with a fixed 14px gap, its children come to ~217px, and on a 281px pane that leaves 24px for four gaps - so it overflowed by 32 and centring split it both ways, putting the -5 button at x -6, half off the screen. Exactly the same shape as R92's column bug, one level down. The gap is responsive now and -5 sits at x10. **(b) CLEAR and FINISH fell off the bottom** once a set was logged - the workout could be started and never finished. Something has to give at that size, and the order is not a judgement call, so the RAIL yields first: losing it costs discoverability the picker still provides, losing FINISH costs the ability to complete a workout. Dropped by setting its height to zero so the fit math and the screen read the same number. **The interesting part was nearly getting that wrong.** Keyed on `fixedHeight`, the rule dropped the rail on an iPhone SE - the model puts 568 46px over. I measured the real screen before believing it: at 375x568 with the rail up, FINISH sits at y549-566, inside the screen. So the rule is keyed on the device instead - every shipping phone keeps the rail, and only something shorter than an SE loses it. A conservative estimate is the right direction for a floor and the wrong basis for taking a feature away.
- **R93 - the fit math was lying again, and the tests were asserting the lie. 712 tests green.** R92's overlap happened because `columnHeight` reported an exact fit at 275x595 for a column that overflowed, so I measured every block on the running app against its constant. `HEADER_TEXT` was **58 against a measured 79** - the lift name, the last-time line, the equipment line and the gaps between them - a 21px optimistic error at every screen size. That is the second constant in this file caught the same way; STEP_HINT was 12 against a real 40 until R81. Corrected, and noted in the source that measuring them against the app is a periodic job rather than a one-off, because they are duplicated from the stylesheet by design. **The honest constants moved the floor from 526 to 600, which makes an iPhone SE 8px short once the rail is budgeted - so I checked the real thing rather than trusting either number.** At 375x568 with a set logged and the rail up, LOG SET sits fully visible at y364-390 and the header does not touch the nav: TODAY gives up its space and R92's tight mode top-aligns the rest. The model is now CONSERVATIVE rather than optimistic, which is the safe direction, and it also budgets the rail before a set exists. **So six tests were asserting something that is no longer the truth** - `columnHeight(l) <= h` at every height - and I restated them rather than tuning a constant until they passed: every height either fits or degrades on purpose, TODAY is the only thing that gives, and the tap targets keep their size whatever happens. The design-size lock moved from 780 to 812, since 780 is now the boundary and every shipping iPhone since the X is 812 or taller.
- **R92 - "it doesnt fit to the screen", and this time it really did not. 711 tests green.** The report came twice and my first answer was the width caps; the second time I measured the actual pane instead of assuming, and found I had been verifying a screen the user does not have - every walk in this loop forced 375x812 while their pane was far smaller. At 281x460 the column comes to 401px in a 391px container, and `s.content` had `justifyContent: 'center'`, which SPLIT that 10px of overflow both ways: the exercise name landed at y34, above its own container's top at y39, drawn straight over the PROGRESS / GOALS links. Ten pixels of overflow, overlapping text at the top of the screen. **The centring was inert in the good case and harmful in the bad one** - `todayWrap` is `flex: 1` and eats every spare pixel, so there is never free space for `justifyContent` to distribute; it only ever decided which way overflow went. Now centred while there is room and top-aligned once there is not, keyed on `todayMin === 0`, which is the model's own signal that everything unshrinkable has already taken its space. **Unconditional `flex-start` was my first attempt and was wrong the other way**: it collapsed a 375x812 phone to the top with 340px of dead space below, which I only caught by measuring the normal case after fixing the broken one. Also worth recording: two intermediate measurements lied because Metro had not picked up the edit and because `useWindowDimensions` does not re-render on a mid-session resize - a hard reload at each size is the only trustworthy way to test a layout that depends on viewport. NEXT: the fit math still underestimates at narrow widths - the model puts the header at 58px and it renders 113 at 281px wide, because nothing in `columnHeight` knows about text wrapping.
- **R91 - the iOS bundle still builds, and the workspace is clean. 709 tests green.** Thirty rounds of changes and nobody had checked the app still bundles for the platform it actually ships on - `Platform` imports, `ScreenModal`, keep-awake and the share-url port are all native-facing, and a broken bundle would not have shown up in a single test or browser walk. `npm run bundle` exports cleanly: 1.76 MB, up from the 1.7 MB the handoff recorded, which is about 60 kB for everything this loop added and is the right order of magnitude for it. Cleared the artifacts I made along the way - `.export`, the scratch card renders, the seeded `public/seed.b64` - and confirmed the ones that stayed are real: `link/og.png` is deployed by build.cjs and referenced by the page's og:image, `app/out/e2e-recap.png` is what `npm run e2e` writes. Also confirmed the fitness-app directory is git-ignored by the parent repo, so nothing here can be accidentally committed to C:\Users\srobs. **NEXT, for whoever picks this up:** nothing is outstanding that a loop can settle - 709 tests green, all seven of BUILD_LOOP's journeys walked, the card robust to hostile content, the logging path 19x faster at five years of history, accessibility done, export/restore working, docs current. The two open items both need a person. **(1)** §5 wants a FILE to leave the app - a clip, or the card as an image - and the app emits only text plus a link; either needs a capture/encode dependency and a device to verify on, which is a §12 decision an unattended loop should not make alone. **(2)** §13's kill test is pre-registered, unrun, and needs ten real lifters; its material now builds correctly from `harness/`. If you want more loop rounds without deciding either, the cheapest untouched ground is the `link/` deployment surface - the AASA file, `_redirects` and `_headers` are templates nothing has exercised.
- **R90 - checked the kill test's materials still build, and found them branded APPNAME. 709 tests green.** §13's kill test is the project's central experiment and it is still unrun; its material comes from `harness/`, which nothing in this loop had executed. Both renderers work: `spike/render-frames.cjs` produces the card unchanged by any of R86-R87's fitting work, with the safe-area overlay confirming every element inside the guides and the action rail clear, and `harness/render-clip.cjs` produces the clip §5 describes - footage full-bleed, ONE number burned on it, the mark restrained. At 216x384 feed-thumbnail scale "225 x 5" is perfectly legible while the wordmark dissolves to a volt shape, which is exactly what §5's mark section says it measured and why the mark is a silhouette rather than text. **The defect was the brand.** The harness demo hardcoded `watermark: 'APPNAME'`, so running it as written hands ten lifters clips branded with a placeholder - and §5 is explicit that on a feed the mark IS the acquisition mechanism, so that undermines precisely what the test measures. Fixed there and in the card renderer's fallback. `clip.js` itself was already correct, reading the mark from data. NEXT: nothing outstanding that a loop can settle. The FILE gap needs a human decision (a capture or encode dependency, and a device); the kill test needs ten real lifters.
- **R89 - regression walk plus a handoff refresh. 709 tests green.** Walked the primary journey end to end on a cleared device after twenty-nine rounds of change - first launch, plan, day, first set, second lift, recap - measuring overflow and sideways scroll at every step. Clean at all six, and the recap correctly carries the SESSION ONE / "BENCH PRESS - THE ONE TO BEAT" claim R57 and R69 built. Brought HANDOFF.md current again (89 rounds, 709 tests) and added an R74-R88 section, because the second half of this loop changed things a fresh session would otherwise trip over: the card sweep and WHY canvas needs one, the memoised `allSets` and that it is frozen because callers sort what they are handed, Progress cutting by time rather than rank, accessibility existing at all, export/restore working on web, and `tools/seed-history.ts` - without which two of BUILD_LOOP's seven journeys cannot be reached.
- **R88 - the same hostile content against the app's screens. No defects.** Drove a 58-character exercise name, a six-digit typed weight, and a 51-character machine name ("Arsenal Strength Plate-Loaded Iso-Lateral Row, Bay 3") through Now, the equipment sheet and the recap. Nothing overflows, nothing escapes a container, the page never scrolls sideways, and the in-app recap renders a seven-figure volume - 7,999,992 - without the shrink-to-fit the CARD needed. **The contrast is the point and worth writing down:** the card broke on four separate values and the app broke on none, because canvas has no layout engine. Every string on the card is placed at an absolute coordinate, so anything that does not fit simply draws over its neighbour; the app has flexbox, `numberOfLines`, and a hero that already sizes itself from its character count - `layoutFor` was written for exactly this after six characters overflowed a 320px phone. Robustness there was designed in once and has held ever since; on the canvas it has to be re-earned for every value drawn, which is why R87's sweep is a sweep rather than three fixes.
- **R87 - swept every value on the card instead of fixing them one at a time. 709 tests green.** R86's long name was one instance of a class, so I pushed all of them: seven-figure volume, 999 sets, a four-figure PR, half-kilo decimals, a long goal line, a long title, and 120-to-300 character absurdities. Three more overflowed to the full 1080px width - the goal line I added in R69, the title, and a seven-figure volume. All three now measure and trim, and the volume hero shrinks its own font the way the app's hero already does, only ever downward so a normal card is untouched. **The reason this matters more than tidiness:** every string on that card arrives from a URL FRAGMENT, so none of it is known-good - the landing page renders whatever a link happens to carry, and "a user would never type that" is not a property of the input. Pinned as a sweep over ten cases rather than three separate tests, so the next value added to the card is caught by a test that already exists. NEXT: same question for the APP's screens - the card is now robust to hostile content and the four screens have only been checked against a 58-character exercise name.
- **R86 - a lift name the user typed could destroy the shared card. 699 tests green.** The app lets anyone invent an exercise name and nothing capped the length anywhere. In the APP that is fine - the header truncates and a 58-character name caused no overflow at 375px. On the CARD, which is the artifact that actually leaves, it was wrecked: "Single-Arm Cable Lateral Raise (Left Side, Slow Eccentric)" printed straight across the PR weight inside the volt slab, ran through the load column in the lift list, and reached 1028px on a canvas whose safe box ends at 996. Two overlapping strings and nothing readable, from a name people genuinely write down. The PR branch now goes through the painter, which is also how it picked up the trimming for free. The open item remains the FILE gap, which needs a human.

Profiled rather than guessed: `repo.allSets()` is 11.4ms at 9,360 sets and `state()` calls it FIVE times. Pinned as a CONTRACT, not a timing: a timing test on a shared laptop measures the laptop, so what is asserted is that repeated reads are identical and that logging, deleting and erasing each invalidate. The column header says exactly that, and the sparkline shows the real shape - a rise then a flat line - so the signal is on screen; but the NUMBER makes a plateau look like progress, and shortening the window would break the contract the header states. That is a product call, not a bug. PROOF https://example.app/r#...". Hand-rolled the base64url and UTF-8 rather than using TextEncoder/btoa: both are browser globals with no guarantee on Hermes, and btoa cannot take non-ASCII, which exercise names can be. **Overrode a prior rule and noting it**: two tests pinned /PROOF$/. PROOF"), with only the headline lift badged. So I went looking at the dependency list instead and found `expo-keep-awake` declared and never used - which means the phone locks during every rest period. §4's whole claim is that this is the fastest way to record a set, and that claim dies for every set after the first if you come back to a lock screen, unlock, and only then are you where you already were. Now held while a workout is live and released on FINISH or on leaving the screen. Gated on `canFinish` rather than on mount, because `useKeepAwake()` would hold it any time the app is open. **Only partly verifiable here**, and worth writing down: the preview pane renders with document.visibilityState = hidden, and the Wake Lock API refuses any request from a page that is not visible, so the lock can never be granted in this environment. What I could confirm is the shape - zero requests before the first set, exactly one after it, NotAllowedError swallowed by `feedback()` without disturbing the log, nothing still held after FINISH. Also noted: `@napi-rs/canvas`, `expo-asset`, `expo-font`, `@expo/vector-icons` and `expo-constants` are declared and unused by app code; check-deps.cjs only polices version drift, not usage. Verified in the app with nine lifts trained and twelve goals set: eight ranked rows, four carrying goal tags, the note reporting exactly one hidden, and that one confirmed to be the only trained lift without a goal. All six of them: the day chooser, the exercise picker, the equipment sheet, settings, the goal form and both confirmations. New `ScreenModal` unmounts on blur via `useFocusEffect` (already imported from expo-router, so nothing new added - §12) and remounts on focus, which is the behaviour the sheets wanted anyway since they all render conditionally rather than toggling `visible`. Starts focused=true on purpose: focus effects do not run until after the first commit, so starting false blanks every sheet for a frame on the way up. Each Progress row now carries its goal - "5 TO 50", or GOAL in volt once met. Measured against the goal's OWN rep count via `bestWeightAtReps`, not against the row's best-at-5+, because two screens disagreeing about how far away the same number is would be worse than not showing it. **Found a real bug while verifying: the Now screen's day chooser floats on top of Progress.** react-native-web renders a Modal through a portal attached to document.body, so it sits OUTSIDE the screen the navigator display:none's - open the chooser, tap PROGRESS, and it follows you, painting over the screen and still hit-testable (confirmed elementFromPoint returns PULL at y700, so you can change the Now screen's day from Progress). MACHINE is the one answer with a second half - the user had asked to record WHICH machine and have it offered again - so it records the kit immediately and STAYS up to ask; picking a known machine, or typing a new one and hitting return, closes it, and dismissing without naming one leaves a kit that is already a truthful answer on its own. **Driving it from automation:** react-native-web's `Pressable` listens for **pointer events**,
not synthetic clicks. A plain `click()` does nothing and looks exactly like a broken button —
dispatch `pointerdown` + `pointerup` + `click`.

Four screens (Now, Progress, Goals, Recap), the router, persistence, and the whole domain.

**⚠ Always `cd` to the project first.** `C:\Users\srobs` is a *different* Expo project with its
own `package.json` and `node_modules`. A drifted cwd in R18 silently patched its files and
bundled the wrong app.

**⚠ Never `npm install <pkg>` bare.** It resolves SDK 57 versions against expo 54, and caret
ranges drift silently. Look the version up first — `node -e "console.log(require('expo/bundledNativeModules.json')['expo-foo'])"`
— then `npm install --save-exact expo-foo@<that>`, then `npm run check-deps`. That script is
part of `npm test` now precisely because this keeps happening.

**The database opens from the App Group container** (§8b), so the Live Activity's App Intent can
reach it. Rules in `src/data/db-location.ts`, filesystem calls in `db.ts`. A build without the
entitlement in its code signing falls back to the app container and **says so** — that fallback
is otherwise indistinguishable from a working app.

- **R56 — the split, and a starting weight that knows who is lifting. 538 tests + tsc green.** **The app asks now instead of guessing.** Once per workout, before anything is logged: what split you run (first time only) and which day of it today is. It replaces the exercise sheet that auto-opened on a first launch — "what are you training" is a better first question than "pick one of twelve movements", and the answer narrows that list anyway. **Upper/lower and full body are derived, not modelled.** `split.ts` predicted this from the start — "upper = push + pull ... a routine builder is a different product" — and it held: `PLAN_DAY_COVERS` maps each plan-day onto the PPL days it contains, so two more splits cost a lookup table rather than the routine builder §5 has no room for. `splitPickerGroups` takes a plan-day and a day that covers two groups narrows to both. Verified live: on UPPER the sheet shows PUSH and PULL together with `OTHER DAYS · 2`; picking LEGS on PPL switches the screen to Squat. **The gate had a bug the first time.** It opened on `planDay === null`, but the app can INFER a day from whatever lift it is showing, so the question was never asked at all — the inference silently answered it. `dayChosen` is a separate field now: what they said, not what could be guessed. SKIP is deliberate and stays, because §4's rule is that the app does not ask what it can answer, and it can answer this badly-but-usefully by inference. **Starting weights went through three versions in one round, which is the honest way to record it.** A fixed per-movement guess (95 lb bench) was wrong for everyone in one direction. Zero — asked for, and implemented — was never a claim about the user but made the first set of every movement a chore, and logging `0 × 8` put a zero through volume. The version that stuck is both: `EQUIPMENT_BASE` floors every suggestion at the empty version of the thing (barbell 45/20, dumbbell 5/2.5, machine 5/2.5), and `startingWeight` scales above that from what they already lift. Every movement carries a `factor` relative to a bench, so any trained lift reads backwards into a bench-equivalent — a 405 squat implies a 338 bench — and one heavy lift calibrates the rest. Calibrated on the number the user gave: **0.43 × 315 = 135**, a 315 bench and a 135 first overhead press. Suggestions round to a loadable 5 lb / 2.5 kg and can never fall below an empty bar, both pinned across five strength levels and every movement. **Also in this batch:** `±5 · TYPE` is gone and the weight and reps numbers are themselves tappable to type; "Somewhere to start" became "First time", since it described a guessed starting weight the app no longer makes; NEXT LIFT returned to the footer but gated on the first set, which is when the question actually exists; the goal target steps in 5s not 10s; and the BY unit menu became an overlay after it was reported that opening it pushed SET GOAL down and made you scroll to reach what you had opened it to change. One more defect fell out of the erase test: `eraseAll` deletes the session row the Now model is holding, and it kept pointing at it — a stale weight on screen and a foreign-key failure on the next log. `startNextIfFinished` treats a session that is GONE the same as one that is finished. Two of my assertions were wrong before the code was, both the same mistake I have now made three times: assuming pounds from a fixture with no locale, where §8 correctly falls back to kg.
- **R55 — the goal sheet: a real deadline control, symmetric chips, and your own lifts as their own category. 533 tests + tsc green.** **BY is a number and a unit menu** instead of four fixed horizons. The deadline someone has in mind is "eight weeks" or "ninety days", and no row of presets holds both; `horizonDays(raw, unit)` converts, `HORIZON_UNITS` are days/weeks/months/years, and two years is the ceiling in whichever unit you say it — pinned at the boundary in all four. A month is a nominal 30 days and a year 365, which is what the old presets already used (3 MONTHS was 90), and the target date is advisory by definition so a calendar-exact month would be precision the field does not have. The sheet prints what the number **comes to** — `56 days — Oct 15, 2026` — because §16's rule is that a number the user cannot check is one they cannot trust, and nobody pictures 90 days without seeing the date. **The FOR chips were not the same size and now are.** They had vertical padding rather than a height, so "12 reps" and "OTHER" wrapped to two lines and made their whole row taller than the one above: a grid that stopped looking like a grid, exactly as reported. Fixed 46px height, labels cut to the bare number (the heading says FOR (REPS)), and measured live — nine chips, two rows, one unique height and one unique width across all of them. **A second lift category.** `pickerFor` already ranked correctly but presented a squat you do weekly and a movement you have never touched in one undifferentiated scroll. `goalLifts` splits them: YOUR LIFTS leads, OR ANYTHING ELSE follows, and a new user sees one row rather than an empty heading. That exposed a real defect in the split — routing through `pickerFor` inherited its cold-start branch, which returns §6's short twelve, so **a goal could not be set on two thirds of the library until the third session.** §6's short list is about a beginner's first LOGGING screen; a goal sheet has no business inheriting it. The whole library is offered, ranking preserved, with a test that the two categories together are exactly the library, nothing lost and nothing in both. TARGET also picked up the `-45 / +45` pair and the floated-unit centring from R54. One process note, the third this session: repairing a doc comment mid-edit briefly deleted `horizonDays` entirely and tsc caught it in one pass — the comment-block replacements in these scripted edits are the fragile part, not the code.
- **R54 — "sometimes it looks off centered", and it was: the hero. 527 tests + tsc green.** Measured rather than guessed, and the report was exactly right. Every element on the Now screen sat dead centre — lift name, "last time", the hint, the reps, LOG SET, all at offset 0 — except **the weight digits, at -17.8px**. `heroNumbers` held the number AND the unit, so the row centred the pair and left the number off. §15 makes the number the hero, and a hero that does not line up with its own screen is the one thing you cannot help noticing. **The first fix was wrong and the tests caught it.** Mirroring the unit with an invisible copy centred the digits and cost a fifth of the hero: `HERO_CHROME` had to reserve the unit twice, taking a three-digit weight on a 375px phone from **113px to 89px**. R40's sizing tests failed, which is precisely what they were written for. The unit is `position: absolute` instead, out of flow entirely, so `heroNumbers` measures the digits alone and centres them for nothing — `HERO_CHROME` still reserves its width once so there is clear space for it to hang in. Verified live: digits, hint and LOG SET all at 0. **The goal sheet was rebuilt as a grid.** `flexWrap` with content-sized chips broke rows wherever the text ran out — "1 reps" beside "12 reps" beside "OTHER", ragged, with different dead space per line. Fixed column widths line the rows up and fill the sheet: nine rep chips land as **5 + 4**, five horizons as **3 + 2**, both measured at exactly two rows. TARGET gained the same `-45 / +45` pair the logging screen has, because reaching 315 from a suggested 245 was seven taps of a stepper, and the ghost-unit centring trick applies there too. **`EDIT` became `TYPE`** and now sets the weight and reps directly rather than the jump amounts — tapping the hero has opened a weight field since R29, but reps had no typed entry at all, so 5 to 20 was fifteen taps. The jump amounts moved to a **SETTINGS sheet on Progress**. §9 bans a settings SCREEN and §5 caps the app at four, so this is a sheet over the screen that already holds export, restore and erase; the ban's intent is that settings becomes the drawer every unmade decision is swept into, and one sheet holding one preference is not that. **And the walk turned up a real defect that was sitting in the bug hunt's unverified pile.** Saving 45 in Settings left the buttons on Now still labelled 134: `useFocusEffect` only re-read when a finished session had rolled over, so anything the other screens changed was invisible until the next tap here — including a restore, or an erase, leaving this screen showing numbers for sets that no longer existed. It re-reads unconditionally now. Three tests pin it, including that an erase performed elsewhere leaves no phantom totals. One process note: the `-134` that exposed it was my own test contamination in the local database, the second time this session that a value I typed while verifying has been mistaken for a default — which is its own argument for the jump amounts living somewhere deliberate rather than one tap off the logging path.
- **R53 — seven requested changes: reset, custom jump amounts, a day-scoped picker, sixteen movements, and equipment. 524 tests + tsc green, schema at v3.** **Reset, as two controls rather than one**, because "reset" split two ways and one of them is irreversible: `CLEAR` on Now takes today's sets and nothing else, `ERASE EVERYTHING` on Progress takes the lot. The second sits directly under EXPORT MY DATA on purpose — §11 has no server copy, so the file that button makes is the only thing standing behind it. Both go through a shared `ConfirmSheet` whose two rules are load-bearing: the destructive button is never the one under your thumb by default (cancel is first and wider), and the body states what will actually go in counts rather than asking "are you sure". `eraseAll` is a HARD delete, unlike every other write in the app: leaving 1,680 rows marked `deleted = 1` and calling that erased would be a lie told for a sync feature that does not exist yet. The twelve built-ins are re-seeded so the next launch has something to log against. **The jump amounts are the user's**, set from the `±5 · EDIT` line — §9 bans a settings SCREEN, not preferences, and a preference set from the control it changes never needs one. Stored per unit via a new `meta`-backed `getPref`/`setPref`, so an lb choice cannot leak into a kg session, and a corrupt stored value falls back to the default rather than breaking the screen. **The picker opens on the day being trained** (`splitPickerGroups`), which is the change asked for by name: on pull day it shows three pull movements instead of eight across three days, with `OTHER DAYS · 5` one tap away. Movements the user invented are never hidden — they have no day, and burying them would be R32's trap one step out — and when the day is not yet knowable nothing is narrowed, because an arbitrary third of the library is worse than all of it. **Sixteen movements added**, chosen for how ordinary they are, and legs went from two to eight — it was the thin day, on the day people find hardest to fill. Bodyweight movements are deliberately absent: pull-ups and dips would log as `0 × 8` and put a zero through volume, PR detection and the shareable, which is a feature rather than a list entry. Adding them exposed a real defect underneath: `pickerFor` past three sessions returned only lifts with HISTORY, so a movement you had never tried was unreachable forever — the way to start doing leg curls was to have already done leg curls. The library is now a tail behind the ranked lifts, so discovery costs a scroll rather than a different screen. **Equipment lives on the SET**, not the exercise: "Lateral Raise" is dumbbells one week and the machine the next, and pinning it to the exercise would rewrite history every time someone switched. Both columns are nullable and nothing defaults to barbell — an unanswered set is unanswered. It carries over from the last set of that lift the way weight and reps do (§4: never ask a question you can answer), scoped per lift. There is deliberately **no machines table**: "save it for easy access" falls out of `SELECT DISTINCT machine FROM sets`, so the list is the history rather than a second home for the same fact that would drift the first time a set was deleted. Verified live end to end: `+ EQUIPMENT` → `DONE ON` → MACHINE → typed "Arsenal" → the header tag reads ARSENAL, and reopening offers Arsenal as a saved chip. Also pinned: the backup round-trips equipment, which `exportAll` gets for free by passing whole `LoggedSet` objects — but free is not the same as verified. Two of my own tests were wrong before the code was: one assumed pounds from a fixture with no locale (§8 falls back to kg), and one logged two machines on a fixed clock and then expected them ordered by time. `knownMachines` gained a name tiebreak so a genuine tie cannot shuffle the list under the user.
- **R52 — the jumps go both ways, UP NEXT removed, and the bottom of the screen turned to face forwards. 481 tests + tsc green.** Requested work, three parts, all on the Now screen. **The minus jumps.** `-45` and `-5` now sit opposite their plus twins, which cost nothing structurally because R51 had already reserved the slots: the empty balancing views that kept each row centred simply became buttons. `addPlate()`/`jumpReps()` are `bumpPlate(steps)`/`jumpReps(steps)` now, signed like the `bumpWeight`/`bumpReps` they sit beside, and both route through `setWeight`/`setReps` so they inherit the existing floors — stripping a plate off 20 lb lands on 0, dropping five reps from a triple lands on 1. The reason the minus needed to exist at all: undoing an over-tap of `+45` cost **nine** presses of the -5 stepper. **The rep jump is five, not ten, and that was asked as a question.** Rep schemes live in 1..`MAX_PR_REPS`, so a ten-rep jump leaves the usable range from almost anywhere inside it — from 3 it lands on 13, which §8 treats as conditioning rather than a strength set, and the app would refuse to score it. Five moves between the two schemes people actually alternate, 5s and 10s, in a single tap, and it is a clean multiple of the +/-1 stepper beside it. **UP NEXT is gone from the footer**, on the judgement of the person using it. It was spending the most valuable strip of the screen guessing at a lift the picker is one tap from the lift name and already orders by the day being trained. `NowModel.next()` and `state.upNext` are deliberately kept: §4 budgets "next exercise" as a SWIPE, and that is the call a swipe would make — they are an unimplemented gesture's API rather than dead code. Worth stating plainly: with the footer gone, changing lift costs two taps (name, then pick) instead of one, and the swipe §4 assumes has still never been built. **The bottom block leads with what is next.** It opened with `TODAY - 3 sets - 2,625 lb`, which is a receipt; mid-workout the question is not what you have done, it is what you are walking back to the bar for. The head reads `NEXT  SET n` now, counted off `loggedThisExercise` so it tracks the LIFT rather than the session — switch lifts and it restarts at 1, switch back and it resumes, remove a set and it walks back down, all three pinned. The record itself stays exactly where it was, because that is where R38's per-lift UNDO and R48's set removal live: the mistake is shown there, so the fix belongs there. Only the emphasis moved; the totals kept their place in the quiet style. Verified live at 375px: `-45 / +/-5 / +45` flanking the hint line, `-5 / - / 22 reps / + / +5` flanking the reps, round trips 200 -> 155 -> 200 and 22 -> 17 -> 22, `NEXT SET 4` leading the block, no horizontal overflow.
- **R51 — big-jump buttons, and the goal sheet's rows filled out. 473 tests + tsc green, bundles at 1.71 MB.** Requested work, four parts. **The jumps.** A `+45` beside the weight steppers and a `+5` beside the reps steppers, both drawn at 40px against the 56px weight stepper and the 48px reps stepper, as asked. §4 sets a 56px floor "for a sweaty thumb, one-handed" and 40 is under it — `hitSlop={14}` settles that: the *touchable* area is 68px, past the floor, while the drawn control stays visibly secondary to the one used every set. The plate is **unit-aware** (`PLATE = { lb: 45, kg: 20 }`) rather than a flat 45, for the reason `schema.ts` gives for never converting weights: 20 kg is the big plate on a metric bar, 45 is not a number a kg gym has, and 20.41 is worse than either because nobody loads it. Placement was forced by R40's lesson — `layoutFor` solves the hero's font size against `HERO_CHROME`, which budgets for exactly two steppers, so a third control in that row would have shrunk the number on every screen and §15 makes the number the hero. The plate jump lives on the `±5` hint line instead. The reps row got a fourth control and a matching empty slot on its left, so a centred row stays centred: measured, the reps number sits at cx 188 on a 375px screen, dead centre. Verified live: 465 → 510 → 555 and 5 → 10 → 15, zero horizontal overflow throughout. **The goal sheet.** FOR was five chips and looked half-empty; it is the eight rep schemes people actually train — 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12 — stopping at `MAX_PR_REPS` because a chip the form would then reject is the sheet arguing with itself. BY gained `1 YEAR`. Both rows end in **OTHER**, which reveals a numeric field: reps 1-12, and a horizon in **weeks** rather than a date, because a date needs a picker and §12 says not to add a dependency for what plain code does — and because a lifter plans in weeks, the same unit the streak counts in. The parsers live in `goals-model.ts` (`customReps`, `customHorizonDays`) so the presets and the typed value cannot disagree about what is legal, and the field holds TEXT rather than a number: a half-typed "1" on the way to "12" must not snap the form to a 1-rep goal. Verified live end to end — OTHER reps 7, OTHER 8 weeks, SET GOAL → a card reading **`Bench Press 135 × 7 · 56 days left`**. One test of mine failed first and was wrong, not the code: it assumed pounds from a fixture with no locale, where §8 correctly falls back to kg as the world majority.
- **R50 — an adversarial bug hunt, and the seven things it found that survived being attacked. 460 tests + tsc green, bundles at 1.71 MB.** Not a journey walk: five finders with different lenses over the whole codebase, 19 candidates, deduped to 9, then a skeptic per candidate whose only job was to refute it. All 9 survived, which is a suspicious enough ratio that **every one was then re-run by hand against a real `Repo` before being believed** — and that caught one whose repro did not fire as written (it used FEWER reps, which takes the direct-comparison branch, not the e1RM one). Four of the seven corrupted the shareable, which is the thing this product exists to make. **(1) `previousWeight: 0` is a sentinel and both renderers printed it as the gain.** §8 awards a PR on e1RM when no set at that rep count exists, leaving `previousWeight` at 0 — and `app/recap.tsx` and `spike/recap.js` both rendered `weight - prev`, so a 315 × 5 after a 300 × 3 history read **"SQUAT +315 LB"** for a 15 lb gain, and a 200 × 10 read "+200 LB". `shareText` already guarded with `prev > 0`, which is proof the field was known to be zero-able; the guard had simply never reached the other two readers. The payload carries `gain: number | null` now, computed once in `buildRecap` where the history is in hand, so a renderer cannot get it wrong again; the card shows `BEST YET` when there is nothing to compare against. The clip line also hardcoded `' LB'` while the volume above it used `D.unit`, so a kg session mixed units in one frame — fixed in the same place. **(2) "heaviest ever" was unconditional.** A 200 × 10 beating a 225 × 5 on e1RM went out as *"Bench Press 200 × 10 — heaviest ever"*, 25 lb lighter than their actual best; it could misfire in the direct branch too, claiming it for a 230 × 5 with a 275 × 3 on the books. New `heaviest` flag on the payload, from `heaviestEver()` — deliberately unfiltered by reps, because the claim is about the bar. It now says *best set yet* (pr.ts's own wording) when that is what it is. **(3) `weekStreak` bucketed on Thursday 00:00 UTC.** `Math.floor(at / WEEK_MS)`, and epoch day 0 was a Thursday — so the edge landed at Wednesday 5pm Pacific, 8pm Eastern, prime gym time. Two sets **two hours apart on one evening** returned a 2-week streak on a fresh install, and it reached the card AND the share message; the converse under-counted, turning three consecutive local Wednesdays into 2 because a fixed 7-day ruler is not a calendar. It is a LOCAL Monday-start calendar week now, matching §10's "instead of resetting every Monday" and the local dates the split already uses, with the day number taken from `Date.UTC` applied to local calendar fields so DST cannot move it. The old tests only ever used exact 7-day offsets, which is why none of them crossed a boundary. **(4) `restore` threw away every session's `startedAt`.** `startSession` had no timestamp parameter, so a 15 July / 45 MIN workout came back as **29 July / 1 MIN** while its own sets kept their true timestamps — the database disagreeing with itself. **(5) `restore` aborted with `UNIQUE constraint failed: sets.id`.** `allSets()` filters `deleted = 0`, so a set the user had undone was invisible to the collision check while its row still owned the primary key: undoing one set made that backup permanently un-restorable. New `knownSetIds`/`knownGoalIds` see every row in any state, which also stops a restore quietly resurrecting goals the user deleted. **(6) UP NEXT ping-ponged.** With nothing logged, `trained` is only the current lift, so the suggestion was its pair — and taking it made the lift you just left the pair again: bench, press, bench, press, two of twelve movements reachable. A `visited` set now excludes where you have been, kept deliberately OUT of `trained` because `trained` also decides `sessionDay` and merely LOOKING at a squat must not turn a push day into leg day. It walks the whole push day and then stops. **(7) Four bare `router.back()` calls.** A no-op when the screen IS the entry route — a web reload or any of the deep links `app.json` declares — and the console had been saying so for rounds: *"GO_BACK was not handled by any navigator"*, which I had written off as a dev warning during journey E. Measured: arriving on `/progress` and tapping DONE left the user with no route to the logging path at all. Guarded with `canGoBack()`, falling back to `/`; verified live, DONE now lands on Now in 218ms. **Not examined:** 10 further candidates fell below the verification cut, including a possible WAL drop in `db-location.ts` and Progress capping to 8 rows before dropping empty ones. Not refuted — just not looked at.
- **R49 — journey H: the card credited a first-ever set with a one-week streak, and a phantom 8x slowdown that was my own stopwatch. 437 tests + tsc green, bundles at 1.71 MB.** The last journey of the rotation, walked across all three edge states. **Empty database:** four clean screens and, checked explicitly this time, **not one element rendering as whitespace** anywhere — Now reads `Somewhere to start`, Progress `Log a few sessions and this fills in.`, Goals `Three at a time. Pick the lifts that matter.` The first-run picker is the largest it ever gets (the starting twelve, three headings) and shows nine of them with 199px below the cut — honest now only because R43 turned the indicator on; before that round this screen would have looked like a nine-movement library. **210 sessions / 1,680 sets:** Progress correctly capped at eight rows, hero at three digits with no overflow, nothing blank. **One set ever:** the thin recap composes properly under R47's spacer — list ends at 681, the *"Short one. It still counts"* line at 703, SHARE at 744 — and that is where the defect was. The stats row read **`SETS 1 · TIME 2 MIN · STREAK 1 WK`**. §6 makes `weekStreak` return 1 the moment anything is logged, and R36 had already refused to put that in the share message, in as many words: *"1 weeks running" after a first session would be the app lying on the user's behalf.* R36 fixed the message and left the card, so the surface that is meant to be checkable went on printing a week-long streak next to a single set. Same pattern as R44's duplicate check and R46's rounding — a rule stated once and applied to one of the two places it governs. There is a single `streakWorthShowing` threshold now, used by the card and the message, so they cannot drift apart again; the payload still carries the true number, because `spike/recap.js` and the harness read that field and it has to stay honest. **And a finding that turned out to be my own instrument, recorded because it nearly became a bug report.** Progress appeared to take **1,695ms** at 210 sessions against R40's 212ms, and it reproduced three times running. It was not real: `progressRows` measured 2-10ms in Node against the same 1,680 sets, and the giveaway was that the browser number **did not move with the workload** — ~1700ms on 210 sessions and ~1700ms on an empty database. A cost that ignores its input is measuring the stopwatch. `document.hidden` is true with the pane closed, and Chrome throttles timers in a backgrounded page: measured here, `setTimeout(60)` returned in **408ms** and `setTimeout(240)` in **992ms**, so a driver that sleeps between taps reports the clamp rather than the app. Remeasured on microtasks, which are not throttled: **log a set 14ms, open Progress 46-62ms** — faster than R40 recorded, no regression anywhere. That is the third instrument trap this rotation after `innerWidth` and ResizeObserver, and it is now in [BUILD_LOOP.md](BUILD_LOOP.md) with the polling helper.
- **R48 — journey G: a set logged wrong in the MIDDLE could not be removed, and it went out as a personal record. 432 tests + tsc green, bundles at 1.71 MB.** Everything the journey table names was already clean, and two earlier rounds held up under re-walking: a mis-tap is one visible UNDO and **FINISH withdraws itself** when the last set goes; a wrong weight undoes fine, and the staged number deliberately survives the undo, because removing a record is not a claim about *why*; abandoning mid-workout and reloading resumes identically — same lift, same hero, same reps, same TODAY, byte for byte apart from the rest clock ticking; and **R38's cross-lift undo still works after R42 changed the scrolling under it** — the bench set was undone from the Tricep Extension screen, the app stayed on Tricep Extension, and the totals followed. **The mistake the table does not name is the one with teeth.** `undo()` pops the *tail* of a lift, so the fat-fingered set in `55, 55, 255, 55` could only be reached by destroying the good set after it and re-logging. And the set chips were inert Views — measured: `cursor: auto`, no role, no tabindex — so there was nothing to tap. That is not tidiness. Driven live before the fix, one stray stepper produced a recap reading **`NEW PERSONAL RECORD · 255 × 12 · TRICEP EXTENSION +200 LB`** and a one-tap share of *"Tricep Extension 255 × 12 — heaviest ever, up from 55. 5,800 lb across 5 sets"* — a celebrated impossible PR, a volume inflated by 1,620 lb, and a message no one would survive sending. It poisons the lift permanently too: 255 becomes the best ever, so "Last time" is wrong from then on and a real PR can never beat it. Journey G asks whether a mistake can be undone *without thinking*, and in the case with the worst consequences the answer was no. Chips are removable now, and **it takes two taps**: `armSet` in the model lights the set on the first and removes it on the second, and tapping a different set moves the light rather than firing — a chip is small and sits beside four others, so a control that destroyed a real set on one stray tap would have traded one mistake for another. `removeSet` refuses anything outside the live session, because reaching back into history from the logging path is how you delete what you cannot see. §17's gate, answered: it adds **no** tap to the logging path (the chips were display-only), it serves shareable output directly since a fake PR is the worst output this product can produce, and nothing is removed to make room — the chips already occupied that space and merely did not respond. Verified live end to end: `1 | 175×5 · 2 | 215×5 · 3 | 175×5`, one tap turns the middle chip red with a `✕` and **changes nothing** — still 3 sets, 2,825 lb — and the second tap leaves `1 | 175×5 · 2 | 175×5` at 1,750 lb, exactly 215 × 5 lighter, with the recap carrying no PR and the share reading *"Bench Press 175 × 5. 30 lb from a 225 squat. 1,750 lb across 2 sets."* Ten tests, including one that pins the trap itself — that UNDO takes the good set and leaves the mistake — and one that walks four taps across three chips and asserts nothing was lost.
- **R47 — the recap had 323px of nothing in the middle of the screen the product is judged on. 423 tests + tsc green, bundles at 1.71 MB.** Out of journey rotation: a "great to look at" round, which [BUILD_LOOP.md](BUILD_LOOP.md) explicitly allows for *"a state that renders as an empty gap rather than as something"*. R45 measured it and left it; this is it. The cause was structural rather than cosmetic — the actions row is pinned to the bottom of the screen while the scroll content is top-aligned, so on a two-lift session **every pixel of slack collected in one place**: the lift list ended at y 421 and SHARE sat at y 744. It did not read as breathing room, it read as a page that had run out, on the one screen §5 says the whole product is judged by. A `flexGrow` spacer between the claim and the itemisation now takes it, with `flexGrow: 1` on the content container so there is free space to take at all. **It is deliberately not `justifyContent: 'center'`,** and the test says why: centering a scroll container whose content overflows pushes its top above the scroll origin, where no amount of scrolling reaches it — the header would be permanently cut off on a short phone. `flexGrow` distributes only POSITIVE free space, so a long session collapses the spacer to 0 and nothing moves. The composition it produces is a receipt: what the workout came to at the top — volume, stats, the PR slab, the goal — and the itemisation at the bottom, meeting the button that sends it, with a hairline above the list so it reads as the second block of something composed rather than as content that drifted. Verified live at three shapes and two screen sizes: **one lift** and **four lifts** on an 812px phone both close to a 24px gap with the summary at 12-277 and the list at 528-720; **five lifts** fills exactly (scrollHeight 744 = clientHeight 744) with the header still at y 12; and on a **568px screen** the content overflows by 42px, rests at `scrollTop` 0, scrolls to 42 and returns — the top reachable throughout, which is the case centering would have broken. Seven invariants in a new `recap-layout.test.ts`, four failing when the spacer and the flexGrow are put back; they also pin that the PR slab stays with the summary rather than being pushed below the gap, and that SHARE stays outside the scroll where it is predictable.
