- **R46 — journey F: the trend column rounded half a pound away, always in the app's favour. 416 tests + tsc green, bundles at 1.71 MB.** Walked by deriving the expected screen from the seeder's own rules first and then comparing, which is the only way to answer journey F's actual question — *is any number invented?* Everything else checked out exactly: all eight best sets match the seed to the pound (`Leg Press 240 × 10`, `Squat 195 × 5`, `Deadlift 225 × 5`, `Tricep Extension 55 × 12`, and so on), the ranking runs legs → pull → push which is the seeded routine in reverse recency, the sparklines are ten bars each with the last in volt and the flat run in the middle is the **deliberate weeks 5-8 plateau** showing up honestly rather than being smoothed away, R37's legend still lands exactly on the column it labels (351px, both), and nothing overflows a 375px screen. **One number did not survive.** `trendAcross` ended in `Math.round`, so a 12.5 lb gain printed as **+13**: the row read `Barbell Row · 115 × 8 · +13 lb`, and the arithmetic a user would do gives a starting weight of **102** — not a weight they ever lifted, and on 2.5 lb increments not one they could load. That is R37's own test for an invented number, failing on precision rather than on basis this time. It hit **four of the eight rows** — every lift the seeder progresses in 2.5 lb steps, which is to say every dumbbell and every kg plate set in real use — and `Math.round` breaks ties upward, so each one was overstating its gain by half a pound in the app's favour while a decline of the same size would have been reported as smaller. Weights are stored in the unit they were entered in and never converted (`schema.ts`), so the difference of two of them is exact; the round is 2dp now, purely to keep floating-point dust off the screen, and a whole-unit gain still prints `+45` with no stray `.0`. Verified live: the same four rows now read **+12.5 lb**, `115 − 12.5 = 102.5` reconciles to a real set, and the wider string still fits the column's 62px without touching the layout — right edges aligned at 351, no name clipped, no horizontal overflow. Six tests, four failing without the fix, including one that asserts the reconciliation directly and one that pins a decline being reported at full size.
- **R45 — journey E: the message that leaves the app named a lift the user had not trained, and none of the ones they had. 410 tests + tsc green, bundles at 1.71 MB.** §5 judges the whole product on this journey, so it was worth arriving at with instruments that work — and the first thing found was that one did not. **The seeder was writing every session's `started_at` as `now`.** `Repo.startSession` stamps its own clock, correctly for an app that only ever starts a session in the present, and `tools/seed-web.ts` handed it a single fixed clock — so a workout from twelve weeks ago claimed to have started today. Two of the recap's five tiles read straight off that row: the date said **TUE 18 AUG** for a session logged on the 15th, and `durationMs` came out `endedAt - startedAt`, negative, clamped to 0, so **every seeded workout was "1 MIN"** however long its sets were spread. The app was right and the instrument was lying, which is R37's exact failure moved from the sets to the sessions holding them; the clock is a variable now and the same recap reads **SAT 15 AUG · 22 MIN**. **Then the journey itself.** A push session of Bench Press 175 × 5 and Overhead Press 95 × 8, finished, recapped, shared in one tap — and the message was *"30 lb from a 225 squat. 4,905 lb across 6 sets. 13 weeks running. PROOF"*. The only lift it named was **squat**, which was not trained that day. Nothing the reader could react to was in it. Only `shareText`'s PR branch ever named the work, and §8 makes PRs deliberately rare — `MIN_SESSIONS_BEFORE_PR`, the never-cry-wolf rule — so this is not an edge case, it is nearly every session. §5 calls a volume summary Strava-shaped, "legible only to people who already lift", and this was worse than the thing being warned about: the receipt without even the lift list, sent into the group chat §5 names as the channel to design for. It opens with a lift and a number now, from `payload.lifts[0]` — session order, so the message and the card agree about what led the workout, rather than a "biggest lift" that would mean comparing a leg press against a bench. One lift, not all of them: §4 wants two seconds in a thread, and the aggregate sentence already covers the rest. The goal line keeps its place in the shareable, which §5 requires or the screen gets cut, but follows the work instead of leading it — a story about a lift you did not touch today cannot be the first thing read. Verified live, same session, same tap: *"Bench Press 175 × 5. 30 lb from a 225 squat. 4,905 lb across 6 sets. 13 weeks running. PROOF"*. Six tests, all failing without it, including that a PR still outranks the plain top set. Seen and not fixed: the recap's lift list ends at y 421 and SHARE/DONE sit at y 744, so a two-lift session shows **323px of empty middle** — the space is there for a longer session to grow into, and the screen is honest, but it reads as unfinished on exactly the workout most people do.
- **R44 — journey D: the trophy blocked the next goal, and then spoke for workouts it had nothing to do with. 404 tests + tsc green, bundles at 1.71 MB.** Both halves are the same sentence R39 already wrote — *"three at a time" means three things you are working TOWARD; a goal you have hit is a result, not a commitment* — applied to the two places it had not reached. R39 fixed the cap and stopped there. **(1) `duplicate` still counted trophies.** `validateNewGoal` guards the cap with `activeGoals` and then, on the very next line, checked `existing.some(...)` for a goal on the same lift. So: hit your 225 squat, go to set 275, and the app answers *"You already have a goal for this lift"* — with no way forward but deleting the thing you just earned. That is R39's own description of the bug it fixed, surviving one line below the fix. Hitting a target and immediately wanting the next one on that lift is the single most likely thing a user does here, and it was the one path closed. A **live** goal on the same lift still blocks a second, which is what keeps the screen and the narrative unambiguous. **(2) A finished goal led every recap forever.** `headlineGoal` sorts achieved first — deliberately, and rightly: finishing one is the best thing that happens on this screen and it should be what gets sent. But nothing bounded it in time. A goal met thirty days ago still won, so a **bench-only Tuesday went out carrying "Squat: 225 × 5. Done."** — not what happened that day, and it crowded out the live goal that was actually moving. It takes `since` now, the start of the session being recapped, and a goal already achieved before it does not headline at all. Not deprioritised: excluded. If an old trophy is the only goal there is, the honest line is no line, and §5 already prefers an absent goal line to an invented one. Walked end to end on twelve seeded weeks. Goals opened on `30 lb from a 225 squat · 60 days left · on pace`; typed 225 into the hero, logged it, and the recap came back **`NEW PERSONAL RECORD · 225 × 5 · SQUAT +30 LB · "Squat: 225 × 5. Done."`** — a goal finished *today* still leads, which was the half worth not breaking. Then the two fixes, live: **ADD A GOAL accepted a second squat goal at 240 × 5**, giving two cards on the lift — the live one leading with *"Train it and this fills in."* and 90 days left, the trophy kept below — where before it refused; and a bench-only session finished immediately after carried **no goal line at all**, falling to *"Short one. It still counts — the streak holds."* instead of a month-old squat result. Three tests fail with either half reverted. Noted and not done: the add-goal sheet suggests a target above the current best (240 after a 225), which is the right instinct, but nothing ties the suggestion to the goal just completed — a user who has hit 225 twice gets the same +15 either way. That is a copy-and-defaults judgement, not a defect.
- **R43 — journey C: the picker looked like the whole library and was missing a day of it. 396 tests + tsc green, bundles at 1.71 MB.** Walked on twelve seeded weeks. Most of journey C was already right, and two earlier rounds' fixes were visibly holding: tapping the lift name opens the sheet on `SWITCH TO · PUSH DAY` with the day being trained leading (R33) and the selected row near the top; `+ Something else` is pinned below the list where R35 put it, and it swaps to an **auto-focused** field, so inventing a movement is tap-type-tap with no stop in between; the movement is created, selected and still there after switching away to another day and back, which is R32's trap not biting. R41's line showed up in a journey it was not written for — `FACE PULL · Somewhere to start`, where a movement with no seed used to render a blank. **The defect was how much of the list you can see.** The sheet capped at `maxHeight: '72%'` — 585px, a 450px scrolling body — while the Goals sheet next door caps at 86%, a number R35 chose deliberately for exactly this problem and never came back to apply here. Grouped by split day the list carries four headings on top of the movements, so with the eight seeded lifts it was already 538px, and **adding one custom movement took it to 624px: 174px below the cut, the entire LEGS group at 0px visible**, with a 7px sliver of Deadlift as the only evidence the list continued. `showsVerticalScrollIndicator={false}` did the rest — a list cut off with no indicator does not read as "scroll me", it reads as the whole library, which is how Leg Press and Squat went missing from a picker whose only job is switching. Raised to 86% and the indicator turned on, alone in this screen. The cap is not claimed to be the fix on its own and the test says so: `pickerFor` returns up to twelve ranked movements **plus every one the user invented**, so this list can outgrow any percentage — the honest half is that it now admits it. Verified live: sheet 698px at exactly 86% of the viewport, body 563px, and all eight seeded lifts fully visible at 22px each including LEGS, with 61px still below the fold and a real scrollbar (`scrollbar-width: auto`, `::-webkit-scrollbar { display: block }`) saying so. The invariants live in `now-layout.test.ts`, which reads the source, and both fail when the two values are put back — the picker may not cap smaller than the sheet holding less, and the list may not hide its indicator. One thing checked and deliberately left: with push leading, the user's own movements sit last and are the 61px now below the cut. Leading with YOURS unconditionally would undo R33's reason for the ordering, and the list says it scrolls now; that is the right trade until someone with twenty custom lifts says otherwise.
- **R42 — journey B: TODAY marked the lift you were on and then stopped showing it. 392 tests + tsc green, bundles at 1.71 MB.** Walked on twelve seeded weeks, and journey B's actual promise holds everywhere it was asked: the app opens on **BENCH PRESS · Last time 175 × 5** with the hero prefilled to exactly that, which is the right lift — the seed's most recent session is legs, three days back, and push follows legs. Nothing is re-asked: no unit prompt, no routine question, no picker (it opens only on `firstEver`). Every switch carries its numbers with it — Overhead Press `Last time 95 × 8`, Tricep Extension `Last time 55 × 12`, each matching the seed exactly, each prefilled, each arrived at in one tap on UP NEXT. R41's line held too: `Last time 175 × 5` stayed put across all three sets rather than being displaced by today. **The defect was underneath all of it.** TODAY is a fixed box in a column that must not scroll (§4), so past two lifts its content outgrows it — 357px of content in a 218px viewport. It *can* scroll, but it never scrolled **itself**, and `showsVerticalScrollIndicator={false}` means nothing on screen says so. On the third lift of the seeded push day the block for the lift being trained — the volt dot that marks it current, its three logged sets, and R38's per-lift UNDO — measured **0px visible**, at y 765 against a scroller ending at 745, with `scrollTop` still 0. The second lift's block was cut by 20px, which is exactly where its UNDO sits. So R38's fix — "the mistake is shown here, so the undo belongs here" — was quietly unavailable for the common case, and a section whose stated job is that "what have I done so far" never requires leaving the screen had stopped doing it at three lifts. `revealOffset` in `now-model.ts` decides now, and it is a function rather than a `scrollToEnd()` for a reason: `buildToday` orders blocks by when each lift first appeared and only appends the current one if it has no sets, so **switching back to a lift trained earlier makes the block you need the first one** — scrollToEnd would scroll confidently away from it. It also returns null when the block is already fully visible, which is what keeps a fix on the logging hot path from becoming a twitch on every tap. **The plumbing had a bug the model could not have.** `onLayout` and `onContentSizeChange` are ResizeObserver-driven and land *after* the effect for the render that caused them, so reading the metrics only in a state effect computed against the previous render's content height — 238px of content against a cached 119, which is `max === 0`, which is "nothing to scroll", which is the original defect wearing a fix. The reveal now runs whenever either input changes, state or measurement; repeating it is free precisely because of the already-visible rule. **Verified as far as this session can.** With real geometry delivered to the handlers — viewport 218, content 238, blocks at y 0 and y 119, current index 1 — the rule returned **20**, and applying 20 took the current block from `99/119px visible, UNDO off screen` to `119/119, UNDO visible`. What could NOT be exercised: ResizeObserver never fires at all here, because **a hidden Browser pane pauses the frame loop** — a plain observer of my own on `document.body` also fired zero times in 400ms, and animated `scrollTo` does not advance either. That is the environment, not the app, and it is now written into [BUILD_LOOP.md](BUILD_LOOP.md) step 2 with the four-line check that tells you which one you are looking at, because layout-driven code under a hidden pane reads exactly like dead code with its handlers correctly attached.
- **R41 — the database moved into the App Group container, and journey A's first tap deleted the copy. 380 tests + tsc green, bundles at 1.71 MB.** Two things, the second found by walking the first's app. **(1) §8b's outstanding item is done.** An App Intent's `perform()` may run in the widget extension process, and a database opened with no directory lands in the app's own container where that process cannot reach it — so `openDatabaseSync` now takes the App Group container declared in `app.json`. Doing it now was the whole point: after launch it means migrating the only copy of a user's history (§11). The decidable half is `src/data/db-location.ts` — pure, 32 tests — because `db.ts` imports react-native and expo-sqlite and no test runner on a laptop can load it, the same reason `open-once.ts` exists. Three rules earned their tests. **The write-ahead log moves with the database**: `schema.ts` sets `journal_mode = WAL`, so moving only `proof.db` strands every commit still in the log — after a force-quit, the session the user just finished. **`proof.db` moves last**, so "the old file is gone" is a truthful completion marker and a crash halfway leaves the database findable at the old path for the next launch to finish; moving it first would leave a database at the destination whose log was still at the source, and the resume check would call that torso migrated. **A failed move opens the OLD directory, never the new one** — `openDatabaseSync` creates what it does not find, so opening the destination after a half-finished move manufactures an empty database beside a full one, which the next launch cannot distinguish from two real databases and correctly refuses to touch; one transient filesystem error would have stranded a user's history for good. A build whose code-signing entitlements lack the group (Expo Go, any build without the profile) falls back to the app container and **says so**, through `RepoGate`'s detail line and a `console.warn`, because a silent fallback is an app that works perfectly while its Lock Screen buttons do nothing. **(2) Journey A, re-walked on a cleared database.** First launch opens the picker on `START WITH · PUSH DAY` — measured on the modal layer at z-index 9999, sheet body 585px at y 227, not the invisible-sheet failure. Pick Bench Press, three taps of LOG SET, FINISH, recap: `2,280 LB · SETS 3 · TIME 1 MIN · STREAK 1 WK`, zero horizontal overflow at every step (`scrollWidth` 375 against `clientWidth` 375), nothing off screen, nothing covered. **The defect was the user's first tap.** Under `BENCH PRESS` sat *"Somewhere to start"*; logging the first set replaced it with `' '` — a literal single space, measured at 20px tall and 4px wide, directly beneath the app's own title. Their very first action deleted the only encouraging line on the screen, and journey A asks in as many words: *any blank?* The branch was `state.prefillSource === 'seed' ? 'Somewhere to start' : ' '`, and it had a second, worse mouth: a movement the user **invented** has no seed, so its source is `fallback` and the line was empty from the very first frame — they never saw copy there at all. Both are the same hole, that the line only knew how to describe a *previous session*. It is `lastTimeLine()` in `now-model.ts` now, not a ternary in the `.tsx`, because nothing in a component could have caught a branch that renders whitespace: an earlier session still wins (§4 asks for exactly that, and it is the number that decides what to load), otherwise the set just logged — *"Just did  95 × 8"*, which is what the hero is prefilled with anyway — otherwise "Somewhere to start", since a seed and a fallback are both the app admitting it chose the number. Verified live: `Somewhere to start` → `Just did  95 × 8` → held across all three sets, and a second session still reads `Last time  215 × 5` rather than being displaced by today. **Not looked at with human eyes** — the preview pane was not displayed this round, so every layout claim above is measured geometry, which is BUILD_LOOP's documented fallback and not its first choice.
- **R40 — journey H, and the hero never knew what it was drawing. 339 tests + tsc green.** The last journey. Both extremes are sound: an **empty database** gives four clean screens ("Log a few sessions and this fills in", "Three at a time. Pick the lifts that matter", "Nothing logged yet."); **one set ever** produces the honest thin recap, *"Short one. It still counts — the streak holds."*, and a Progress row reading `95 × 8 | —` because a single point has nothing to compare against; and **210 sessions / 1,680 sets** boots the Now screen in 251ms, logs a set in 55ms, opens the picker in 47ms and renders Progress in 212ms, correctly capped at eight rows with nothing overlapping. **The defect was the hero number.** `layoutFor` sized it from the viewport and never from the *number it had to draw*, and `typedWeight` allows six characters — so at `999999` the row was **135px wider than a 320px phone**: `scrollWidth` 455 against a `clientWidth` of 320, the page scrolling sideways, the + stepper off the screen. The fix solves for a font size that fits between the steppers, using constants **measured off the running app** rather than estimated — 0.5991 of font size per digit, minus the 3px of negative letter-spacing, checked against a real render ("95" at 113px measures 129px, and 2 × (0.5991 × 113 − 3) = 129.4). Floored, not rounded, because rounding a fit-driven size up puts it back over the edge it was computed to stay inside. **Measuring it properly showed the everyday case was wrong too**: a three-digit weight at the old 113px needed 382px on a 375px screen and had been overflowing by 7px for the entire project. Nothing caught it because every check compared against `innerWidth` — which the overflow itself inflates, so the question "is this off screen" could only ever answer no. That is the same shape of blind spot as the invisible sheets, in the measuring tool this time rather than in the app; [BUILD_LOOP.md](BUILD_LOOP.md) now says to compare `scrollWidth` against `clientWidth`, which cannot be fooled by the thing it is measuring. Verified live at 375 and at 320: `95`, `225`, `1000` and `999999` all render with **zero horizontal overflow** and a tappable + stepper, the hero scaling 112 → 109 → 83 → 57.
- **R39 — journey D: you had to delete a win to set a new target. 332 tests + tsc green.** Walked on seeded history, and most of it was already right: Goals reads `30 lb from a 225 squat · on pace` with both numbers checking out against the data; the recap **carries the goal line**, which is §5's actual obligation — goals must feed the output or the screen gets cut. Then the payoff moment, hitting 225 × 5 on a goal set thirty days earlier, and it lands properly: `NEW PERSONAL RECORD · SQUAT +30 LB · "Squat: 225 × 5. Done."`, sharing as *"Squat 225 × 5 — heaviest ever, up from 195. 1,125 lb across 1 set. 13 weeks running. PROOF"*. **The defect was what happens next.** §5 caps goals at three, and the cap counted **achieved** ones — so after three wins the app demanded the user delete a trophy before it would let them set a new target, punishing exactly the person the feature exists for. "Three at a time" means three things you are working *toward*; a goal you have hit is a result, not a commitment. New `isAchieved` / `activeGoals` in the domain, used by `canAddGoal`, `validateNewGoal` **and** the repo's hard cap, so the rule holds at every layer rather than only in the UI that happens to ask. Verified live: with the squat goal met, three new goals were added on top of it — four cards on screen, the trophy kept, ADD correctly withdrawing once three *active* goals exist. One thing noted and deliberately not done: when a goal is achieved the share text says "heaviest ever" and drops the fact that a target was met, because `shareText` treats PR and goal line as alternatives. Fixing it properly needs the payload to know both that the goal was achieved and that it was about the same lift as the PR, and mixing a bench PR with a squat goal reads as noise. It is a copy judgement, not a defect.
- **R38 — journey G: the mistake was on screen, the fix was not. 327 tests + tsc green.** Walked on seeded history, and the first two mistakes were already clean: a mis-tap is one visible UNDO and FINISH withdraws itself when the last set goes; abandoning mid-workout and coming back resumes **byte-identically** — same TODAY, same lift, same prefill. The third was not. **UNDO only ever worked on the lift you were currently training.** Log a set on bench, move on to overhead press, then notice the bench weight was wrong: the bad set sits there in TODAY, plainly visible, and the only way to remove it is to realise you must switch back to bench first — tap the name, find it in the picker, pick it, undo. Four taps and a realisation, to fix something the screen is already showing you. Journey G asks "can it be undone without thinking", and the honest answer was no. `undo()` takes an optional lift now and every block in TODAY carries its own UNDO, so the fix lives where the mistake is displayed. Verified live: two lifts logged, bench undone **from the overhead press screen**, still on overhead press afterwards, and Bench Press correctly reappearing as UP NEXT since it is push day and bench is untrained again. One process note, added to [BUILD_LOOP.md](BUILD_LOOP.md): `pointerdown` and `pointerup` dispatched in the same tick get swallowed, and the result is indistinguishable from a dead button — this round briefly "found" a broken UNDO that was only ever my own driving.
- **R37 — journey F, unblocked by a seeder, and the predictor was suggesting the wrong day's lift. 322 tests + tsc green.** Journey F could not be walked at all: it needs history spread over months and the app can only log *now*, so every date-dependent surface — the streak, the sparklines, §7's decay, "last time" — had only ever been judged on a single day's data, the one shape a real user never has. `web-db.ts` keeps the browser database as **base64 of a raw SQLite file**, and `node:sqlite` writes exactly that, so `tools/seed-web.ts` builds twelve weeks through the app's **own `Repo`** — same schema, same migrations, same queries — and drops it where the dev server already serves `sql-wasm.wasm` from. `npm run seed`, then one `fetch` in the console. The history deliberately **plateaus in weeks 5-8**: one that only ever rises makes every screen look good and tests nothing. Three findings. **(1) Progress printed a number nobody could check.** Beside "Squat 195 × 5" sat "+29", which was neither the weight gained (+35) nor a percentage — it was an **e1RM delta**, and `pr.ts` already forbids awarding on e1RM for precisely this reason: it disagrees with what a lifter would say. It is a like-for-like weight change now — same lift, same reps — and `null` rather than 0 when the ends are not comparable, because 200×5 to 200×8 is real progress that a weight delta reports as nothing and printing 0 would be a claim. **(2) The column had no stated basis.** "+25" alone says nothing about over what; the unit is printed and one right-aligned heading, `CHANGE, LAST 10 SESSIONS`, sits over that column and no other. My first attempt put a second heading on the left, above the lift *names*, labelling a column it was not over — caught by measuring that the legend's right edge lands on the trend column's (351px, both). **(3) The predictor was sending people to the wrong day.** With twelve weeks of a real push/pull/legs routine, UP NEXT after Bench Press was **Squat**. `predictSession` orders by typical position within a session, and on PPL *every* day's opener is position 0 — the ranking has no idea the days exist. Their history still ranks; the split now only rules out answers on the wrong day, and only when a same-day answer exists. Verified live: Bench Press → Overhead Press → Tricep Extension, the actual sequence in the data. Progress: every one of the eight lifts' best sets matches the seed exactly, no overlaps, nothing clipped.
- **R36 — journey E: what actually leaves the app. 316 tests + tsc green.** §5 judges the whole product on whether the output is worth sending, so this is the journey that matters most, and it had two faults. **(1) Tapping SHARE threw.** `Share.share` *rejects* when the platform cannot open a sheet — the project's own web preview rejects with "Share is not supported in this browser" — and it was wired straight into `onPress`, unhandled. So the one button this product exists to serve produced an **unhandled promise rejection**: a red stack trace over the recap in development, and in production a tap that silently does nothing. Same rule as `feedback()` on the Now screen — the presentation layer may not blow up — with one difference: a failed share is worth *saying*, because the user asked for it and is owed an answer, where a buzz that does not happen is not. It now fails to a quiet line under the button. The sweep test grew a third check: a platform call that can reject is never a bare `onPress`. **(2) The message did not contain the numbers.** It was `headline(recap) — watermark`, and `headline` is written to sit ON the card, *above* the numbers, so it omits them by design: "Heaviest 5-rep bench press". Alone in a share sheet that became **"Heaviest 5-rep bench press — PROOF"** — the single most postable fact in the entire session, **225**, was the one thing missing, and a reader learned nothing they could react to. New `shareText()` in the model composes a message that stands on its own: *"Bench Press 225 × 5 — heaviest ever, up from 195. 2,700 lb across 2 sets. 5 weeks running. PROOF"*. A one-week streak is deliberately never mentioned — §6 makes the streak read 1 the moment anything is logged, so "1 weeks running" after a first session would be the app lying on the user's behalf. Writing it exposed a third thing: `payload.pr.lift` was stored `.toUpperCase()`, a **styling decision baked into the data**, which was invisible while only the card read it and shouted the moment anything else did. The payload carries the real name now and the card uppercases at render. Verified live by shimming `navigator.share`: the app hands over `"3,135 lb across 3 sets. PROOF"`, no unhandled rejection. Two things checked and found CORRECT, not bugs: no PR was awarded on a second session (`MIN_SESSIONS_BEFORE_PR = 3`, the never-cry-wolf rule doing its job), and a workout left open four hours was auto-ended on the next launch.
- **R35 — journey C, and the same invisible-sheet bug in Goals. 307 tests + tsc green.** Started by hunting the *class* rather than the instance, and the Goals "add a goal" sheet had R34's bug verbatim — `animationType="slide"`, invisible on web since it was written. The pin is now a **sweep**: it reads every `.tsx` under `src/ui` and `app`, so the next one cannot hide in a file nobody thought to check. Fixing the animation exposed a second fault underneath it: that sheet had **no `maxHeight`**, unlike the Now picker's 72%, and it is bottom-anchored — so content taller than the viewport does not clip, it grows **upward off the top**. LIFT measured at y −885, TARGET at y −752, SET GOAL at y −60. What made it that tall was `chipRow`'s `flexWrap: 'wrap'` applied as the *style* of a **horizontal ScrollView**: the twelve lifts wrapped onto six lines instead of scrolling onto one. Row styling moved to `contentContainerStyle`, the sheet capped at 86% with a scrolling body and SET GOAL pinned outside it. Now 516px tall in an 812px window, every section hit-tested visible, twelve chips on one row scrolling 331px of 1393px. **Then the goal it created said "behind pace" — five seconds after being set.** `elapsed` was floored at a whole day, so a brand-new goal was judged one day old with zero progress: `0 >= 1/90` is false. That same floor made the `elapsed <= 0 -> null` branch beneath it unreachable, so the intent to stay quiet early had been written and had never once fired. Pace now makes **no claim until the lift has actually been trained since the goal was set** — waiting for training rather than for a grace period is what makes it a fact rather than a guess, because a weekly lifter is "behind" six days in seven on any linear reading of the calendar. **Journey C** proper turned up two more, both made worse by R33's split headings: "+ Something else" was the nineteenth row at y 1068, so adding a movement meant scrolling past every movement you were not looking for — it is pinned below the scroll now, the same shape as SET GOAL. And opening the picker while training a lift you invented put the **selected row at y 1098**, below the fold with nothing on screen marked: `YOURS` now leads when that is where you are, while the workout stays named by what was actually trained. Verified live end to end: custom movement created, trained, switched away from and found again, with the current lift at y 336 and the add row at y 756.
- **R34 — the exercise picker had never once been visible. 291 tests + tsc green.** Found while checking the split groups actually rendered. The sheet's fixed container computed to `top: 812` on an 812px window — **one full viewport below the screen**, `transform: matrix(1,0,0,1,0,812)`. Cause: on react-native-web `animationType="slide"` is a 0.3s keyframe with `animation-fill-mode: none`, so when it finishes the element **reverts to its start transform**, `translateY(100%)`. The picker slid up and then dropped straight back off the bottom. It had done that since it was built. `animationType="none"` fixes it; the sheet now sits at top 0 and every row hit-tests as tappable, with the overflow reachable by scrolling (14 of 19 rows visible, 506px of 818). **The reason thirty rounds of "verified live" missed it is the important part**: this loop drives the app with synthetic pointer events and reads `innerText`, and *both work perfectly on an element nobody can see*. Driving it is not looking at it. [BUILD_LOOP.md](BUILD_LOOP.md) step 2 now carries the geometry check — `getBoundingClientRect` for on-screen, `elementFromPoint` for covered — and says to run it over every row that matters, not one. Second fix, the last item off the open list: **FINISH was offered from launch**, and tapping it with nothing logged was a round trip to a recap reading "Nothing logged yet" plus an ended session containing no sets — a phantom row for every launch someone opened and did not train. `canFinish` now gates it, and `finish()` no-ops on an empty workout so the open session is reused instead. The streak was checked and is not affected: `weekStreak` counts sets, not sessions, so no number was ever invented. Verified live: FINISH absent on an empty screen, present after one set, gone again after UNDO.
- **R33 — FINISH → DONE fixed, and the app learned what goes with what. 287 tests + tsc green.** The recap is `router.push`ed on top of Now, so DONE is a `router.back()` and the screen underneath was never unmounted — the model came back still holding the session it had just ended. The user was left inside a finished workout (TODAY listing the sets they had just been congratulated on, a live rest clock, FINISH offered again) and **logging from there wrote into a closed session**, whose `endedAt` was by then earlier than sets inside it. `startNextIfFinished()` rolls onto a fresh workout; the screen calls it on focus so the slate is clean before anything is tapped, and `log()` calls it too so a write can never land in an ended session whatever the navigation did. Verified live: DONE now returns to an empty TODAY, no rest clock, opening on what was just trained. **Then splits** — asked for, and §17's gate is answered in the header of `src/domain/split.ts`: no tap is added, it serves first-run friction, and what it removes is the picker's reasonless flat ordering. Push/pull/legs, because it is the split people actually run and it partitions the starting twelve cleanly with every movement on exactly one day. The picker is now grouped with the day being trained leading and the sheet labelled `PUSH DAY`; the other days stay below, because a grouped list that hides them is a filter and a filter is a mode to get stuck in. It also closed a hole nobody had noticed: **UP NEXT was blank on a first-ever workout** — §7 ranks the history and removes what is already done, which for a beginner is the empty set, so the one person who did not know what to do next was the one person told nothing. The split fills in only there; once §7 can rank real history it wins, because someone who squats on push day is not wrong. One thing the walk corrected: ties were broken toward the lift trained FIRST, which had the app labelling the screen PUSH DAY and leading with push movements while the user sat looking at SQUAT. The lift you are **on** breaks ties now; a majority still beats it, so browsing to a curl mid-push-day cannot rename the workout.
- **R32 — the custom-exercise trap, and the screen fits any viewport. 252 tests + tsc green.** Two reports from use. **(1) A movement the user created could not be got back to.** `pickerFor` dropped it from *both* branches — before three sessions it returned the starting twelve verbatim, and after them it ranked by history, so a new lift was invisible until it had been trained, and it could not be trained because selecting it is what the list is for. Add "Hack Squat", switch away, gone. The only route back was retyping the exact name into "+ Something else" and relying on the duplicate check. Fixing it surfaced a **second defect in the same function**: names came from a STARTING_TWELVE-only map with `?? exerciseId` behind them, so once a custom lift *did* rank, the sheet showed the user `hack_squat`. `pickerFor` now takes the library — the order is what they have trained, ranked; then what they made but have not trained; then the generic twelve, which only appears while nothing can be ranked yet. Goals takes it too, so a goal can be set on a lift you invented. **(2) "When I preview it doesn't show it all."** True, and worse than cosmetic: the Now column spends ~660px of *fixed* height and never scrolls (§4 — a logging path you have to scroll to is not a one-tap logging path), so at 375×600 UP NEXT and FINISH rendered at y 590–630 and were simply unreachable. The vertical rhythm now scales with the height it actually has, via `layoutFor` in the model — so it is **tested**, which is the point: `columnHeight(layoutFor(w, h)) <= h` across every plausible viewport is an invariant no amount of reading the stylesheet gives you. Two floors are deliberate: LOG SET never drops below the 56px thumb target, and the hero is capped by height as well as width — sizing it off width alone is what ate the space. TODAY collapses fastest (s²) because it is the one part that scrolls. At 780px and up the numbers are **identical to what the screen was drawn with**, so no phone is affected. Two follow-ons found only by re-measuring: at 500px the set chips painted straight over the footer, because a flex child's implicit min-height is its content — `overflow: hidden` on the TODAY block; and at 1280px wide the layout did not break but *stretched*, steppers 1200px apart with the number marooned between them, so the column now letterboxes at 430px and a wide pane shows the app at the shape it ships in. Verified live at 375×500, 375×600, 375×812 and 1280×620: nothing clipped, nothing overlapping, and a custom lift created, re-found in the picker and logged.
- **R31 — the Now screen was overlapping itself. 236 tests + tsc green.** Reported from use, not from reading: things sitting on top of each other. Measured every text node's box in the running app and found **two collisions, both in the header, both invisible to all 232 tests.** (1) The PROGRESS/GOALS row was `position: absolute, top: 6` while the header below it started at the container's `paddingTop: 8` — *the same band*. The two were separated only by the exercise name happening to be short. "TRICEP EXTENSION" spans x 67–308 and PROGRESS spans 20–90: **the words printed through each other**, and SQUAT missed by 54px, which is why nobody caught it. The row is now in flow with the content in a column beneath it, so the header cannot reach it at any name length. (2) With that fixed, a custom movement — "Romanian Deadlift From A Deficit" — ran from **x −58 to x 433 on a 375px screen**, hanging off both edges. `numberOfLines={1}` was already set; it can only ellipsize against a *definite* width, and the header's `alignItems: center` sizes to content. The first fix, `maxWidth: '100%'` on the Text, **did not bind** — the Text's parent is a `Pressable`, itself shrink-to-fit, so the constraint had nothing to resolve against. `alignSelf: 'stretch'` had to go on the **Pressable**. Now bounded to 20–355 and truncating. A third reported overlap was **not** one and was left alone: the hero number's box clips the `±5` hint by 4px, but that is line-box gutter — measured against canvas metrics, the digits' ink ends at y 247 and the hint starts at 270, a 23px gap. Progress, Goals and Recap were swept the same way and are clean, so this was the Now screen only. Four tests, and they are the first in the project to read *source* rather than a model: layout has no model, and nothing behind one could have caught this. They cannot tell you the screen looks right — they fail the moment either decision is reverted, which is the whole job.
- **R30 — journey B (returning user, second session). 232 tests + tsc green.** Walked it and the very first screen was wrong: after one finished workout of squats, the app opened on **BENCH PRESS** at a seeded 95 lb, labelled *"Somewhere to start"* — while its own UP NEXT simultaneously pointed at **Squat**. The whole design rests on §4's "pre-filled with last time's numbers" and last time's numbers were a tap away instead of on the screen; a returning user was greeted by a movement they had never performed. **The cause was an asymmetry, not a missing feature.** `suggestNext` ranks the user's own lifts from the first session onward, but `openingExercise` went straight from `predictSession` — which deliberately returns nothing until **three** sessions exist, because it infers a *routine* — to the head of the starting twelve. Nothing occupied the rung between. So the swipe target knew what they lifted and the screen they landed on did not, for sessions two and three, which is exactly when a habit is or is not forming. New `openingLift()` in `predict.ts` fills it: predicted routine if there is one, otherwise **the first lift of their last session**. The first, not the last — you begin a workout where you began it last time, and the accessory you finished on is nobody's opener. That is the same reasoning `predictSession` already uses when it orders by typical position. Verified live end to end: fresh install → Squat ×2 → switch to Bench → FINISH → DONE → **reload now lands on SQUAT / "Last time 95 × 8" / 95 LB / 8 reps / UP NEXT Bench Press**, one tap from a logged set, and swiping to Bench prefills 95 × 8 from its own history. Ten tests; five *existing* tests also fail against the old opener, which is how little of that path was actually covered.
- **R29 — typed weight entry finished and pinned. 220 tests + tsc green.** Two rounds of user feedback landed here: the workout had "no progression in being able to record a whole workout" (fixed by the TODAY section, which shows every lift trained this session with running sets and volume), and 45 → 225 was **36 stepper taps**. Tapping the hero number now opens the one field on this screen. The first cut committed on **blur**, which was a stuck state, not a rough edge: type a number, tap LOG SET directly, and the *old* weight was logged — the two handlers race and nothing on screen says which won. **The commit rule is now every keystroke**, so there is no confirm step to lose the race with: what is on screen is what gets logged. The parsing moved out of `NowScreen.tsx` into `typedWeight()` in `now-model.ts`, because it *is* the feature and in the component nothing could reach it. That relocation immediately turned up a second defect the inline regex had: `"22..5"` displayed as `22..5` while `parseFloat` committed **22** — the number on screen and the number logged silently disagreed. A second decimal point is now dropped, and a test asserts the two can never differ. Third fix: a stepper pressed while the field is open now closes it. On web the tap blurs anyway, but on a phone the keyboard stays up and the field goes on showing the typed string while the weight steps underneath it. Blank or half-typed input leaves the working weight alone — zeroing someone's working weight mid-set is worse than not having the feature. Verified live at all three: typed 225 → tapped LOG SET **with the field still focused** → `225 × 8`, 1 set, 1,800 lb; typed 135 → `+` → 140 and the field closed; cleared the field → LOG SET → logged 140, not 0. Six tests, one of which fails against the previous parsing.
- **R28 — journey A (first ever launch), walked as a beginner. 214 tests + tsc green.** First round of [BUILD_LOOP.md](BUILD_LOOP.md), which replaces "read the code and reason" with "walk the app and fix what breaks" — the prompt exists because R27's three worst bugs were all found by using the thing, not by reading it. **Found a spec violation, not a rough edge:** §6 says *"first launch shows a short list of the most common movements — tap one and you are logging,"* and the app instead silently picked Bench Press with no visible sign the exercise name was tappable. A first-timer who came to squat was stuck. Now `firstEver` is on the model and the picker opens on a genuinely empty install. **It is not onboarding** — nothing to read, nothing to dismiss, it is simply the choice the app was otherwise making on the user's behalf. Verified live: first launch shows "START WITH" and the twelve; pick Squat, sheet closes, log 95 × 8; reload resumes on Squat with the set intact and **no picker**. Four tests pin that the choice is offered once and never to a returning user.
- **R27 — THE APP RUNS. Three real bugs found by using it. 210 tests + tsc green.** Got it executing in a browser via react-native-web, which unblocks every future round: the app can now be driven and verified on a laptop instead of waiting for a phone. Two obstacles first — expo-sqlite's web backend needs `SharedArrayBuffer` (cross-origin isolation, which would not stick through Metro's dev server and the preview proxy), and Metro cached a resolution failure from before a dependency existed. Solved with a **sql.js `Db` adapter**: ~90 lines, dev-only, and the real `Repo`, schema, migrations and queries all run through it unchanged. That is the two-method `Db` abstraction paying for itself. Opening is now async, which `RepoGate` absorbs — it already existed to handle open *failure*, so adding "not ready yet" was natural. Bugs, in ascending order of seriousness:
  - **A tap could cost you a set.** `log()` called `Haptics.impactAsync` *before* `model.log()`. §8b already states the rule for the Live Activity — "every write goes to the database first and the presentation second" — and haptics violated it: on any platform where the call throws or rejects, the write never happens. All six handlers reordered behind a `feedback()` helper that cannot throw.
  - **The exercise picker would not close.** On react-native-web a transparent `Modal` stays on screen after `visible` goes false, so choosing a lift switched the exercise and left the sheet covering the app. Both sheets now unmount instead of toggling — platform-independent, and it drops their internal state, so reopening never shows a half-typed exercise name or a cancelled goal draft.
  - **Progress displayed a set the user never performed.** It paired the best *weight* at ≥5 reps with the threshold rep count, rendering "105 × 5" for a set that was actually 105 × 8. Same class of dishonesty as claiming a PR they did not hit. `bestSetAtReps()` now returns the real stored set so the displayed pair is always something that happened.
  - **First launch behaved exactly as specified**, which is worth recording too: cold start on Bench Press at a seeded 95 × 8 labelled "Somewhere to start", plate-correct ±5 steppers, per-exercise set chips, a ticking rest timer, resume-on-relaunch landing on the last lift actually *logged* rather than merely selected, and a recap totalling 5,360 lb across 7 sets with **no PR claimed on day one**.
- **R26 — export/restore wired to a screen; 207 tests + tsc green, bundles at 1.7 MB.** Made the surface decision I had been deferring: **a single line at the bottom of Progress, not a settings screen.** §9 bans a settings screen and §11 requires an export — a settings screen would exist to hold one button, which is exactly how the clutter §5 is written to prevent gets in, and Progress is already the data screen. Native calls isolated in `ui/backup.ts`, everything decidable in `ui/backup-model.ts` (same split as `db`/`open-once` and `locale`/`inferUnit`). Backups are **dated, not timestamped**, so a second export the same day replaces the first instead of leaving near-identical files in the user's Files app, and they are written to *cache* so the OS can reclaim them once sent. Three findings:
  - **An audit script comparing every dep against `expo/bundledNativeModules.json` found react at 19.2.8 and react-native at 0.81.6** — caret ranges had drifted them off SDK 54, which wants 19.1.0 and 0.81.5. That is precisely the mismatch that fails on first boot for no visible reason. All pinned exact and the audit now reports clean.
  - **tsc caught a narrowing bug worth keeping:** `if (parsed.error)` cannot narrow a `string | null` discriminant, because an *empty* error message is falsy — a failure with a blank reason would have been read as success. Now `!== null`.
  - Pinning react-native down a patch left its internal tree at the old version; a clean reinstall still missed `@react-native/virtualized-lists`, which had to be installed explicitly. **npm does not reliably repair a transitive tree after a version pin — verify the tree, do not trust the install.**
- **R25 — audited for R24's bug class and found it twice more. 199 tests + tsc green, bundles.** Rather than assume the unit bug was a one-off, I grepped for the pattern that caused it — and `liveSession()?.unit ?? 'lb'` was also in `progress-model.ts` and the goal-creation sheet. Both are surfaces you open *between* workouts, so both fell through to pounds for every metric user: Progress labelled kilos as pounds, and the goal sheet suggested pound-shaped targets to a kg lifter. Fixed to `lastUsedUnit()`, and pinned with cross-site regression tests that build a kg-only history with **nothing live** — the exact condition the bug needed. **The generalisable lesson: `liveSession()` is the wrong source for anything a user has *chosen*, because the screens that ask are precisely the ones where no session is live.** Finding a bug is worth less than finding the shape of it.
- **R24 — fixed a silent bug that gave every metric user imperial sessions. 196 tests + tsc green, bundles.** Found by re-reading `NowModel`: `begin()` read `liveSession()?.unit ?? 'lb'`, and it is called *precisely when there is no live session*, so it always fell through to pounds. §8's "infer lb/kg from device locale" had never been wired up at all — a German user got lb sessions, lb-sized seed weights, and 5-unit steppers instead of 2.5. Now `inferUnit()` reads the region from a locale tag (US/LR/MM → lb, everything else → kg, **including the UK, whose gyms are plated in kilos even though the country weighs people in stone**), and `unitForNewSession()` makes **their own previous unit always win over the locale** — someone training in kilos on a US phone chose that, and switching it under them would corrupt every prefill and PR comparison. `repo.lastUsedUnit()` supplies the history side; `src/ui/locale.ts` is the only file touching a native module for it, so the inference stays testable and a locale lookup failure cannot take down the logging screen. **Also: `npm install <pkg>` keeps resolving SDK 57 versions against expo 54** — the fix is `require('expo/bundledNativeModules.json')`, which names the exact version the SDK wants (expo-localization → ~17.0.9, not ^57).
- **R23 — rest timer, 184 tests + tsc green, bundles.** Writing §8b created an inconsistency in the previous round: it specified that logging a set restarts a rest timer, and no such thing existed anywhere in the app or in §5. **Counts UP, never down** — a prescribed rest interval is a programming opinion and §5 already forbids imposing a programming model on someone running their own; a stopwatch answers the question a lifter actually has and needs no configuration. Past five minutes it changes colour and does nothing else: no alert, no sound, no nag. Measured across the session, not per exercise, because the rest that matters is since you last did work. **Design note worth keeping: the per-second tick deliberately does not call `model.state()`** — that re-queries sets, history, the picker and the prediction, so ticking through it would make the timer get slower the longer someone has used the app. The tick only invalidates the render and rest recomputes from the last set's timestamp, which is already in hand. `formatRest` handles the hour case because §8's 90-minute idle window means a phone left on a bench really does reach it, and "127:04" reads like a bug.
- **R22 — Live Activity specified (§8b), and it moved a decision that was about to become a migration.** §2 promoted this to *the* logging path four rounds ago and left it undefined. Researching it first surfaced the thing worth catching: **an interactive Live Activity button runs an App Intent's `perform()` in the widget extension process, a separate sandbox from the app.** A database opened with no explicit directory — which is exactly what `db.ts` does — lands in the app's own container where that process cannot reach it. So the SQLite file has to live in an **App Group container**, `app.json` now declares the group and the entitlement, and `db.ts` carries the unresolved work in a prominent comment. **The point is the timing: doing this before launch is free; doing it after means migrating the only copy of a user's training history that exists, with no server to restore from if the move half-fails.** Also spec'd: the ~8h+4h budget and the requirement that the activity end the moment §8's idle rule ends the session (a stale activity showing yesterday's bench press is worse than none); `timerInterval` for the rest countdown so iOS animates it locally instead of burning budget on per-second pushes; and database-first-activity-second ordering, because `areActivitiesEnabled` can be false silently and a dead activity must cost presentation, never a set. Noted honestly that `LiveActivityIntent` may run in-app and make the sandbox issue moot — **verify on a device, do not bet a data migration on a doc sentence.**
- **R21 — data export and restore (§11), 177 tests + tsc green.** `data/portable.ts`: plain readable JSON with self-describing keys, not a SQLite blob — a blob would be smaller, faster, and hostage-taking with extra steps, which defeats the trust signal the spec asks for. Three decisions the tests pin: **restore is additive and never deletes** (a "replace everything" mode is a data-loss button wearing a helpful label, and restoring onto a device used since the export must not throw away the sets in between); **nothing is ever silently dropped** — every unrestorable row is reported with a reason, because "imported successfully" over a file that lost half someone's history is worse than a clear failure; and **a file from a newer schema is refused rather than guessed at**, since this build would drop unknown columns on the next export and lose data on a round trip. Hitting the three-goal cap during restore is reported, not fatal. **Finding: my own test premise was wrong** — I asserted a missing `squat` would orphan its sets, but the starting twelve are seeded into every database, so only a *user-created* movement can actually go missing. The test now uses a custom exercise, which is the only case that can really happen.
- **R20 — the app survives a database failure instead of white-screening. 159 tests + tsc green, bundles.** `getRepo()` was called inside three component bodies and `Repo`'s constructor migrates, so a throw from `openDatabaseSync` or a migration happened *during render* — white screen, no message. On a local-first app with no server copy that is also the moment a user concludes their history is gone. Now `tryGetRepo()` returns failure as a **value**, a `RepoGate` in the root layout renders every route behind a successful open, and the error screen leads with *"your sets are still on this device — nothing has been deleted."* **It deliberately does not offer to delete and recreate the database** — the obvious "fix" destroys the only copy that exists (§11); recovery is a support conversation, not a button. Also added `+not-found` (reachable in exactly one real way: an old build opening a newer share link) and re-exported expo-router's `ErrorBoundary`. The open-once-and-remember-**failure** logic went into `open-once.ts` so it could be tested at all — `db.ts` imports a native module no test runner can load — and the tests pin the reason it caches failure: 50 `get()` calls must invoke a throwing opener once, not fifty, or a locked database file spins the UI thread.
- **R19 — add a custom exercise; core loop complete. 152 tests + tsc green, bundles at 1.67 MB.** `addCustomExercise()` slugifies, registers via `repo.addExercise()` *before* anything can be logged (the FK makes ordering mandatory), then switches to it. **Finding: slugification is lossy and the upsert made that dangerous.** "Hack-Squat" and "Hack Squat" both reduce to `hack_squat`, and `addExercise`'s `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET name` would have silently *renamed* the first — quietly merging two different movements' history into one. `freeSlug()` suffixes instead. I caught it because I wrote a doc comment claiming collision handling that the code did not do; the comment was the bug report. Exact-name matches are reused case-insensitively so nobody ends up with two Bench Presses. The text field is the only keyboard in the app, behind a tap on the least-used control of the least-used sheet.
- **R18 — THE APP COMPILES. 1.66 MB iOS bundle, 145 tests + tsc still green.** `expo export --no-bytecode` runs the real Metro bundler with no device, so "needs hardware" was wrong again. Verified by grepping the output bundle for a distinctive string from every screen and the domain — all ten present, so nothing was tree-shaken or stubbed. Four real problems, in order:
  - **My working directory had silently drifted to `C:\Users\srobs`.** The first `expo export`, and worse the first `npm install`, ran from the home directory — so I patched *its* `package.json` and dropped a `babel.config.js`/`metro.config.js` there, and bundled a project that was not this one. All reverted; that `package.json` is pre-existing and belongs to another project (expo-secure-store, zustand). **Lesson: every shell command in this project must `cd` explicitly or use absolute paths — relative-path file edits in a heredoc are silently destructive when the cwd is wrong.**
  - `main` was unset, so Expo fell back to the legacy `expo/AppEntry.js` and demanded an `App.tsx`. expo-router needs `"main": "expo-router/entry"`.
  - **`"type": "module"` had to go.** Metro, babel and the Expo config loader are all CommonJS; with it set, Node refuses to load `metro.config.js` as ESM on Windows. Node still runs the `.ts` sources and tests fine — it detects ESM syntax and reparses, costing a warning and nothing else.
  - The module tree was malformed by the drifted install — expo's and react-native's own deps sat in the parent tree while `expo` sat locally, and npm kept installing SDK **57** internals against expo 54. Whack-a-mole failed; `rm -rf node_modules package-lock.json && npm install` fixed it in one pass.
  - `metro.config.js` now pins `projectRoot`, `watchFolders` and `nodeModulesPaths` to this package and sets `disableHierarchicalLookup` — **not** cosmetic hardening: the parent directory is a different Expo project, and without this Metro will silently bundle its modules.
- **R17 — Goals screen + navigation, 145 tests + tsc green.** `ui/goals-model.ts` adds only what the screen needs on top of the already-tested domain: id minting, the repo round-trip, and turning a `GoalError` into a sentence that says what to do about it. The card shows `narrativeLine()` — *the same string that lands on the recap* — so what a user sees here and what they end up sending are visibly one sentence. `suggestTarget()` extends §4's "an empty number field is a bug" to goal creation, with a test asserting **the default the UI offers is never one the rules reject** (the obvious way to ship a form that argues with itself). **Also fixed: Progress and Goals existed but were unreachable** — nothing navigated to them. Two muted words at the top of Now, deliberately far from the hero number; the comment records that a third item makes it a tab bar and breaks §15.
- **R16 — exercise picker, 134 tests + tsc green.** A bottom sheet on the Now screen, opened by tapping the lift name — deliberately not styled as a button, because §7 makes selection a prediction problem and the common case is never touching it. **Finding: the picker did not contain its own selection.** `pickerFor()` ranks by history, so any lift chosen out of the starting twelve *after* history exists was absent from the list, and the sheet would open with nothing marked as selected. Caught by writing the invariant as a test before trusting the UI. `NowModel.state()` now guarantees the current exercise is always in its own picker.
- **R15 — Progress screen (§5 screen 2), 133 tests + tsc green.** `ui/progress-model.ts` reuses `rankExercises` — the *same* decayed score the logging path uses — deliberately: a Progress screen ordered differently from the exercise picker would give a lifter two different answers to "what am I training right now". Capped at 8 rows, so §8's mature clause holds and old lifts fall off the screen rather than into a scroll. Sparklines are **normalised within their own window**, because an absolute scale flattens a 200 lb bench into a straight line next to a 500 lb deadlift; a flat history draws a flat 0.5 line instead of dividing by zero. Drawn with plain Views — ten normalised bars need no charting dependency, which would otherwise be the largest thing in the bundle for the least-used screen. **Finding: the `sets → exercises` foreign key is enforced**, and my test hit it immediately with unregistered ids. That is the constraint working (it stops a typo'd id becoming a phantom lift), but it means **the not-yet-built "add a custom exercise" path must call `addExercise` before its first `logSet`** or the write fails.
- **R14 — recap wired end to end, 123 tests + tsc green.** `ui/recap-model.ts` is the one place that knows how to pull arrays out of the database and hand them to the pure domain functions, so payload logic stays testable with literals and this stays testable with a real database — neither has to fake the other. `app/recap.tsx` renders the real payload (a static preview; the video needs a device). Three behaviours worth keeping: a **`thin`** flag marks a first-ever single set as worth *showing* but not worth pushing someone to send; `headline()` ranks what actually travels — a PR beats a finished goal beats raw volume; and today's sets still cannot beat themselves, so two improving sets in one session produce one PR measured against history, not against each other.
- **R13 — Expo deps installed, whole project type-checks, 113 tests + tsc green.** Turns out "needs hardware" was too pessimistic: Metro needs a device but **tsc does not**, and type-checking the React code written blind found two real bugs in the expo-sqlite adapter that no test could have caught, because nothing here can import the real module at runtime. (a) `executeSync(params?)` was declared optional, making my interface *wider* than expo-sqlite's real signature, so `SQLiteDatabase` failed to satisfy it. (b) The `Db`/`Stmt` interface bound `unknown[]`, which type-checked happily against the node:sqlite test double and is simply not assignable to a SQLite bind value — now a narrow `BindValue = string | number | null | Uint8Array`, which is all the repository ever binds anyway. **Install finding:** `npx expo install` fails on SDK 54 with an ERESOLVE between `react-dom@19.2.8` and `react@19.1.0`; pinning `react-dom@19.1.0` explicitly resolves it. `npm test` now runs build + tests + tsc, so the RN code can never silently rot again.
- **R12 — goals persistence, 113 tests green.** `goals` table added as migration **index 1**, not folded into the base schema — index 0 is already the shape a shipped database would have run, and editing it would mean existing installs silently never get the table. A test stands up a real v1 database (rows and all), constructs `Repo` against it, and asserts the training survives while the new table works. `created_at` is stored because it is load-bearing, not bookkeeping: progress is measured from what the user could lift *when they set the goal*, so losing that column turns every bar into a lie. **The three-goal cap is enforced at the write as well as in the domain** — a UI bug that let a fourth through would otherwise persist it and §5's "hard cap" would quietly stop being true — while updates to an existing goal are exempt so editing your third goal doesn't hit the ceiling. End-to-end test: a stored goal produces "30 lb from a 315 squat" on the recap payload.
- **R11 — Goals (§5 screen 3), 105 tests green.** The screen v7 threatened to cut unless it fed the output, so the primary export is `narrativeLine()` — "30 lb from a 315 squat" — not the progress bar, and `buildRecap()` now carries a `goalLine` field so the obligation is asserted by a test rather than promised in prose. **Finding: a progress bar measured from zero lies on day one.** Someone with a 300 lb squat would show as 95% of the way to 315 before training once, so progress is measured from the baseline *when the goal was set*. Guard rails reject a goal already beaten (the bar would start full), duplicates per exercise, rep counts above 12, and dates in the past. `narrativeLine()` returns null rather than inventing a line when a goal has had no movement — an untouched goal says nothing. Added goals to the browser bundle (29 exports).
- **R10 — Expo shell, 86 tests still green.** `app.json` (PROOF, dark, Live Activities + associated domains + the `/r` intent filter already matching link/), `src/data/db.ts` opening the database once as a module singleton rather than a context — `Repo`'s constructor migrates, and running migrations twice because two providers mounted is a bug that only appears on someone else's phone. expo-router root has no tab bar and no headers; `index` *is* the Now screen, so a cold launch cannot land anywhere else (§4), with Progress and Recap pushed on top. **Finding: sed-transforming one file into a sibling produces plausible-looking nonsense** — the generated Progress stub kept a stray clause about video export from the Recap stub it was derived from. Caught it by reading the output; rewrote it directly. Generating code by find-and-replace across files is not a shortcut, it is a way to ship comments that lie.
- **R9 — expo-sqlite adapter (§12), 86 tests green.** `data/expo-db.ts` maps expo-sqlite onto the same two-method `Db` interface `repo.ts` already takes, so identical repository code runs on `node:sqlite` in tests and on device. It cannot be tested against real expo-sqlite on a laptop, but its *contract* can: the test fakes expo-sqlite's shape over `node:sqlite` and runs the real `Repo` through it, catching misnamed methods, dropped parameters and unwrapped results. **Decision worth keeping: statements are prepared per call and finalised in a `finally`, not cached.** expo-sqlite leaks a native handle for every statement left unfinalised and the logging path prepares one per set; caching would be faster and would mean owning a lifecycle across unmounts and hot reloads, while at a few dozen rows per workout the prepare cost is invisible and the leak is not. Two tests pin it — 50 sets leak zero handles, and a throwing statement still finalises.
- **R8 — the Now screen (§5), 83 tests green.** `ui/now-model.ts` is a pure state machine holding every rule with teeth; `ui/NowScreen.tsx` is a thin binding that only renders and forwards taps, so behaviour changes land in a file CI can actually run. Tests assert the §4 tap budget directly: repeat-last-set is one action, change-weight-and-log is three, a whole session of four sets across two lifts is six. **Finding: `upNext` was returning the exercise you are already on**, so the swipe target read empty until you had logged something — "next" has to exclude the current lift, not just the completed ones. Also asserted: steppers do NOT reset after logging (the next set is usually identical, and clearing them costs a tap), and relaunching mid-workout resumes while a session abandoned days ago is closed and backdated instead of resumed.
- **R7 — persistence (§12), 67 tests green.** `data/schema.ts` + `data/repo.ts` on `node:sqlite` (ships in Node 24, no native build). Repo takes a minimal `Db` interface and imports no driver, so the same code runs on expo-sqlite via an adapter. Three decisions worth keeping: weight is stored **in the unit it was entered in** (normalising 102.5 kg through pounds loses the user's actual plate loadout to float error, and numbers that drift destroy trust); every table carries `updated_at` + a soft `deleted` tombstone from day one because retrofitting those onto a shipped local DB for §11 CloudKit sync is a migration nobody survives; `historyBefore()` excludes the current session so a set cannot beat itself. **Finding: strip-only mode rejects TypeScript parameter properties** (`constructor(private db: Db)`) — they need a real transform, not erasure. Explicit field declarations throughout.
- **R6 — spec sync.** Folded R1–R5 findings into PROMPT.md §8/§12: badging-is-not-detection, streak-counts-weeks-with-current-week-grace, prefills-declare-their-source, and a table of the built domain modules telling a builder to wire the UI to them rather than rewrite. `npm test` now builds the bundle then runs everything.
- **R5 — domain wired into the harness, 56 tests green.** `build-domain.cjs` emits a browser bundle using Node's own `module.stripTypeScriptTypes` — no compiler, no bundler, no dependency. **Finding: flattening ES modules into one scope is wrong.** Two modules both declared a private `DAY_MS` and the bundle died on redeclaration; module-private names are meant to be private, so each module now gets its own IIFE with imports resolved from a shared registry, and a test asserts privates don't leak. Added `bundle-parity.test.ts` comparing bundle vs source output byte-for-byte, because the harness renders what ten real lifters will see: if it diverged from the app, the kill test would silently measure the wrong artifact. Harness now has "Derive from raw sets" — PR flags, volume and streak come from the product's logic instead of whatever the operator typed.
- **R4 — cold start (§6), 49 tests green.** `coldstart.ts`: the starting twelve with conservative population seeds, `prefillFor()` guaranteeing §4's "an empty number field is a bug" across every lift and both units, and a picker that shows generic lifts until there is history and their own lifts after. `prefillFor` returns a `source` (`history` | `seed` | `fallback`) so the UI can say "last time" truthfully and never let a guess pose as the user's own data. End-to-end test: a first-ever single set produces a complete recap that claims no PR.
- **R3 — session lifecycle + recap assembly, 39 tests green, end-to-end render proven.** `session.ts`: 90-min idle auto-end backdated to the last set, week-based streak with current-week grace, and `buildRecap()` emitting exactly the payload `spike/recap.js` consumes. `tools/render-recap.ts` runs simulated training → domain → payload → real PNG. **Finding: detection can be correct while presentation cries wolf.** The e2e run badged 4 of 5 lifts as PRs — each genuinely true (12 weeks at fixed weight, then a bump), but four volt rows flattens the hierarchy and the badge stops meaning anything. Now only the headline PR is badged; the rest stay in the data and in Progress. Unit tests could not have caught this — it only showed up in the rendered image.
- **R2 — exercise predictor (§7), 25 tests green.** `predict.ts` scores `Σ 0.5^(daysAgo/28)` per past occurrence, so frequency emerges from summing and recency from decay. §8's year-two decay requirement fell out structurally rather than needing a special case — 200 sessions of an abandoned programme do not resurface. Selection is by score but ORDERING is by typical position in a session, because opening on the accessory they always do last is technically right and useless.
- **R1 — PR detection (§8), 16 tests green.** `app/src/domain/pr.ts` + tests, pure TS on Node 24 native type-stripping, zero deps. Two findings. (a) e1RM must NOT gate awards — with a prior 275×2 on the books it rejects 230×5, which every lifter calls a 5-rep PR; it now only ranks within a session, and the award rule is "more weight than ever, for the same or more reps." - R301 — proved field-scan.cjs can actually fail before trusting it further, per a sibling's finding tonight (castle-bashers' own dead-field gate missed `+=`/`++` writes). Calibrated by hand: added a real canary field to `ProgressRow`, confirmed the scan flagged it (exit 1), then gave it ONLY a compound-assignment touch (`row._calibrationCanary += 1`, no read anywhere) and reran — it passed clean (exit 0). Confirmed blind spot, and it's the mirror image of castle-bashers': `\.field\b` matches a write exactly as readily as a read, so a field set but never read back was invisible to this gate the whole time it's existed. Fixed by inspecting every `.field` occurrence rather than just testing existence: a trailing assignment operator (`=`, `+=`, `++`, etc., with `==`/`===` deliberately let through since those compare) marks that one occurrence as a write, and the field only counts as used if at least one occurrence is NOT a write. - R333 — the sibling vein: unusual CIRCUMSTANCE rather than unusual user. First profile — the app killed mid-workout, a session left open with real sets logged and never explicitly finished — found the strongest bug of this second sweep. Seeded a session two sets in, abandoned past the 90-minute idle threshold (`IDLE_END_MS`), never ended. On load it correctly auto-closed (`isStale`/`autoEnd`, already wired in now-model.ts) and the recap read correctly — real duration, real "SESSION ONE" copy. Then tapped **"EDIT THIS WORKOUT"**, the feature R313 built specifically for "the set you typed wrong, noticed after FINISH" — and the reopened session closed itself again on the very next read, silently, landing back on a fresh SET 1 as if nothing had happened. Root cause: `reopenSession` only clears `ended_at`; `isStale`/`autoEnd` measured idleness purely from the last SET's timestamp, which a reopened-but-old session still has from hours or days ago, so the idle rule re-fired immediately — the older the workout being corrected, which is the entire point of reopening, the more certain the reopen was to silently fail. Fixed by giving `Session` a real `updatedAt` field (already stored in the DB, never surfaced to the domain layer) and measuring idleness from `max(lastSetAt, updatedAt)` instead of `lastSetAt` alone — a fresh reopen buys a genuine new 90-minute grace period, matching what a live session gets, while `autoEnd`'s own backdating still anchors to the real last SET so a reopened-then-abandoned-again session doesn't inflate its reported duration. Exposed two PRE-EXISTING test fixture bugs in the process, the same shape as R331's own seed-script mistake: two tests (`repo.test.ts`, `now-model.test.ts`) called `startSession` without an explicit `at` against a session meant to represent "started days ago," so the session's own `updated_at` silently defaulted to the test's "now" while only its SET carried the intended old date — inert under the old code (which never looked at `updated_at`), and would have failed for the wrong reason under the new code had they not been corrected to actually construct a consistent fixture. Live verification had its own false-negative first: the fix appeared not to work on the first check, and rather than conclude the fix was wrong, restarted the dev server (the same stale-Fast-Refresh lesson from earlier tonight) — on a genuinely fresh server and a freshly reseeded fixture, "EDIT THIS WORKOUT" correctly resumed the session: **SET 3, 2 sets already logged, UNDO and FINISH both live**. 1598 green (+2 real regression tests for the exact reopen-then-instant-reclose shape, both fixture bugs corrected), tsc clean, both gates clean. next: three more unusual-circumstance profiles remain on the peer's own list (storage/write failure, corrupt/partial record, clock moving backwards or across DST) — worth at least one more pass, since this first one found the night's most serious bug in under twenty minutes of live driving.

Clean — `weekIndex` already reads the LOCAL calendar date via `getFullYear`/`getMonth`/`getDate` before doing any day-boundary arithmetic, which is exactly the discipline that avoids the DST bug class (naively dividing raw milliseconds by a 24-hour constant, which breaks on the one 23-hour or 25-hour day a year) — this was already correctly designed, not accidentally safe. No code change; a real, checked negative result, not assumed from reading the function alone. 1598 green, unchanged, tsc clean. next: storage/write failure and a corrupt/partially-written record remain unexplored, but as R334 already noted, neither is honestly drivable live in a web preview — there is no real device storage to fault-inject, and fabricating "corruption" would test the browser's error boundary rather than the app's own domain logic, risking a manufactured finding rather than a real one. Three unusual-circumstance profiles run tonight (killed mid-workout: the session's best find, fixed; clock backward: clean; DST boundary: clean) is a strong, honestly-bounded close for this vein — the remaining two items on the list are better served by naming the limitation than by forcing a synthetic test that would not resemble what actually happens on a device.
