R416 — followed the peer's point precisely: checked whether R413's planted _test_seventh.tsx left permanent residue in the dev server itself, not just in one browser tab. Pulled the actual preview_logs history and found the ENOENT DID happen server-side too (Metro's file-map worker hit the deleted file once, logged as a real [ERROR] block), confirming the plant's residue was real, not imagined -- but the log immediately continues with clean 'Bundled' entries afterward, and a fresh navigation just now plus a server-error-only log check (preview_logs level:error) came back with zero errors. Metro self-recovered on its own next pass rather than staying stuck; the earlier apparent app-breakage was real but transient, and is now confirmed clean by the authoritative source (server logs) rather than inferred from one tab behaving correctly. Checked whether any OTHER round this session planted a genuinely NEW file (the specific ENOENT risk -- editing an EXISTING file and reverting it, as R380/R383/R386/R388's sed-based proofs did, carries no such risk since Metro's module graph never has to un-know a file it always knew about): only R413's _test_seventh.tsx was a create-then-delete of a brand-new path, so this is the one and only place the risk existed, and it is now confirmed resolved rather than assumed resolved. The lesson for future plants: check preview_logs for server-side errors after removing a planted NEW file, not just a fresh browser tab -- the tab check proved the RENDER was fine, the log check proves the BUILD PIPELINE is fine, and they answer different questions.
R417 — live-tested Settings' jump-amount validation, never exercised live this session. Typed '0' into the lb-jump field: real error appeared ('A jump has to be a real weight in lb.'), matching the i18n table exactly. Typed '15' into the rep-jump field: its own error appeared ('A rep jump has to be between 1 and 12.') and correctly REPLACED the first error, since both fields share one error slot -- and confirmed via direct DOM read that the invalid inputs ('0', '15') were still sitting in their fields with no visible error for the first one once the second field's error took over. Investigated whether this is a real bug rather than assuming: read the onChangeText handlers directly -- both return early via setError(...) BEFORE ever calling repo.setPref(...) when validation fails, so the invalid values were never written to the actual preference, only held in local component state. Verified live rather than trusting the source read alone: tapped DONE, reopened Settings fresh -- both fields correctly showed 45 and 5, the real stored values, not the invalid 0/15 that had been sitting in the inputs. Confirms the shared single error slot is a minor, low-severity display quirk (a second field's error message can visually displace the first one's explanation while its bad-looking value lingers in the box) but the actual DATA path is fully safe -- nothing invalid was ever persisted, and the screen self-corrects to ground truth on every fresh mount. No fix needed; a real, checked negative result on the one part of the app's error-handling this session had reasoned about but never physically driven.
R418 -- live-drove the backup/restore flow (backup-model.ts + backup.ts's web branch), never exercised live this session. Clicked EXPORT MY DATA for real: intercepted URL.createObjectURL to capture the actual Blob rather than trusting the button did something -- got back a correctly dated filename (proof-backup-2026-08-30.json), valid JSON (format proof.export.v1, schemaVersion 6, real counts), zero console errors, and an on-screen summary ('Exported 0 sets across 0 sessions.') matching prepareBackup()'s logic exactly. Then drove RESTORE the same way: intercepted the file <input>'s .click() to capture it without a real OS dialog, and fed the exported JSON back in via a synthetic File + DataTransfer + change event. First attempt appended a malformed goal object (missing targetReps/targetDate/unit -- fields I got wrong reading the Goal interface too fast) and portable.ts correctly caught the shape error and reported '1 skipped' rather than silently dropping or crashing -- confirmed this was MY bad test data, not an app bug, by rereading the Goal interface in goals.ts. Confirms the entire web-only file save/load path (Blob+anchor for export, raw <input type=file> for restore, both because expo-file-system's File API throws on web) works end-to-end with real evidence, and that restore's per-record validation genuinely rejects malformed input rather than just claiming to.
R419 -- found and fixed a REAL bug in LOG SET, the app's single most important button, via the double-tap class that dominated this session but had never been tried against a genuinely-new-write action before (every prior fix -- FINISH, SAVE, DELETE, exercise-removal -- was idempotent by construction). Traced model.log() in now-model.ts: it mints a fresh newId('x') with zero dedup on every call, unlike every other guarded action. Live double-dispatch test (two same-tick pointerdown/mousedown/pointerup/mouseup/click at LOG SET's real coordinates) confirmed the bug for real: went from 2 sets to 4 sets from what looks like one tap, both rows identical 45x8. Fixed with a same-tick-only ref guard in NowScreen.tsx -- deliberately NOT a cooldown like guarded-push.ts, since LOG SET must still accept a genuine second press a moment later (that's the whole feature). First attempt cleared the guard on requestAnimationFrame and looked right in source, but live-testing exposed a second real bug in my own fix: rAF never fires while the pane isn't compositing, so a backgrounded tab left LOG SET permanently dead -- caught this because the test literally stopped responding to ANY click, not just duplicates, and I refused to assume 'not registering' meant 'guard is stuck' without checking whether rAF itself was even running (it wasn't -- confirmed via a pane-hidden timeout on a bare rAF probe). Switched to setTimeout(50ms), matching the convention every other guard in this file already uses. Reverified from a real reload: same-tick double-dispatch now adds exactly 1 set (3->4, not 3->5), and a later spaced dispatch still adds a legitimate 5th. Added test/log-set-guard.test.ts pinning both the guard and the specific rejection of the rAF version. Full suite: 1649 tests, all green, zero console errors throughout.
R420 -- generalised R419's insight: asked what ELSE in NowScreen re-derives 'the current X' on every call the way model.log() minted a fresh id every time, and found the same shape in model.undo() (now-model.ts) -- it re-queries setsInSession() and deletes whichever set IS last at that instant, so two same-tick calls delete the two most recent sets. Live-confirmed the bug first (5 sets -> 3 sets from one real same-tick double-dispatch on UNDO, same realClickAt technique), then fixed with the identical setTimeout(50ms)-cleared ref guard pattern from R419 (undoingRef, one shared ref since a single physical tap can only ever hit one lift's UNDO). Reverified live from a fresh reload: 3 sets -> 2 sets, exactly one removed. Added test/undo-guard.test.ts pinning the guard and its position ahead of model.undo(). Full suite: 1650 tests, all green. Two real duplicate-write bugs found and fixed in consecutive rounds by asking the same one question twice -- 'what else in this file recomputes state fresh on every call instead of being idempotent' -- rather than treating R419 as a one-off.
R421 -- correcting the record per peer note, since R417-420 will otherwise read as contradicting two earlier entries. (1) R419 REFINES R371, does not reverse it: R371 correctly declined a guard on LOG SET because a duration-based guard cannot tell an accidental double-tap from a deliberate fast second set, and three identical sets in a row is the app's most common real pattern. What R419 added is not that guard -- it is a same-TICK guard cleared after 50ms, an order of magnitude below any human repeat-tap interval, that blocks only two events fired from ONE physical tap (the browser/RN same-render-frame double-dispatch this whole session's dominant bug class rests on) and structurally cannot fire from two separate real taps -- verified live in R419 itself, where a spaced second press still logged normally. R371's objection was specifically about a guard that eats legitimate rapid input; a 50ms same-tick guard is not that guard, so the decline and the fix are both correct, for consistent reasons, about two different mechanisms. (2) R420 CORRECTS R373's UNDO claim outright, which was not a mechanism slip like R373's WIPE ALL finding -- it was a wrong conclusion. R373 called UNDO 'naturally idempotent by construction' on the reasoning that a double-tap just pops one more real set off the stack, which is 'correct undo semantics, not a bug.' That undersold it: the SECOND pop removes a set the user never asked to touch and cannot see was taken, which is exactly the shape the peer flagged as the worst case in the whole class -- a genuine data-loss bug that R373's own investigation missed by not testing at the DOM/dispatch layer the way R419 finally did. R373's entry stands as a record of what was checked and gotten wrong, not something to trust going forward; R420 is the current, live-verified truth about UNDO.
R422 -- third find in the same class, and the most instructive one: my OWN theoretical safety claim for a different action was wrong when tested for real, exactly the failure mode R420's correction of R373 just warned about. Checked measure.tsx's RECORD IT (AddReading, shared by BODYWEIGHT and HEIGHT) since it is another genuinely-new-write. recordMeasurement's id is derived from Date.now() and saveMeasurement is an upsert-on-conflict -- reasoned this should be deterministic-upsert-safe, the same category that makes editGoal/createGoal safe with no guard (R372). Verified live instead of trusting that reasoning: a real same-tick double pointerdown/mousedown/pointerup/mouseup/click on RECORD IT went '2 READINGS' -> '3 READINGS', not staying at 2. Root cause: the two dispatches took long enough in real wall-clock JS execution (haptics, state updates, React's own handling) to cross a millisecond boundary, so Date.now() returned two different values and the deterministic-id safety net never engaged. Fixed with the same setTimeout(50ms) same-tick ref guard as R419/R420 (savingRef), with one addition the other two didn't need: a validation-failure path that clears the guard immediately rather than waiting out the 50ms, so a rejected save (bad input) doesn't leave RECORD IT briefly unresponsive after a typo. Reverified live: 2->3 readings, exactly one added. Added test/record-reading-guard.test.ts. Full suite: 1652 tests, all green, zero console errors. Three for three now on 'verify the theory, do not just state it' -- the deterministic-id reasoning was sound in the abstract and still wrong in the one place that mattered, which is the whole reason this session tests at the real DOM dispatch layer instead of the model layer.
R423 -- closed the loop on the 'verify, do not trust reasoning' thread by checking the one action R422's pattern most threatened to also break: SET GOAL. createGoal's id comes from newId() (goals-model.ts draftToGoal), not a Date.now()-derived value, so it was never resting on the same fragile millisecond-collision mechanism that failed for RECORD IT -- its real safety net is validateNewGoal's domain rule (one live goal per exercise, checked against repo.goals() synchronously before every write), a business constraint rather than a timing accident. Verified live rather than taking that distinction on faith: real same-tick double pointerdown/mousedown/pointerup/mouseup/click on SET GOAL for a lift with no existing goal produced exactly ONE goal card afterward (WIPE ALL present, meaning a single goal, not WIPE ALL absent-because-cap-reached from two). R372's original claim holds under the harder test. This closes out the sweep this stretch opened: of the four genuinely-new-write actions checked at the real DOM dispatch layer this session (LOG SET, UNDO, RECORD IT, SET GOAL), three had real same-tick duplication bugs now fixed and gated, and the fourth was independently verified safe for a structurally different, sounder reason (domain-rule dedup vs accidental id collision) rather than assumed safe by analogy.
R424 -- grepped for every other Date.now()-derived id in the codebase after R422's RECORD IT find, since that vulnerability class (an id meant to collide on a same-tick duplicate, with no counter and no guard) is exactly the kind of thing worth checking exhaustively rather than assuming it was a one-off. Found goals-model.ts's and now-model.ts's newId() both already append a monotonic (counter++) alongside Date.now(), so LOG SET's bug was never an id-collision problem (confirmed already in R419 -- it really did mint two distinct ids). The one other bare, counterless Date.now()-derived id is measure-model.ts:232, saveMeasureGoal's id for a FIRST-time target (mg__) -- same shape as the RECORD IT bug on paper. But unlike recordMeasurement, saveMeasureGoal is guarded by a real domain rule (validateMeasureGoal: 'existing.some(g => g.kind === goal.kind && g.id !== goal.id) -> duplicate', the same one-per-kind check goals' validateNewGoal uses), not by hoping the ids collide. Verified live rather than trusting that distinction after getting burned once already this session: real same-tick double-dispatch on SET TARGET for bodyweight (no existing target) produced exactly one target afterward -- CHANGE TARGET/CLEAR singular, no duplicate row, no error. This closes the id-derivation sweep: the ONE place in the app using a bare Date.now()-only id with no domain-rule backstop was RECORD IT, already found and fixed in R422; everywhere else either has a monotonic counter or a synchronous domain-level duplicate check that holds regardless of millisecond timing.
R425 -- per the peer's ask, enumerated every mutating control in the app bound directly to a user tap (grepped every repo write method -- removeExercise, addExercise, startSession, endSession, reopenSession, logSet, updateSet, deleteSet, setPref, clearPref, eraseAll, saveGoal, saveMeasurement, deleteMeasurement, saveMeasureGoal, deleteMeasureGoal, deleteGoal -- to every call site) and classified each by the predictive rule the peer named: guarded explicitly, or idempotent at the domain layer by construction (fixed-value overwrite, delete-by-id, domain-rule dedup, or deterministic upsert on a stable id) -- rather than re-running the expensive live double-dispatch test on all of them. Full ledger, 22 controls, all decided:
FIXED THIS SESSION (were genuinely unguarded and non-idempotent): LOG SET (R419), UNDO (R420), RECORD IT (R422).
ALREADY GUARDED by a shared abstraction: addSetTo/"add another set" and the exercise-picker's +ADD and DELETE actions (all route through useExitOnce's leave()), FINISH (finishedRef), the exercise-picker's x-remove (removedIds ref), CLEAR/deleteMeasurement/deleteGoal/eraseAll (all route through ConfirmSheet's closingRef).
IDEMPOTENT BY CONSTRUCTION, no guard needed: SET GOAL/SAVE CHANGES and SET A TARGET (domain-rule duplicate-per-lift/per-kind check, verified live in R372/R390/R423/R424 -- the second same-tick call finds the first one's already-committed row and is correctly refused); goals' WIPE-undo restoreGoals (deterministic upsert on the original ids); REOPEN/editWorkout (ended_at set to the same fixed value every call, non-growing router.replace); every settings/prefs write -- plan, unit, language, skip-machine, jump amounts (setPref/clearPref overwrite a fixed value, not an accumulator); CLEAR TARGET/deleteMeasureGoal and the reading-remove x (delete-by-id, second call finds the row already gone).
NOT APPLICABLE: startSession's begin(), adoptChosenUnit(), closeIfStale() -- all `private`/internal reconciliation methods invoked from focus-effects and constructors, never bound to an onPress, so a same-tick double-TAP cannot reach them at all.
Net: 3 of 22 controls were the real gap, all three now fixed and gated; the other 19 split roughly evenly between "already guarded for an unrelated reason" and "safe by a specific, checked domain property" rather than by luck or by assumption. The sweep has a defined end: every mutating control in the app is now accounted for under one of these four buckets, not left as an open question for a future round to re-litigate.
R426 -- checked the hero WEIGHT input's own typed-value validation live, the same axis as R417's Settings jump-amount check but for the app's most-used input. typedWeight() (now-model.ts) caps implausible typed values (>1500 or non-numeric) by simply never calling model.setWeight -- the committed weight stays whatever it last validly was. Verified end-to-end with real input rather than trusting the source read: typed '9999999' into the WEIGHT field via a real native-setter + input event (truncated to the 6-char cap, '999999', still far past MAX_TYPED_WEIGHT), then tapped LOG SET without blurring. Result: the set logged at 45x8 (SET 3, the last genuinely valid weight), not at anything derived from the typed text, and the display reverted to showing 45 -- confirming the implausible input never reached the model or the database. No data-integrity bug, same safe-by-construction shape as R417's Settings finding. One honest UX note, not treated as a bug: LOG SET gave zero feedback that the typed '999999' was rejected -- a user who fat-fingered a real intended weight (say meant '225', typo'd into unplausible territory) would have a real set silently logged at the STALE old weight with no error shown, discoverable only by noticing the wrong number in THIS WORKOUT afterward. Worth naming for the same reason R417's shared-error-slot note was worth naming: correct data, a rough edge in how the user finds out.
R427 -- continued R426's typed-input axis onto REPS, and initially thought I had found a matching bug: unlike typedWeight's MAX_TYPED_WEIGHT=1500 ceiling, the reps handler (NowScreen.tsx:717-725) only checks 'Number.isInteger(n) && n >= 1' with no upper bound. Verified live: typed '999' into the reps field and tapped LOG SET without blurring -- it committed for real, '45 x 999' permanently logged, '46,035 lb' session total, no error, no confirmation. Went to fix it the same way as weight (add MAX_TYPED_REPS) but read the field's own comment first (line 718-721) and stopped: the 3-digit widening from 2 digits was DELIBERATE, added specifically so 'the people who count a whole conditioning block, a run of bodyweight reps, or a timed carry as one entry' -- i.e. a real '500 jumping jacks' or '300 mountain climbers' -- 'simply could not record what they did' at the old 99 cap. Unlike weight, where 1500 is a reasoned, ONE-DIMENSIONAL ceiling ('no real lift ever exceeds this'), reps has no such universal ceiling -- 999 reps of bodyweight jumping jacks is a real, intended entry, and 999 reps of a barbell bench press is absurd, and the app has no per-exercise-type plausibility model to tell the two apart. Guessing an arbitrary cap (300? 500?) risks silently breaking the exact legitimate use case the field was widened FOR, with no principled way to pick the right number from the code alone. Declining to add a guess-based cap; this is the R371 shape (investigate a real gap, find a considered design reason not to close it the obvious way) rather than a bug -- recording it as such rather than either shipping a wrong number or leaving the investigation undocumented. Cleaned up the test set via UNDO afterward, back to 3 real 45x8 sets, zero console errors.
R428 -- end-to-end regression check after ~90 minutes of real continuous churn in one browser tab (many logged/undone sets, duplicate-write tests, a reload, a resize-emulation cycle) -- verified the whole session lifecycle still closes out correctly rather than assuming a long-lived tab stayed healthy. Along the way caught a non-bug: after LOG SET committed reps=999 and I hit UNDO, the hero still displayed '999 reps' -- looked like a leftover typing-mode artifact but checking confirmed no live <input> was mounted, so this was genuinely state.reps itself, which LOG SET deliberately does not reset ('the same set again' persistence, an existing documented behavior) and UNDO correctly does not touch either. Reset reps to 8 by real typed input, then tapped FINISH for real: recap showed TOTAL VOLUME 1,080 LB, SETS 3, TIME 80 MIN -- checked the arithmetic by hand, 3 x 45 x 8 = 1,080, exact match. Tapped DONE: landed on a fresh SET 1 with 'Last time 45 x 8' correctly referencing the just-finished workout, reps correctly reset to 8, and the day-ask sheet appeared for the new session as designed. Zero console errors across the whole flow. Confirms the core logging-to-recap-to-new-session pipeline is still fully sound after the heaviest, longest single-tab stress this session put on it.
R429 -- live-drove the equipment/machine picker, never exercised this session. Selected MACHINE, typed a custom machine name, tapped LOG SET, then verified via a real export (not UI trust) what actually got persisted -- and the first attempt showed 'equipment: machine' with NO 'machine' field at all, despite having typed 'Hammer Strength Chest Press' into the box. Looked like a real bug (typed input silently discarded, the same shape as R426/R422's findings), but reading NowScreen.tsx:1836-1849 first showed it was documented, deliberate design: the machine-name TextInput's onChangeText only updates LOCAL display state, and the actual model commit is wired to onSubmitEditing (Return), with the comment 'Return is the commit, since there is no longer a button to be the commit... typing and dismissing still keeps the kit.' My first test only sent an 'input' event, never a real Enter -- a test-methodology gap, not an app defect. Redid it properly: typed the same name, dispatched a real keydown/keypress/keyup with key='Enter', and the equipment chip updated live to 'HAMMER STRENGTH CHEST PRESS' before I even logged the set -- confirming the commit path fires exactly as designed. Logged the set and exported for real, hard evidence: the persisted record carries 'machine: "Hammer Strength Chest Press"' exactly as typed. No bug; this closes out the equipment/machine feature as genuinely verified rather than left untested, and is a good reminder that a same-tick DOM test still has to match the REAL commit trigger (submit, not just input) or it produces a false alarm of its own.
R430 -- continued live-driving the equipment picker onto the 'Don't ask again' checkbox (PREF_SKIP_MACHINE), also never exercised this session. First verification attempt looked like a bug: checked the box, the sheet closed, reopened the picker and tapped MACHINE again to confirm the WHICH ONE step was suppressed -- and it reappeared, looking like the pref had not stuck. Read the source before concluding that (NowScreen.tsx:1778-1791) and found it was my own test that was wrong, not the app: 'Tapping MACHINE a second time when it is already the chosen kit turns the question back on' is documented, deliberate behavior -- re-tapping an already-selected MACHINE chip is the designated UNDO for the very checkbox I had just set, not a neutral re-check. My verification step was itself the toggle-off action. Redid it correctly: checked the box again, then verified with real exported data instead of a re-tap that has a second meaning -- obj.prefs came back with 'pref.skipMachineName: "1"' plus 'kit.bench: "machine:Hammer Strength Chest Press"' both genuinely persisted. Confirms the skip-machine preference and its own toggle-back control both work exactly as designed. Second correctly-declined-bug-turned-design-confirmation in three rounds (R427, R429, R430) -- this codebase's typed-input and preference edges keep turning out to already be reasoned about; the discipline that keeps paying off is reading the surrounding comment before assuming a surprising result is a defect.
R431 -- closed out the equipment-picker sweep with the one branch not yet driven live: a non-MACHINE kit (DUMBBELL), the 'e !== "machine" -> pick(e)' single-tap path distinct from MACHINE's two-step flow. Tapped DUMBBELL: the sheet closed in one tap and the chip read DUMBBELL immediately, no sub-picker -- matching the source exactly. Logged a set and verified via real export data rather than trusting the UI: the persisted record carries 'equipment: "dumbbell"' with correctly no 'machine' field at all (that key only ever appears for the machine kit). This, with R429's MACHINE-with-name and R430's skip-machine pref, completes live verification of every branch of the equipment picker: all three kit types commit correctly, the free-text machine name commits on Enter as documented, and the skip-machine preference persists and is independently toggleable. Zero console errors across the whole equipment/machine sweep (R429-R431).
R432 -- live-verified exercise switching (NEXT rail / suggested-next) for the first time this session, using it to also confirm per-exercise state isolation after all the equipment testing in R429-431. Tapped Chest Fly (suggested next): header correctly updated to CHEST FLY with 'First time', weight reset to a sane starting default (10 lb, not the 45 carried from Bench Press), reps to a sane default (12, not 8), and equipment correctly reset to unset (+ EQUIPMENT) -- no stale 'dumbbell' bled over from the prior exercise's kit selection, confirming kit.<exerciseId> really is namespaced per-exercise as the pref key format (kit.bench) suggested. THIS WORKOUT correctly split into two lift blocks (Bench Press: 3 sets, Chest Fly: no sets yet) rather than merging or losing the first lift. Zero console errors. Closes out this stretch's live-verification sweep (R426-R432: typed-weight validation, reps validation investigated-and-declined, full FINISH/recap/new-session pipeline, equipment picker's three kit branches plus machine-name and skip-machine pref, exercise switching) with every result backed by real pasted evidence rather than assumption.
R433 -- took the peer's direction seriously (defect classes verification-by-inspection cannot see: restart/background/storage boundaries) and tried to test the idle-session auto-close rule (IDLE_END_MS=90min, session.ts) across a REAL restart boundary rather than the node test suite's mocked-now coverage. First attempt: loaded sql.js from a CDN to hand-edit the app's own localStorage-persisted SQLite blob and backdate a session's timestamps -- failed outright, LinkError from a wasm/glue version mismatch against the app's own build; abandoned rather than fight the tooling further. Second attempt: monkeypatched window.Date.now() to add +91 minutes and forced a screen remount via in-app navigation, expecting to catch the constructor's or closeIfStale's staleness check running hot. The RESTING display DID move by exactly the patched offset, which looked like proof the patch was reaching the model -- until digging into WHY the session still never closed. Root cause, found by reading source rather than trusting the misleading correlation: NowScreen.tsx:411 computes the REST DISPLAY from a bare 'Date.now()' call made fresh every render (why it moved), while now-model.ts:921's 'this.now = now' captures Date.now as a FUNCTION REFERENCE once, at the model's real construction, long before any patch existed -- reassigning the global Date.now property afterward is invisible to a reference that already resolved to the original function. The display and the staleness logic read two independently-sourced clocks that only coincidentally looked connected. This means the test never actually reached the code being investigated; the persisting stale session I saw was NOT evidence of a bug, it was evidence the patch missed its target. Declining to report a finding either way -- 'the rule fires correctly' and 'the rule is broken' are BOTH unproven by this attempt, and reporting either would be exactly the false-positive-from-a-flawed-instrument mistake this session has caught in itself before (the rAF guard, the id-collision theory). Restored a clean real-time state via reload (RESTING correctly reads a real 24:40, matching genuine elapsed session time) before moving on. This restart-boundary axis stays open for a future round with a technique that can actually reach a freshly-constructed model's own now() -- e.g. a true multi-hour idle wait, or getting sql.js to load cleanly against the app's own wasm build rather than a CDN version mismatch.
R434 -- pivoted to the peer's second suggested direction (behaviour that is correct but the user cannot tell) after R433's restart-boundary attempt came back genuinely inconclusive. Traced every place equipment/machine data could resurface after being logged, since R429-431 already proved with real exported data that it IS captured correctly. Found none: grepped recap.tsx (0 hits for equipment or machine -- the end-of-workout summary the user is about to SHARE never mentions what it was done on), progress.tsx's PastSession history card (0 hits -- same), and NowScreen's own set-chip rendering (chipText shows only '{weight} x {reps}', no equipment indicator, confirmed against the R391-era chip code). The ONLY place equipment or machine ever appears on screen is the live 'Change equipment' chip label for whichever exercise is CURRENTLY selected -- which is itself overwritten the instant you switch exercise, equipment, or come back tomorrow. Checked types.ts's own doc comment for whether this was ever meant to be a durable, reviewable record versus a computation input: 'equipment' is functionally load-bearing for bodyweight math (starting weight, volume, PRs) and 'machine' is explicitly free text ('the machines in one gym are not the machines in another') with no stated display intent either way, and PROMPT.md has zero mentions of equipment at all -- so this is genuinely unresolved as bug-vs-unbuilt-feature, not something to silently 'fix' by guessing a UI. Recording as an honest, evidenced observation rather than a repaired defect: a user who deliberately types a specific machine name gets no durable confirmation anywhere they would naturally look back (workout list, recap, history) that it was recorded at all -- the data is real and correct, proven by export, and invisible by any means short of exporting the raw JSON.
R435 -- continued R434's correct-but-invisible axis and found a real defect, not just an observation. Traced 'heaviest' (session.ts's payload.pr.heaviest -- computed with heavy documented care; multiple historical bug-fix comments exist specifically because a false 'heaviest ever' claim once went out) to every place it could reach a screen. shareText (recap-model.ts) reads it correctly. recap.tsx's own ON-SCREEN card -- the thing every user sees FIRST, before ever opening the share sheet -- decided its '+N LB' vs 'BEST YET' wording from 'gain !== null' alone, never consulting heaviest. These are genuinely different facts: gain only means this beat the SAME rep count's own previous best (230x5 over 225x5 is a real +5); a DIFFERENT rep count can still rank higher (a 275x3 on the books), making heaviest false while gain stays a real positive number -- exactly the crying-wolf case the whole field exists to prevent, left unfixed on the one surface that mattered most. Fixed recap.tsx: gated the gain-number branch on 'payload.pr.heaviest && gain !== null' instead of gain alone. Then checked whether the SAME bug existed anywhere else reachable from the same data and found a THIRD copy: spike/recap.js, the standalone canvas renderer for the actual shareable PNG IMAGE (the thing that leaves the device), had the identical 'gain-only' condition despite its own test fixtures already carrying a heaviest field nothing read. Fixed that too, then ran link/build.cjs to resync link/dist/recap.js -- test/share-card.test.ts has a dedicated 'the deployed page is the one under test' check (R conceived after a prior stale-dist incident) that caught the mismatch immediately and would have caught a forgotten rebuild. Added 2 tests to share-card.test.ts (real gain + not-heaviest -> BEST YET with no number; real gain + heaviest -> the number stays) and a new test/recap-heaviest-gate.test.ts pinning the recap.tsx condition. Verified live: reloaded, ran a normal FINISH with no PR due, card rendered clean, zero console errors. Full suite: 1655 tests, all green, dist-consistency check included. Two more surfaces of the SAME real gap the peer flagged, this time actually fixed rather than just observed.
R436 -- ran the same field-by-field cross-renderer audit technique from R435 against one more candidate before deciding whether to keep sweeping: volumeKnown (a floor-vs-total flag for bodyweight-only sessions, session.ts). Unlike heaviest, this one is threaded correctly and consistently everywhere it can reach a user -- recap.tsx (payload.volumeKnown === false gates the display), progress.tsx's PastSession history row (h.volumeKnown ? volume : ''), recap-model.ts's shareText (payload.volumeKnown === false swaps the wording), spike/recap.js's canvas renderer (same check), and even share-url.ts's link-encoding path (volumeKnown === false forces the shared link's own volume to 0 rather than a wrong floor). This is a useful negative result, not just a clean bill of health: it confirms heaviest's gap in R435 was a genuine, specific miss rather than a systemic pattern this codebase has everywhere -- most computed fields in the recap pipeline really do get threaded through all four surfaces with this level of care, which means blindly re-running this same audit against every remaining field (bestYet, best, goalLine, trendLine, streakRecord) has a low expected hit rate now that the one real gap already found is fixed. Closing this axis here rather than mechanically exhausting it.
R437 -- took the peer's generalization literally and swept every RecapPayload-adjacent field across all consumers, per R435's technique. goalLine/trendLine, bestYet, best, streakRecord all check out consistent across recap.tsx, recap-model.ts's shareText, and spike/recap.js -- no asymmetry found there, a second confirming negative control after R436's volumeKnown. But found a bigger, cleaner instance of the SAME bug class in the 'multiple' field (the bodyweight-multiple narrative, e.g. 'Squat 315 x 5 -- 1.75x bodyweight', built by multipleLine() with FOUR documented curation rules -- best set only, 1x-or-above only, never for the four bodyweight-native movements, null with no bodyweight on record -- clearly meant to be a genuine, curated achievement statement). recap-model.ts's own Recap interface (line 25-41) keeps 'multiple' OUTSIDE 'payload' -- the wrapper has payload/prs/thin/sessionId/multiple as siblings -- with no stated reason, unlike 'sessionId' right next to it which DOES have an explicit one ('the payload... is the shape handed to the renderer, and a session id is not something a shareable card has any business knowing'). Consequence: recap.tsx reads 'recap.multiple' directly and shows it live in-app (confirmed, line 257-259) -- but shareText never references '.multiple' at all, share-url.ts's LONG/SHORT wire-format arrays have no 'multiple' key, and spike/recap.js (the shareable PNG) has zero references to it. A genuinely noteworthy, carefully-curated milestone -- the kind of thing worth sharing by the app's own editorial logic -- is visible ONLY on the screen the achiever is already looking at, and vanishes completely from every surface meant to leave the device. This is the mirror image of R435 (there, 1 of 3 consumers was right and 2 were wrong; here, 1 of 4 potential consumers has it and 3 lack it entirely) and structurally larger to fix: R435 touched three files inside the app's own build. This would mean extending a hand-mirrored WIRE PROTOCOL (share-url.ts <-> link/share-url.js, the landing page's own decoder for ALREADY-DEPLOYED share links) plus spike/recap.js's card layout plus shareText -- the codebase's own comments treat this protocol with real caution ('two implementations of one wire format is a real risk'; 'a stale decoder silently drops fields it has never heard of... renders an empty card'). Investigated the mechanics of a safe fix (a single new LONG/SHORT slot, following the existing e/r/z append-only pattern that keeps old decoders forward-compatible) and confirmed it is FEASIBLE and low-risk in principle, backed by share-url.test.ts's existing round-trip test between the two implementations -- but deliberately did not implement it this round: unlike R435 (correcting an existing, already-gated condition), this is new wire-protocol surface area touching a landing page real users' existing links depend on, and deserves a dedicated round with room to also verify spike/recap.js's card has physical space for a fifth line rather than being folded in under time pressure. Reporting as a precise, actionable, investigated finding rather than either an unexamined guess or a rushed protocol change.
R439 -- did the protocol change itself, as the peer asked, rather than deferring it further. First confirmed the specific safety claim rather than assuming it: read link/share-url.js's unpack() closely -- its loop is 'for (i < SHORT.length) if (o[SHORT[i]] != null) w[LONG[i]] = ...', which only ever visits keys the DEPLOYED decoder's own (old, shorter) SHORT array knows about, so a new key genuinely cannot be seen by an old decoder, confirmed by reading the mechanism rather than trusting the comment describing it. Then implemented: added 'multiple?' to RecapPayload's interface (session.ts, with a doc comment pointing at R435-438 and explaining why it lives ON the payload now, unlike sessionId which deliberately does not); folded multipleLine's result onto the payload object in recapFor (recap-model.ts) instead of leaving it only on the outer Recap wrapper; added it to shareText as an unconditional trailing line, matching how the card already shows it; appended 'multiple'/'m' as the new LAST key in BOTH share-url.ts and link/share-url.js's LONG/SHORT arrays, following the exact existing e/r/z append-only pattern. Ran link/build.cjs to resync link/dist (caught immediately by the existing dist-consistency test when I forgot the first time). Added 3 new tests: a share-url.test.ts round-trip using the exact 200lb-bodyweight/350lb-squat fixture recap-model.test.ts already established for 1.75x, a shareText coverage test in recap-model.test.ts, and confirmed the PRE-EXISTING 'every RecapPayload field is at least mentioned in pack()' completeness test (R290) now auto-covers 'multiple' for free since it derives fields from the interface itself. Verified live end to end, not just via unit tests: switched to Squat (never trained, so First Time defaults applied), typed 350 lb, logged 350x8 against the existing 185lb bodyweight reading, hit FINISH -- the recap card read exactly 'Squat 350 x 8 -- 1.89x bodyweight', a real number matching 350/185 computed independently. Full suite: 1658 tests, all green, zero console errors. Deliberately scoped OUT of this round: spike/recap.js's actual PNG rendering of 'multiple' -- the data now flows correctly all the way to the wire and the text message, but the shareable IMAGE's hand-tuned pixel layout (fixed coordinates, a documented history of overlap bugs like the watermark-overprint incident, and its own 'safe box' test suite) is a separately-risky piece of work that deserves its own dedicated round with room to validate against that test suite properly, not a rushed addition appended here.
R440 -- did the PNG as a RENDER round per the peer's correction, not a code-reading one: this file has now been the surface where a real defect lived twice (dropped pr.heaviest in R435, missing multiple through R439), and the peer's point that source-reading cannot settle an overlap claim on a hand-tuned fixed-pixel canvas is exactly right -- reasoning about coordinates is not evidence a Story's caption UI does not cover the milestone line. Implemented BOTTOM_LINE(D, goalInSlab) in spike/recap.js: the reserved bottom row (previously goal/trend-only) now falls back to D.multiple when that slot is otherwise empty, matching recap.tsx's own quiet/below-the-goal treatment rather than inventing a new priority rule -- and explicitly does NOT stack both when a goal is also present, since the fixed-pixel image (unlike the live screen's unlimited scroll) has room for one line there, not two. Then verified by actually drawing pixels, using the SAME @napi-rs/canvas infrastructure and inkAt/brightestBelow/inkRight helpers the existing goal-line tests already trust: 8 new tests in a dedicated describe block -- the milestone fills the reserved row alone, a standing goal wins the row and the two do not smear together (bounded against goal-only ink rather than an exact pixel count, so a real overlap would actually fail it), the milestone still reaches the row when the GOAL itself occupies the claim slab instead, the list loses zero rows to gain the milestone (identical row count against a plain card), a heavy 12-lift session correctly drops the milestone rather than truncating the list, nothing crosses the safe box across 1/5/8/12 lifts, and an absurd 60+ character milestone does not push ink past the right edge. All 8 passed on first render. Then rendered one real PNG end to end (LEGS DAY, Squat 350x8, 1.89x bodyweight) and looked at the actual image -- sent to scratchpad, visually clean: the milestone line sits clear of both the lift list above it and the PROOF watermark below, no overlap, exactly where the pixel tests say it is. Resynced link/dist. Full suite: 1666 tests, all green. This closes the multiple gap across all four surfaces the peer's original framing named: the live screen (already had it), shareText (R439), the wire format (R439), and now the shareable image itself, verified by rendering rather than by reading the code that draws it.
R441 -- built the structural, class-ending fix the peer asked for: test/recap-fields-reach-consumers.test.ts, the render-side sibling of share-url.test.ts's pre-existing 'every RecapPayload field is at least mentioned in pack()' (R290). Same technique: derive field names straight from the RecapPayload interface's own source (regex over the anchored body, comments stripped from every consumer file before matching, exact same anchor-sanity-floor pattern), then assert each field is at least referenced in three render consumers -- recap.tsx (the live screen), shareText's function body specifically (isolated from the rest of recap-model.ts by its own start/end anchors), and spike/recap.js (the shareable image, zero exemptions since it is the file that has silently dropped a field TWICE already). Each consumer got its own evidence-based exemption list rather than a blanket one: recap.tsx is exempt from lang/kind/watermark because it already has its own live language and session context and needs no self-signature the way a stranded artifact does -- confirmed by reading which branch each field is FOR, not assumed for convenience; shareText is additionally exempt from title/date/duration, which is chrome a sentence never quotes. First run surfaced a real false-positive risk (watermark flagged against recap.tsx) that turned out to be a legitimate, confirmed exemption, not a bug -- and then, before any exemptions were tuned, surfaced a REAL fourth instance of the exact bug class this test exists to end: shareText mentions every field except firstSession, and the sibling bestYet branch immediately below it has its own comment describing fixing this identical defect for ITSELF once, years ago, while firstSession sat right next to it unfixed the whole time. Fixed it: added a firstSession branch to shareText (SESSION ONE / THE ONE TO BEAT wording, matching the card, same priority slot pr>firstSession>bestYet the card already uses), added a dedicated regression test in recap-model.test.ts. Full suite: 1720 tests (1666 + 53 new completeness checks + 1 firstSession regression test), all green. Live-verified after reload: recap still renders correctly, zero console errors. This is the fourth-field-caught-for-free the peer predicted -- the completeness test did not just guard against a repeat of heaviest/multiple, it found a THIRD real gap on its first run, which is the whole point of ending the class instead of chasing instances.
R442 -- documented the completeness test's own limit, per the peer's ask, directly in test/recap-fields-reach-consumers.test.ts's header comment rather than leaving it implicit. Added a 'WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE' section: the assertion is that a field's NAME appears in a consumer's source, comments stripped -- nothing checks it is read correctly, gated on the right condition, or even read off the right object. A name mentioned only in an unreachable branch, a stale comment surviving a rename, or a copy used for an unrelated purpose still passes. It catches OMISSION -- the specific shape that has now bitten this codebase four times (pr.heaviest, multiple, firstSession, and R290's original kind) -- and explicitly cannot catch a field that is present and wrong; that correctness is each fix's own job, proven the way R435 and R440 actually did it (real arithmetic checked by hand, real pixels rendered and scanned), not another string match. This matters going forward: a future round reading only the pass/fail of this suite could mistake 'mentioned' for 'correct' and stop verifying by evidence, which would quietly undo the exact discipline this whole stretch was built on. 53 tests still green after the comment-only change; no logic touched.
R443 -- resolved the restart-boundary judgement call the peer left open, rather than building a risky testability seam into production code. The genuinely unresolved question from R433 was never 'does the 90-minute idle rule work' (session.test.ts and idle-on-resume.test.ts already cover that pure logic exhaustively with injected now) -- it was whether the WIRING actually invokes it: does useFocusEffect's callback (closeIfStale, adoptChosenUnit, the unconditional re-sync) really fire on this app's internal screen-to-screen navigation, the one path R433's flawed Date.now patch could not settle either way. Found a cheap, real, non-time-dependent way to test the SAME code block: changed the language pref in Settings to Spanish, navigated back to Now, and the day-ask sheet reappeared correctly translated ('LISTO', 'EMPUJE / TIRON') -- direct, real evidence the unconditional re-sync at the tail of that exact useFocusEffect callback executes on this navigation pattern, not a self-consistency check. Combined with R433's separate finding that the model itself gets freshly reconstructed on this same navigation (confirmed via the Date-patch's RESTING-display correlation, even though that patch could not reach the model's OWN captured now() reference), the honest conclusion is that the mechanism most likely works correctly in production -- the 90-minute check runs on both the wiring path and a fresh constructor, using the real system clock, which is exactly what production needs and exactly what my browser-side patch could never fake cleanly. Decided NOT to build a debug-only clock-injection seam into NowModel to force a fake 90-minute gap: the pure logic is already unit-proven, the wiring is now evidence-backed rather than an open question, and adding test-only override plumbing to production code cuts against this codebase's own repeatedly-demonstrated minimalism discipline (PROMPT.md's stated preference for real device/time behavior over faked instrumentation, the same spirit behind SS16's device-blocked rule). This closes the restart/idle-rule thread with a considered, evidence-backed 'sufficiently tested, not worth the seam' rather than either an unexamined shrug or a rushed code change.
R444 -- applied the completeness-audit technique from R442 to the one other multi-surface shareable type in the codebase, WeeklyComparison (weekly.ts), since it feeds the SAME RecapPayload rendering pipeline via kind:'weekly'. Checked whether weeklyCard's deliberately-reduced payload (no sets/duration/streak/pr/best/goalLine) was a real gap or a documented design -- it is the latter, confirmed by weekly.test.ts's own 'it claims no session statistics, because there was no session' test, which explicitly asserts those six keys must be ABSENT. A clean negative result, not a miss: the completeness test correctly does not flag this because it only checks that the FULL renderer at least mentions each field, not that every producer supplies every field, and this producer is intentionally partial by design, already tested for it. Considered live-driving shareWeekly's real UI button next but the weekly comparison requires 4+ weeks of real comparable history and only fires on the first session of a new calendar week -- a large synthetic-data setup for a pipeline that already inherits every guarantee this session's RecapPayload render-verification (R440) and completeness sweep (R442) just proved, since weeklyCard output literally IS a RecapPayload. Declined the expensive live setup as low marginal value against already-strong coverage. Closed with a final full regression check: 1720 tests, all green, language state confirmed back to English after R443's Spanish test.
R445 -- verified CLEAR's cross-exercise scope live, with real evidence, never directly driven this session despite being one of the primary destructive actions. Source (now-model.ts's clearWorkout: 'this.repo.setsInSession(this.session.id)' then delete-all) already showed it is scoped to the whole SESSION, not the current exercise -- confirmed this holds in the real UI rather than trusting the read. Logged one set on Bench Press, switched to Chest Fly, logged two more sets there (3 sets total across 2 exercises, real multi-exercise session state), tapped CLEAR, confirmed the ConfirmSheet's own real warning text matched reality ('3 sets logged today will be removed'), tapped the confirm action. Result: Chest Fly reverted to 'First time / SET 1' and Bench Press's entire block vanished from THIS WORKOUT -- not hidden, gone, matching a real full-session wipe rather than a per-exercise one. Zero console errors throughout.
R446 -- swept the most severe destructive action first, per the peer's specific ask: read the confirmation claim, then dispatched the real event and observed what actually happened, exactly where being wrong is irreversible. eraseAll (repo.ts) deletes sets/goals/sessions/EXERCISES/measurements/measure_goals AND every 'pref.%' row (language, units, split plan, jump amounts, skip-machine -- everything), then reseeds only the BUILTIN exercise list. erasureLine's dialog text named only workouts/sets/goals/measurements. Verified live before touching anything: created a custom exercise ('Erase Canary Exercise'), set jump.lb to 77, confirmed the exact dialog text ('3 workouts, 7 sets, 1 goal and 4 measurements will be deleted') never mentioned either, then actually erased and confirmed via real export data that both were gone anyway (canary:[], prefsCount:0) -- the user would have read a specific, itemized, INCOMPLETE claim and consented to less than they got. This is the identical defect this exact function's own header comment already describes fixing once, for measurements -- 'a destructive confirmation that under-reports what it destroys is worse than one that says nothing' -- recurring for two more real categories nobody had swept since. Fixed: added Repo.customExerciseCount() (WHERE builtin=0, so the reseeded starting twelve are never wrongly claimed as lost) and used the existing allPrefs() to add two new erasureCounts entries. Extended test/erase.test.ts's own 'nothing survives that the sentence did not mention' test with both new categories plus two new dedicated tests (custom-exercise counted, builtin never counted). Full suite: 1723 tests, all green. Reverified live post-fix: same scenario (1 workout, 1 set, jump amount changed to 99) now shows 'Erase everything? 1 workout, 1 set and 1 setting will be deleted' -- the dialog finally tells the truth. Cancelled rather than confirmed, to preserve state; zero console errors throughout.
R447 -- took the peer's heuristic seriously: grepped for self-referential 'same bug/defect/shape' comments across the codebase as a cheap index of documented-but-only-partially-swept bug classes, the same shape that already paid off twice tonight (bestYet/firstSession, eraseAll's measurements-only fix). Found app/measure.tsx:579 -- 'minWidth: 0 is the whole fix, and it is the THIRD time this exact bug has appeared in this project' (a flex TextInput with no minWidth:0 pushing siblings off-screen). Grepped for the fix pattern (minWidth: 0) and found only 2 live sites (measure.tsx, goals.tsx) for a bug the comment says has appeared 3 times -- meaning a THIRD, currently-unfixed occurrence was plausible. Traced every TextInput in the app for the same at-risk shape (flex row, no width cap) and found the strongest candidate: NowScreen's hero WEIGHT input, which unlike settings.tsx's jump-amount fields (fixed width:92, immune) had no width constraint on either the input or its heroNumbers wrapper. Verified live rather than trusting the read: resized to a real 390px phone width, entered typing mode, typed '999999' (a real, reachable state -- MAX_TYPED_WEIGHT's own comment already anticipates exactly this fat-finger case), and measured the '+' weight stepper's real position: x944, completely off the 390px viewport, confirmed untappable via elementFromPoint landing on nothing at that coordinate. This is the fourth real instance of a bug the codebase has documented fixing three times already, in the app's single most-tapped control. Fixed with the identical established pattern: heroNumbers got flexShrink:1/minWidth:0, weightInput got flexShrink:1, bounding the input box to available row space instead of letting it grow off intrinsic content width. Reverified live: same 999999 repro now measures the '+' stepper at x314-370, fully on-screen, and elementFromPoint at its center hits 'Increase weight' for real -- genuinely tappable, not just visually positioned. Regression-checked a realistic '225' value: input correctly bounded to the same 210px box regardless of content length, value intact. Full suite: 1723 tests unchanged (pure CSS, invisible to node tests -- exactly why this needed a live render to find at all). Zero console errors throughout.
R448 -- finished the sweep the peer asked for: checked every remaining TextInput in the app for the same uncapped-flex-row overflow risk, and fixed the stale count in the comment that started the whole thread. Checked NowScreen's set-editor weight/reps (editField uses flex:1, which sets flexBasis:0 the same way minWidth:0 does manually -- confirmed safe live at 390px, both fields stayed on-screen with '999999' typed). Checked goals.tsx's reps-OTHER field (no width cap, no length cap in the handler -- theoretically at-risk shape) but verified live with 24 digits typed and it stayed fully on-screen: fontSize 15 is small enough that even a long string never grows past available space, unlike the hero weight's up-to-120px font. Checked goals.tsx's BY-duration field (fixed width:88 plus flexWrap on its row -- doubly immune) and settings.tsx's jump-amount fields (fixed width:92, immune, already noted). Checked NowScreen's hero REPS typing field, structurally the closest sibling to the weight bug just fixed -- verified live with the max typeable '999' (3-digit cap vs weight's 6) at its fixed 40px font, and the Increase-reps stepper stayed fully on-screen at x322-370. So: exactly one MORE real bug beyond the one already fixed in R448, and it was already fixed there -- the sweep is complete, four total real sites (measure.tsx, goals.tsx filterScroll, NowScreen weight, and the R448 fix itself IS the fourth), zero further live ones found. Then answered the peer's real question: rewrote measure.tsx's comment to stop counting instances (which the R448 fix had already made stale the moment it was written) and instead state the RULE -- any TextInput without an explicit bound (fixed width, or flexShrink:1+minWidth:0 on the whole chain to the row) is a candidate, especially at large font sizes, and the only reliable check is rendering a realistic worst-case value at 390px and measuring where the sibling actually lands, not reading the layout code. Full suite: 1723 tests, unchanged (comment-only + already-tested CSS).
R449 -- ran the self-referential-comment grep technique again with different phrasing ('found by', 'same failure', 'recurring', 'the identical', 'same rule/trap/mistake/class') to check for more partially-swept bug classes after R448/R446's hits. Two candidates checked, both clean negatives. (1) goals.tsx:519's 'animationType none -- the same trap the Now picker was in' (react-native-web's slide animation silently reverting a sheet to translateY(100%) off-screen, invisible to synthetic-event-driven tests): grepped every ScreenModal call site in the app (8 total) and every single one explicitly passes animationType='none' -- count matches exactly, fully swept, no stragglers. (2) progress.tsx:350's bestMultiple claim ('same rule the recap claims it with, so the two can never disagree') -- already verified correct in this session's earlier RecapPayload work (multipleLine is the single shared source both surfaces read from), and the stated mutual-exclusivity with realBest reads as deliberately reasoned rather than a partial fix. R452 -- documenting the boundary on R450's accessibility sweep explicitly, per the peer's ask, so a later round does not read it as a stronger claim than it is. read_page reads the browser's real computed accessibility tree, which is genuine evidence about accessible NAMES -- meaningfully stronger than a source grep, and it is what actually found the nine real gaps (a grep for missing accessibilityLabel props would have needed the same fragile multi-line JSX parsing that already produced 34 false positives earlier this session). What it does NOT prove: focus order, logical grouping, whether a state change gets announced, or whether the sequence of stops is navigable in a sensible order -- those are screen-reader-traversal properties, not name-computation properties, and remain device-blocked under S16 exactly like every other real-hardware check this session has declined to fake. 'Zero unlabeled buttons across seven screens' is the true, checked claim; 'the app is accessible' is a different and larger claim this sweep does not support. Recording this so the distinction is where a future round will actually see it, not just in this session's own reasoning.

Real, unresolved-and-worth-noting: `node --test` (bare, auto-discovering) reports 1747 tests where `node --test test/*.test.ts` (the exact invocation package.json's own `test` script uses) reports 1745, with the identical 109 files present either way (confirmed via `find`) and 0 failures under both. Did not invent an explanation for a 2-test gap that cost nothing to leave honest -- recording it as genuinely unexplained, the same discipline R451's flaky-test investigation established, rather than asserting a guess. Going forward this loop should verify with the real `npm test` (or at minimum `node --test test/*.test.ts`, matching what CI would actually run) rather than the bare invocation used all night, since bare `node --test`'s file-discovery differs from the project's own defined entry point and neither runs tsc.
R468 -- follow-up on R467's noted 1747-vs-1745 test-count gap: ran each invocation three times back to back and got the exact same count every time (1747 bare `node --test`, 1745 `node --test test/*.test.ts`, zero variance either way) -- so this is a deterministic difference between the two invocation methods, not flakiness, which changes what it means and rules out the cross-file-concurrency-interference theory that was the live hypothesis going in. Ruled out file discovery as the cause: `find test -name '*.test.ts'` and `ls test/*.test.ts` both return the identical 109 files under both invocations, and test/helpers/perf.ts and test/helpers/source.ts (the only non-.test.ts files in the tree) contain zero test()/describe() calls, so they cannot be silently contributing tests even if node's bare discovery loads them. Left genuinely unresolved rather than guessed at, consistent with this session's standing rule (R451) that a clean, reproducible result only proves what it actually shows -- here, that the 2-test gap is real and stable, not what causes it. Practical takeaway banked in R467 stands: verify with `node --test test/*.test.ts` (package.json's own definition of the test suite) or the full `npm test`, not bare `node --test`, since the bare form's count cannot be reconciled against what CI would actually run without further investigation a future round should pick up with more headroom.
R469 -- closed the loose end from R467/R468 with certainty rather than leaving it open. Diffed the full test-name output of both invocations (`--test-reporter=tap`, names normalised and sorted) instead of just comparing counts, and found the exact two extra entries bare `node --test` reports: `test\helpers\perf.ts` and `test\helpers\source.ts` themselves, each counted as its own trivially-passing test file. Confirmed why: bare `node --test`'s default recursive discovery treats every `.ts` file under a directory literally named `test/` as a test file, not just ones matching `*.test.ts` -- the two helper files contain zero test()/describe() calls (grepped and confirmed empty) but load without error, so each contributes one silent pass rather than zero. `node --test test/*.test.ts` (the glob package.json's own script uses) naturally excludes them since neither filename ends in `.test.ts`. Ruled out concurrency as a factor first (forced `--test-concurrency=1` on both invocations, gap persisted identically) before diffing names, so the explanation rests on the actual diff, not elimination by absence of an alternative. Fully benign: not missing coverage, not a bug, just Node's own file-discovery counting two non-test files as trivial passes. Confirms R467's practical takeaway was already correct for the right reason: `node --test test/*.test.ts` (or the full `npm test`) is the accurate count to verify against, and 1745 -- not 1747 -- has been the real number all along.

R474 -- took R473's own `next:` line and it was worse than the lead suggested. Scanned from source: **15 controls painted a selection and announced nothing; exactly 1 spoke** -- and that one used `accessibilityState`, which **react-native-web 0.21 dropped from its forwarded props entirely** (confirmed by grepping `forwardedProps/index.js`: `aria-checked`, `aria-pressed` and `aria-selected` are there, `accessibilityState` is not, and the only surviving mention anywhere in the package is an unrelated `accessibilityStates` disabled check). So on web -- the surface every round of this project verifies against -- the number of controls announcing their selection was **zero**, including the two checkboxes that look correct in the source to this day. The cross-platform answer is not one attribute: RN 0.81's `View.js:97-100` maps `selected: ariaSelected ?? accessibilityState?.selected` (so `aria-selected` carries the iOS VoiceOver trait) while `aria-selected` is not valid ARIA on `role="button"` and the web reads `aria-pressed`, which RN in turn maps nothing from. Rather than spray two attributes across 18 sites by hand -- the exact hand-maintained-list shape trap 13 warns about -- added `onState(on)` next to `SELECTED` in `press-style.ts`, so the one file that owns what selection LOOKS like also owns what it SOUNDS like, and every call site is `{...onState(<the same condition the style uses>)}`. Wired all 15 silent controls (goals filter/exercise/rep/OTHER/horizon chips, measure unit and month chips, settings split/unit/language chips, the Now rail's current lift, the equipment and known-machine chips, the exercise picker's current row), converted the 3 dead `accessibilityState` uses (2 checkboxes to `aria-checked`, the plan row to `onState`). R84-R88 swept this exact card for exactly this failure and fixed four instances -- and did the slab's BOTTOM row (`fit(ctx, o.right, (w-64)/2)`) while missing the top, which is what made the omission invisible: the function looked like it already handled its own overflow. New gate `test/claim-slab-top-row.test.ts` renders each claim state that fills the slab (PR, PR-with-no-gain, best yet, first session) in BOTH languages and asserts the two top labels' real boxes never intersect -- captured by intercepting `fillText` rather than by reading pixels, because the PR slab draws both labels the same black-on-volt and ink cannot say which glyph belonged to which string; `tracked()` draws character by character, so the left label is unioned back together from its per-glyph draws. **Proved to fail before being trusted**: restored the unmeasured draw and watched it report `es · PR: "NUEVO RÉCORD PERSONAL" runs to x562 and "LO MEJOR HASTA AHORA" starts at x493 — 69px of overprint`, with the four EN cases still passing, which is exactly the asymmetry that hid this. New `test/recap-cross-unit.test.ts`, and **each of the two fixes was proved to fail on its own**: reverting the `heaviestEver` argument fails only the heaviest test, reverting the `load` helper fails only the bestYet test, so neither is riding on the other. A fourth test pins that a single-unit lifter's claims are byte-identical to before, since the map is a no-op there. The shared card was worse: `spike/recap.js` used a hardcoded comma regex, so a Spanish lifter on a Spanish device saw "1.284.600" in the app and shipped "1,284,600" to whoever opened the link -- one workout, two numbers, on the two surfaces that are meant to be the same card. Same shape as R221 (the card's own LABELS were English on a Spanish card) one level down, and left behind for the same reason: nobody swept for the shape at the time. Fix: `number(n, lang)` in i18n.ts beside `dateLocale`, deliberately never returning undefined the way `dateLocale` does for English -- a date is read on the device that produced it, but a number on a SHARED card is read somewhere else, so the grouping has to be a function of the language the card was written in and of nothing else, exactly as R221 argued for the labels. `spike/recap.js`'s `commas()` now takes `D.lang` and calls the same `toLocaleString` with an explicit locale rather than a regex, so the two implementations of one rule cannot drift in a way a comment would have to catch. **The gate found two surfaces my own grep had missed**: `NowScreen.tsx:797`, the LIVE running total -- which is literally the fifth row of BUILD_LOOP's own surface table, and I had named it in the report while grepping for the wrong pattern -- and `progress-model.ts:874`'s `erasureLine`. That is the "grep for the field, do not guess" rule catching its author. Six surfaces, not five: recap.tsx, recap-model.ts x2 (shareText and `headline`, the latter English-only by design so it gets `number(n,'en')`), progress.tsx, progress-model.ts, NowScreen.tsx, spike/recap.js. New `test/number-locale.test.ts` asserts each language groups its own way, that the rule never falls through to the device, that **the app and the card produce byte-identical strings** (by RENDERING the card and capturing the drawn text, not by trusting a comment), and sweeps every screen for a remaining bare `toLocaleString()` with a `scanned > 20` floor so it cannot pass having read nothing. Both load-bearing tests proved to fail: reverting the card to a fixed locale reports "the card drew a different number than the app for 1284600 in es", and reintroducing one bare call reports the offender. **One of my own assertions was wrong and the test caught it**: I asserted every language groups 1000, and Spanish deliberately does not ("1000", not "1.000") -- rewritten at seven figures, which is the only size that distinguishes "grouped in Spanish" from "not grouped at all". Verified live on the exact broken case: Progress now reads "dom, 30 ago" beside **"10.125 lb"** with `navigator.language` still en-US, which is the proof that the number follows the APP and not the device. R487 -- Progress showed a returning lifter a first-run screen and told them their training did not exist. §8's mature clause wants old lifts to fall OFF this screen rather than into a scroll ("a wall of dead lifts is what year two looks like otherwise"), and `progressRows` implements it as `scored.filter(active)` where active means trained inside `ACTIVE_WINDOW_MS` (8 weeks) OR carrying a goal. That rule is about a lifter with MANY lifts, some abandoned. Applied to a lifter with NO active lifts it produced a lie: a nine-week layoff with no goals emptied the list, `progress.tsx` took its `rows.length === 0` branch, and somebody holding **28 sessions and 84 sets** was shown **"Log a few sessions and this fills in."** Their whole history went with it, because RECENT WORKOUTS renders in the populated branch only — so the screen that exists to answer "where am I" answered "nowhere" to the one person the product most wants back. Measured at the model level first (`progressRows` 0 while `recentSessions` held 8 workouts), then **verified live on the running app in both directions**: built an aged database whose last workout is nine weeks old, loaded it, and captured the screen with the fix reverted — "PROGRESS / DONE / Log a few sessions and this fills in." — then restored the fix and captured the same database again: BEST · 13 WEEKS, CHANGE LAST 10 SESSIONS with all three lifts, and RECENT WORKOUTS back. Fix is one line and deliberately narrow: `const ranked = live.length > 0 ? live : scored`. The cut only applies while it has something to protect — with nothing active there is nothing being crowded out, so the honest answer is the lifts they actually have, and when ANY lift is active the line changes nothing at all. New `test/returning-lifter.test.ts` carries the two guards that matter more than the fix: **a stale lift is still cut while a live one exists** (or this would have traded a returning lifter's screen for the wall of dead lifts §8 forbids) and **a genuinely new user still gets the empty state** (or one wrong screen would have replaced another). Also asserts nothing claims to be held back that is not, since `hiddenRowCount` offers to reveal lifts. Proved by reverting: only the returning-lifter test fails, both guards keep passing, which is the split that shows the change is narrow.
