R552 — PICK (logged first): the SHARE surface. Shortlist was (a) the share-URL
payload, (b) the recap screen's message ladder, (c) the Goals screen. Picked
(a)+(b) as one target because R540 found the session's only real defect there
and there has been no systematic pass since. §5 says the message is the half
that actually travels, and the share link is the one artefact that leaves the
device and is read by people with no app — so anything wrong in it is wrong in
public and cannot be corrected later. Contract to check: what the CARD claims
and what the MESSAGE claims must agree, and both must survive the round trip
through the URL.

R552 — BUILD/REVIEW/SHIP on the pick logged above. Three surfaces decide what a
workout gets CALLED — the recap screen, the share message, and the card image a
stranger opens — and each carries its own copy of the same priority ladder, in
TSX, TS and plain JS. The repo has THREE gates asserting every payload field is
MENTIONED in each, and mentioned is not agreed: R435's defect was a field
mentioned everywhere, where the sender's card read "+10 LB" and the card their
friend opened read "BEST YET" for the same workout, and R540's was `bestYet`
firing on a claim `findPRs` had already refused. R290 looked at testing the
ladder and declined, because it "does not reduce to a flat list of names without
restructuring RecapPayload" — TRUE OF THE SOURCE, and it does not have to be
tested from the source. Render the card, generate the message, and ask each what
it called the workout. Eight tests over seven payload shapes, including the
three precedence cases where two claims are true at once and only one is right,
and the last one renders from `unpack(pack(x))` through the DEPLOYED decoder,
because the card a stranger opens is built from the link and R435 escaped
exactly there. All three ladders agree today. MY INSTRUMENT WAS BLIND TWICE IN
ONE ROUND and both times it reported product defects that do not exist. First it
read the card's drawn text joined with a separator — the card draws tracked
headings ONE CHARACTER PER `fillText`, so "NEW PERSONAL RECORD" arrived as
"N | E | W | ..." and five workouts were reported as claiming nothing. Then,
with that fixed, it judged the MESSAGE with the CARD's vocabulary: the two
deliberately differ, the card printing the label NEW PERSONAL RECORD and the
message writing "heaviest ever, up from 200", and forcing them to share phrasing
would be a worse product for the sake of an easier test. What has to agree is
the claim, not the wording, so each surface is now read in its own. REVIEW: suite
2040 pass / 0 fail (real count, up 8). Three plants, each a disagreement that
has actually happened or nearly did — disable the card's bestYet branch (R435's
literal shape), reorder the message's ladder so bestYet outranks firstSession,
and drop the field in the decoder so it survives packing but not unpacking. Each
fails by name; the third fails ONLY the round-trip test, which is what earns
that test its place. Verified in the PRODUCT by finishing a real workout and
reading the recap. SHIP: `--check` current, `link/build.cjs` dist/ ready, all
three planted files restored and `git status` clean on them, app reseeded. |
next: the share surface now has claim-level coverage; what it still lacks is the
Spanish half — `CARD_WORDS` carries the es labels but no case exercises them,
and §16 wants both languages saying the same thing. That is a contained next
round. Tab bar remains the top item and the owner's; R548's strength-vs-size
question is filed beside it. Also owner-only: the R508 bundle scope (~48 kB) and
the two R483 items.

R553 — PICK (logged first): the Spanish half of the share surface. Shortlist was
(a) the es claim cases R552 left unexercised, (b) the Goals screen, (c) the
first-run/cold-start path. Picked (a): R552 built claim-level agreement between
card and message and tested it in English only, and its own `CARD_WORDS` already
carries the Spanish labels with nothing driving them — a vocabulary list nobody
exercises is the blind instrument this session keeps finding, one step from

card is the artefact that leaves the device, so a Spanish sender's card is read
by people who will never see the app.

R553 — BUILD/REVIEW/SHIP on the pick logged above. Drove R552's whole claim
matrix through BOTH languages: fourteen cases plus the round trip, and all three
ladders agree in Spanish as well. Checked the Spanish message wording first
rather than assuming — "lo más pesado hasta ahora" for a record, "la mejor serie
hasta ahora" for a best, "SESIÓN UNO, la marca a batir" for a first workout —
and chased one thing that looked wrong and was not: the shared volume reads
"5960 lb" in Spanish against "5,960" in English, which is `toLocaleString('es')`
doing correct Spanish typography (no separator below five digits), and
`shareText` was already using the locale formatter. THE INSTRUMENT WAS BLIND A
THIRD TIME, in the same file, and this one is the sharpest of the three. My card
vocabulary was hand-copied and I had copied only the English labels, so `SESIÓN
UNO` read as no claim and two CORRECT workouts were reported broken — a
hand-kept copy of another file's strings, in the test whose entire job is
catching drift between copies. Fixed by deriving the vocabulary from the
renderer's own `LABELS` (HANDOFF #13), which cannot fall behind the thing it
describes. That immediately produced a FOURTH blindness, and it is worth
recording exactly: the parse regex lost its backslash (`\s` became `s`,
trap 7 again), `labelsFor` returned nothing, and `anyOf([])` built `new
RegExp('')` — WHICH MATCHES EVERY STRING — so every card in every language
claimed a personal record. An empty vocabulary does not fail safe: it does not
read as "no claim", it reads as the FIRST claim, everywhere. `anyOf` now throws
on an empty list, and the escape is built with `String.raw`. REVIEW: suite 2049
pass / 0 fail (real count, up 9). Two plants: blank the Spanish first-session
labels and one case fails while English stays green, proving the es half is
really being exercised; break the parse and the run stops with "no labels: the
parse found nothing to match" instead of passing. Verified in the PRODUCT by
switching the app to Spanish and finishing a real workout — "DÍA DE EMPUJE /
VOLUMEN TOTAL / SERIES / RACHA 13 SEM / COMPARTIR" — then switching back and
reseeding. SHIP: `--check` current, `link/build.cjs` dist/ ready, `spike/recap.js`
restored and clean, app back in English on seed.b64. | next: four blind
instruments in three rounds is itself the finding — three of them were a
hand-copy of something another file owns, and one was an empty pattern that
fails OPEN. Worth a round adding the second of those to HANDOFF as a trap in its
own right, since "an empty matcher matches everything" is not obvious and cost
this round twice. Tab bar remains the top item and the owner's; R548's
strength-vs-size question is filed beside it. Also owner-only: the R508 bundle
scope (~48 kB) and the two R483 items.

R554 — PICK (logged first): the fail-OPEN matcher, as a HANDOFF trap and as a
gate. Shortlist was (a) that, (b) the Goals screen, (c) first-run/cold-start.
Picked (a) because it is the only item on the list with evidence behind it from
this session rather than a hunch: four blind instruments in three rounds, and
the two most expensive were the same mechanism — a matcher built from an empty
list, which does not fail safe. `new RegExp('')` matches every string and
`[].join('|')` is '', so a vocabulary that failed to parse reads as the FIRST
claim on every input rather than as no claim. That is not obvious, it cost R553
twice, and nothing in the repo says it. Contract: HANDOFF carries the trap with
the measurement, and a gate finds any OTHER place building a pattern from a list
that could be empty.

R554 — BUILD/REVIEW/SHIP on the pick logged above. This round is written from a
defect I CAUSED rather than found, which is the only reason it is worth a round:
four blind instruments in three rounds, and the two most expensive were one
mechanism. `[].join('|')` is the empty string, `new RegExp('')` matches every
string, and the direction is what makes it invisible — an empty pattern does NOT
read as "no match", it reads as THE FIRST BRANCH, on every input. In R553 that
turned a failed parse into every card in both languages claiming a personal
record. Trap 16 now records it with the measurement, together with its quieter
sibling: `for (const x of derived) assert...` over an empty population is a test
that passes without running a single assertion. The defence is one line in both
cases — make the empty case throw or fail, never continue. AUDITED THE REST OF
THE REPO AND IT IS CLEAN, for a reason rather than by luck: `field-scan.cjs` and
`orphan-scan.cjs` interpolate names captured by `([a-zA-Z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)`,
which cannot match empty, and every derived-population loop in the suite asserts
its population first — `bundle-verify-is-derived` with a `deepEqual` on the
calls, `no-control-bytes` with "there are source files to scan at all". So the
gate is a rule for the one shape that has actually gone wrong, not a sweep.
AND THE GATE WAS BLIND ON ITS FIRST RUN, which is the fifth time this session
and the fastest it has ever been caught. Its pattern used `[^)]*`, which cannot
cross the `)` in `labels.map(quote).join('|')` — the exact line it exists to
find — so it reported zero offenders, which is a pass. The "rule has something
to protect" test caught it on the first run, and that test is in the file
precisely because a rule with a zero population is indistinguishable from a rule
that does not work. Writing HANDOFF's entry hit trap 7 as well: the backslashes
in the sentence ABOUT collapsed escapes were themselves eaten, and the line was
repaired by index. REVIEW: suite 2052 pass / 0 fail (real count, up 3). Three
plants: remove the guard from the real instance (two tests fail), add a NEW
unguarded list-built pattern in another file (caught and named by file and
line), and soften trap 16's direction sentence in HANDOFF (the pin fails). SHIP:
`--check` current, `link/build.cjs` dist/ ready, `git status` clean apart from
the round's own files, app confirmed healthy. | next: the instrument-blindness
theme is now documented and gated, and this is the point to stop mining it —
five rounds of test infrastructure against one round of product is the wrong
ratio for an app whose owner asked for a less bland UI. The untouched product
surfaces are the Goals screen and the first-run path, and neither has had a pass
this session. Tab bar remains the top item and the owner's; R548's
strength-vs-size question is filed beside it. Also owner-only: the R508 bundle
scope (~48 kB) and the two R483 items.

R555 — PICK (logged first): the FIRST-RUN path, walked in the product. Shortlist
was (a) the Goals screen, (b) first run, (c) more test infrastructure — (c) is
ruled out by my own last entry, which is the point of writing the ratio down.
Picked (b) over (a) because it is the one screen every user sees and the one
nobody in this session has looked at: every measurement for eighteen rounds has
been taken against a SEEDED history, and OWNER.md's complaint was that the main
screen "looks a little sloppy and AI-generated" — a judgement about what a
person sees on opening the app, which on day one is a cold start with nothing in
it. Method: clear the database in the running app and walk it as a new user,
recording what is actually on screen rather than what the code says should be.

R555 — BUILD/REVIEW/SHIP on the pick logged above, and the round's best decision
was NOT to build the thing I found. Walked first run in the product with the
database cleared: split chooser, day chooser, first logged set, the SESSION ONE
recap ("SESSION ONE / 45 x 8 / BENCH PRESS — THE ONE TO BEAT", streak correctly
suppressed because one week is not a streak), then Progress and Goals on a
one-session history. All correct, and Progress prints "—" for a change it cannot
compute rather than inventing a trend, which is the §8 behaviour most apps get
wrong on day one. Noted but did not touch: while the split sheet is open the
whole weight control above it is dimmed and LOG SET is fully occluded — normal
modal behaviour, and a design judgement rather than a defect. THE ONE UNKEPT
PROMISE is stated in `coldstart.ts` itself: `source` exists "so the UI can tell
the user which it is — a seeded guess should not pretend to be their history",
and the app shows a confident 45 under "First time" and never says which.
`prefillSource` is computed on every render and read by no screen. I was two
minutes from writing the label when I checked the acknowledgement — R299 had
already weighed exactly this and left it, because "the Now hero is the most
crowding-sensitive surface in the app", with a Removes-when naming the owner.
So I measured the premise instead of repeating it, and it has CHANGED: on a
375x568 phone with a full twelve-week history the column now fits with ZERO
overflow, and that line uses 115px of a 335px column — nearly three times its
width still free. The constraint there is vertical and a one-line label adds no
height, and the label would only ever appear on day one or on a movement never
trained, which is the emptiest that screen ever is. So the first half of the
Removes-when is met on measurement and the second half is the owner's, and it is
filed in OWNER.md with the number attached — a filing without one is just an
opinion forwarded, which is what happened the first time. REVIEW: suite 2056
pass / 0 fail (real count, up 4). Two plants: drop the barbell floor and the
new-user test fails on the opening weight; delete the measurement from the
acknowledgement and the pin fails, so the reasoning cannot silently revert to
inherited. Product verified by walking it, viewport emulation reset to desktop
and the seeded app confirmed healthy afterwards. | next: the app's day-one path
is sound and its owner-facing questions are now three, all measured and all
waiting. Goals is the last screen with no pass this session. Tab bar remains the
top item; R548's strength-vs-size and R555's day-one label are filed beside it.
Also owner-only: the R508 bundle scope (~48 kB) and the two R483 items.

R556 — PICK (logged first): the GOALS screen, walked in the product. Shortlist
was (a) Goals, (b) the equipment/machine picker, (c) the Progress "YOU" screen.
Picked (a): it is the last surface with no pass this session, it is one of the
two links in the top row so every user can reach it in one tap, and it is where
§16's "every number checkable" is hardest — a goal is a claim about the future
and the screen has to say how far away it is without inventing progress. Method
as R555: walk it in the running app on a real history and read what is on
screen, rather than reading the model and assuming.

R556 — BUILD/REVIEW/SHIP on the pick logged above. Walked Goals in the product
on a real history and it is sound: one card, the target as the hero, a bar, "30
lb from a 225 squat", "60 days left · on pace". Checked the two things §16
actually demands rather than judging the look. The bar is 116px of a 289px track
and its own aria label says "40 percent there" — picture and words agree, and
the 40% resolves to a baseline of 175, which is their best when the goal was set
rather than a percentage of the target, so it measures progress they made rather
than distance from zero. And "on pace" turned out to be the most carefully
guarded claim on the screen: it returns null until there is real training to
judge, after being fixed twice for exactly the cry-wolf §8 forbids. THE GAP WAS
THE UNIT SEAM, which every other surface was checked against this session and
this one never. `goals.test.ts` has a kilogram goal, and its history is in
kilograms too, so nothing ever crossed — and crossing is the case that needs
`sessionUnits`, because a `LoggedSet` carries no unit and a goal carries its own
separate one. Built a kg-goal-on-lb-history seed and read the card: "12 kg from
a 100 squat", 89% on the bar. Correct — 195 lb is 88.45 kg, the gap is 11.55,
and the goal is stated in ITS unit throughout. Four tests pin that. THE PLANT IS
WHY THIS ROUND MATTERS. Removing the one conversion and reloading, the product
does not print a slightly wrong number: the screen reads "1 GOAL ACHIEVED",
congratulating a lifter who squats 195 lb for hitting 220.5. The whole card is
gone, replaced by a celebration. That is the §8 failure at its worst on the one
screen whose entire job is saying how far away something is, and it was one line
from happening with nothing watching. REVIEW: suite 2060 pass / 0 fail (real
count, up 4); all four tests fail on the plant. Verified in the PRODUCT both
ways with the bundle grepped, viewport reset to desktop, app reseeded. | next:
every screen has now had a pass, and the unit seam is closed on all of them.
Three owner questions are filed and measured. The honest next move is either the
equipment/machine picker (the last unwalked surface) or stopping the audit and
asking what the app still LACKS rather than what it gets wrong. Tab bar remains
the top item; R548's strength-vs-size and R555's day-one label are filed beside
it. Also owner-only: the R508 bundle scope (~48 kB) and the two R483 items.

R557 — PICK (logged first): the EQUIPMENT / MACHINE picker, the last unwalked
surface. Shortlist was (a) the picker, (b) stop auditing and ask what the app
LACKS, (c) the exercise picker/search. Picked (a) to FINISH the sweep rather
than abandon it one surface short — nineteen rounds of walking screens have
turned up six real defects including R556's, so the method is still paying, and
after this I can say the audit is complete instead of nearly complete. It is
also the surface with the most state per §4: equipment is remembered per

"don't ask which machine" is a preference that changes the flow. Contract to
check: what the app REMEMBERS matches what it SHOWS, and the machine name never
survives a change of equipment.

R557 — BUILD/REVIEW/SHIP on the pick logged above, and the round's result is a
change I BUILT AND THEN REMOVED. Walked the equipment picker: BARBELL /
DUMBBELL / MACHINE / BODYWEIGHT, the machine-name step, "Don't ask again". The
model layer is already thoroughly covered — a colon in the machine name, a blank
name, and switching kit away all have tests, and the pref really does round-trip
"machine:Hammer Strength: Iso Row" intact. What I found is a DECISION nothing
pins: the typed machine name commits on Return and on nothing else, so typing
"Arsenal" and tapping outside keeps the kit and silently drops the name. That is
the opposite of the rule the equipment beside it follows, quoted in
`setEquipment`'s own comment — "an answer given and then abandoned is an answer
thrown away" — and tapping outside is how a phone keyboard usually gets
dismissed. So I wrote the one-line fix, using `onApply`, which exists precisely
to record without closing the sheet. THEN I COULD NOT PROVE IT WORKED, and
chasing that is the round. The handler was in the bundle (grepped), focus
demonstrably moved (`activeElement` changed both ways), and nothing happened —
which reads exactly like "react-native-web drops onBlur", and trap 15 is a real
instance of that shape, so it is a believable and WRONG conclusion. Attached
listeners for `blur`, `focusout`, `focus` and `focusin` to the same element:
ZERO fired, `document.hasFocus()` false, `visibilityState` hidden, and fronting
the tab does not clear it because the pane is hidden by the window rather than
by the tab. The pane delivers no focus events at all. That is HANDOFF trap 17
now, with the numbers, and it is device-blocked territory — so the fix came back
out. An unverifiable change does not ship, and §12 says device-blocked checks
stay blocked and unfaked. The behaviour is filed for the owner instead, with the
evidence and the note that it needs a device check. AND THE SUITE CAUGHT MY
BLIND INSTRUMENT BEFORE I DID, which is a first this session: my new test sliced
source with a bare `indexOf`, the repo has a gate against exactly that, and it
failed on the full run. Switching to `around` then failed AGAIN, loudly, because
the first `onSubmitEditing=` in the file is the typed-weight field six hundred
lines away — which legitimately has an `onBlur`. Anchored on the placeholder,
which appears once. The bare form would have passed while reading the wrong
control. REVIEW: suite 2063 pass / 0 fail (real count, up 3). Three plants: add
a second commit path (the screen test fails and tells the next session to answer
the filing and verify on a device), truncate the pref at the separator (the
round-trip test fails), soften trap 17's number (the pin fails). Product
verified for what IS verifiable — the picker sets BARBELL and the chip follows —
and `git status` on `app/src` is empty, so the removed fix is byte-for-byte
gone. SHIP: `--check` current, `link/build.cjs` dist/ ready, app reseeded. |
next: every surface is now walked and the audit is genuinely complete, which was
the point of doing this one rather than abandoning it a screen short. Four
owner questions are filed, all measured. The honest next move is what the app
LACKS rather than what it gets wrong — and that is mostly owner territory, so
the first job is proposing options rather than building one. Tab bar remains the
top item.

R558 — PICK (logged first): the RECAP screen's own claim ladder, the one copy of
it R552 could not reach. Shortlist was (a) that, (b) propose "what the app
lacks" options for the owner, (c) the exercise search/add path. Ruled out (b) as
a BUILD target — it is owner territory and I already have four questions waiting,
so adding a fifth unanswered one is not work, it is queueing. Picked (a) because
R552 proved the card and the message agree and explicitly could NOT include the
third surface: recap.tsx is JSX, so its ladder was checked by reading, not by
running. R435's defect was two surfaces disagreeing, and the third one is the
one a lifter actually looks at before deciding whether to share. Contract: the
screen's slab must make the same claim as the card and the message, on the same
payloads, and be checked by rendering rather than by reading.

R558 — BUILD/REVIEW/SHIP on the pick logged above. R552 proved the shared CARD
and the share MESSAGE make the same claim, and said outright that it could not
include the third surface: `recap.tsx` is JSX, the suite has no test renderer,
and §12 forbids adding a dependency to get one. So two surfaces were EXECUTED
and one was DESCRIBED — and the described one is the screen a lifter actually
looks at before deciding whether to share. Closed it without a renderer and
without a dependency: the slab guards are pure predicates over the payload, so
the real expressions are lifted out of the file and evaluated. That distinction
is the round. A test that MATCHES a guard's text passes on any edit keeping the
words; this one runs whatever the file now says, so editing a guard edits what
the test executes. Seven payloads through all three surfaces in both languages,
plus the precedence cases where two claims are true and one is right. THE PLANT
PROVES THE DIFFERENCE: reorder the screen's ladder so `bestYet` outranks
`firstSession` — leaving the card and the message untouched — and two cases fail
naming the SCREEN, in English and Spanish. That is R435's defect shape (two
surfaces disagreeing about one workout) on the one surface that had no runnable
check. A second plant removes `payload.best` from the `bestYet` guard, which
would draw a slab that reads a lift name off undefined on the screen shown after
every workout, and the data-guard test catches it. Also pinned the instrument
itself: a missing guard THROWS rather than yielding a predicate that answers
false for everything, which is trap 16 applied to an extraction rather than a
matcher. REVIEW: suite 2072 pass / 0 fail (real count, up 9). Product verified
by finishing a real workout and reading the recap; `git status` clean on
`app/app` and `app/src`, so both planted edits to `recap.tsx` are gone; app
reseeded. | next: all three claim surfaces now agree by execution rather than by
reading, and every screen has been walked. What remains is genuinely owner
territory — four questions are filed and measured, and the tab bar has been the
top item since R523. The useful next rounds are the kind R551 and R554 were:
turning things this session learned the hard way into rules that hold, rather
than hunting defects that increasingly are not there.

R559 — PICK (logged first): a gate against the FIXTURE defect that cost me most
this session — a set logged with an `at` EARLIER than its own session's
startedAt. Shortlist was (a) that, (b) a rule for "verify the plant applied AND
fired" (already trap 10), (c) more product hunting (three rounds running found
no defects, so the returns are gone). Picked (a) on evidence: it burned a large
part of R540, where my seed logged sets two minutes before `startSession`
stamped the session, so today's own sets satisfied `x.at < session.startedAt`,
became their own prior best, and the screen showed NOTHING — which reads exactly
like "the fix works" when the fix is not even under test. A fixture can be wrong
in the direction that looks like success, and nothing in the repo says so.
Contract: find every seed and fixture that builds a session then logs sets into
it, and fail any whose set times precede the session start.

R559 — BUILD/REVIEW/SHIP on the pick logged above, and the checker found SIX
broken fixtures the moment it existed — all six written by me, this session.
`Repo.startSession` stamps `started_at` from its own clock, correctly, for an
app that only ever starts a session in the present. A seed that builds HISTORY
with a fixed clock therefore gives every past session a start time of today, and
the app's rule for history (`x.at < session.startedAt`) then reads that
session's own sets as its prior best. `seed-web.ts` already knew this — R37,
documented at length in its own comment: wrong date labels and every workout
"1 MIN" because `endedAt - startedAt` goes negative and clamps. My six seeds
reintroduced it one at a time and nothing said so. THE POINT IS THE DIRECTION OF
THE FAILURE. R540 lost half a round here: the seed logged its sets two minutes
before the session holding them, so the card correctly claimed nothing and the
screen looked exactly like the fix working — while the planted defect was never
under test. A fixture that renders an empty screen is obviously broken; one that
renders a PLAUSIBLE screen quietly answers a different question. Fix is
`assertSaneTimes`, called by every seed immediately before it writes, so the
fixture proves itself rather than being trusted. It throws rather than warns,
because a warning in a tool nobody watches is trap 16 in another costume — the
run still succeeds and the bad file still ships. Verified in the PRODUCT both
ways: with the seeds fixed, Progress reads "Sun, Sep 6 / Thu, Sep 3 / Mon, Aug
31 / Fri, Aug 28"; regenerating one seed the old way and reloading, every single
workout reads "Tue, Sep 8". Same screen, same data, four different days
collapsed into one. REVIEW: suite 2077 pass / 0 fail (real count, up 5). Three
plants: a new seed that forgets the check (caught by name, and the scan is
derived from the directory so tomorrow's seed is covered without anybody
remembering), a seed that checks AFTER writing (caught — order matters, since
checking late still ships the file), and downgrading the checker to a
`console.warn` (three tests fail). SHIP: `--check` current, `link/build.cjs`
dist/ ready, all seeds regenerated, app reseeded and confirmed. | next: this is
the third round in a row whose value was a rule rather than a fix, and the
fixtures were the last piece of instrument this session had proved unreliable.
Everything now measured is measured with something that has been shown to fail
when it should. The remaining work is genuinely the owner's four questions.

R560 — PICK (logged first): the RESTORE path, which is the one place a user can
destroy real data and the one surface I have deliberately never exercised.
Shortlist was (a) restore, (b) ERASE EVERYTHING, (c) stop. Picked (a) over (b)
because erase is a confirmed destructive action whose whole job is to delete,
while restore is the path where a MISTAKE looks like success: it reads a file
somebody else's app wrote, and a partial or silently-dropped import leaves a
lifter with a history that looks plausible and is missing things. R559 just
showed what a plausible-but-wrong dataset costs when nothing checks it. Method:
export the seeded history, damage the file in the ways a real file gets damaged,
and check the app reports rather than swallows. Nothing destructive runs against
the live app — every case goes through an in-memory Repo.

R560 — BUILD/REVIEW/SHIP on the pick logged above. Exercised RESTORE against
eight ways a real backup gets damaged — truncated mid-download, not JSON at all,
valid JSON of the wrong shape, an empty object, sets whose sessions are missing,
the same file restored twice, and a restore onto a phone that already has
DIFFERENT training on it. Every one is handled and reported honestly: damaged
files are REJECTED with a reason rather than half-imported, orphan sets are
skipped naming the missing session, a second restore adds nothing and says "3
skipped", and restoring onto a busy phone MERGES (3 sets to 6) rather than
replacing, with the sentence saying exactly what it added. Then I checked
coverage before writing anything and found 27 tests already pinning all of it —
so no test was written, because duplicating coverage to make a round look
productive is the opposite of the job. WHAT THE PROBE DID FIND is a blind spot
in the orphan-field scan. `report.skipped` carries a REASON for every skipped
row and only the COUNT reaches the user, so I went to check whether that had
been adjudicated like `prefillSource` was — and `RestoreReport` had never been
scanned at all. Adding it flagged THREE fields as dead, and all three were false
alarms: `summarise()` reads them and lives in `src/data`, which the scan did not
search. A whole production directory outside the instrument's field of view, and
the shape most likely to be affected by that was the one I was asking about. So
the search area and the population grew together (R543's rule: a gate that cries
wolf gets switched off), and with `src/data` searched the flags cleared honestly
rather than by exclusion. REVIEW: suite 2079 pass / 0 fail (real count, up 2).
Three plants: a new `RestoreReport` field nothing reads is caught by name;
dropping `src/data` from the search fails TWO tests including the scan's own
clean-run check; dropping `RestoreReport` from the shapes fails the population
test. Product verified — Progress shows EXPORT MY DATA / RESTORE with its
promise intact ("a plain JSON file, yours to keep, readable without this app").
Nothing destructive was run against the live app; every damage case went through
an in-memory Repo. SHIP: `--check` current, `link/build.cjs` dist/ ready, plants
reverted, `git status` clean on `app/src`. | next: the skip REASONS still reach
nobody — the count is honest but a lifter told "3 skipped" cannot learn their
backup is damaged. That is a product judgement against the owner's "if it needs
explaining, it's wrong", so it is a fifth filing rather than a fix, and I would
rather not add one before the four outstanding are answered. Tab bar remains the
top item.

R561 — PICK (logged first): ERASE EVERYTHING. Shortlist was (a) erase, (b) the
Settings screen end to end, (c) the skip-reasons filing. Picked (a): R560 chose
restore over it and it is now the last unexercised path, it is the only
IRREVERSIBLE action in the app, and §11 makes the export file the only backup —
so the sentence a user reads before tapping it is load-bearing in a way no other
copy is. Two things to check and both are checkable: the sentence must name
everything that will actually go, and the erase must leave nothing behind that
would make the app look like it still has data. Everything runs against an
in-memory Repo; nothing destructive touches the live app.

R561 — BUILD/REVIEW/SHIP on the pick logged above. Exercised ERASE EVERYTHING
against a device holding one of every erasable thing. It is correct: the
sentence names all six categories including the two R446 added, and afterwards
sets, sessions, goals, measurements, measure-goals, custom exercises and prefs
are all zero, the starting twelve are back, and the single surviving row is the
schema version — deliberately kept, and the only thing that should be. Also
caught my own probe lying: `repo.addCustomExercise?.()` does not exist on Repo,
so optional chaining silently skipped the one category R446 was ABOUT, and the
first run reported a clean erase of something that was never there. THE GAP IS
THE GUARD, NOT THE CODE. This defect has recurred twice — R480 (English
literals, so a Spanish lifter read "Se eliminará 700 workouts, 14,000 sets and 3
measurements") and R446 (four things named while a custom exercise and every
changed setting went silently, both verified live) — and the existing test
guards it by HAND-LISTING the six categories that exist today. That cannot catch
a third occurrence, because the failure mode IS a new thing being deleted
without being named. So the population now comes from `eraseAll`'s own SQL:
every table it empties must be spoken for by a counted category, with a reason
per row, and the two that are not one-to-one (measure-goals folded into
measurements, exercises counted only as CUSTOM because seedBuiltins puts the
twelve straight back) say why. Verified the difference rather than assuming it:
under a planted seventh table the existing test fails with "no such table:
notes" while the new one fails with "erase destroys these and the warning never
names them — the R446 defect, a third time: notes". One fails because SQLite
complained; the other explains the defect. REVIEW: suite 2083 pass / 0 fail
(real count, up 4). Second plant: make erase empty the whole `meta` table and it
is caught taking the schema version with it. Product verified by opening the
real confirmation on the seeded device — "36 workouts, 288 sets and 1 goal will
be deleted from this device. There is no backup but the one you export yourself,
and this cannot be undone" — with measurements, custom exercises and settings
correctly ABSENT rather than listed as zero, then CANCELLED. Nothing was erased;
the data is intact. SHIP: `--check` current, `link/build.cjs` dist/ ready, plants
reverted, `git status` clean on `app/src`. | next: every destructive and
data-losing path is now exercised and derived rather than listed. What is left
is the four owner questions and a fifth I am holding back deliberately.

R562 — PICK (logged first): the SETTINGS screen end to end. Shortlist was (a)
Settings, (b) the exercise search/add path, (c) the skip-reasons filing. Picked
(a): it is the last screen never walked in full, and it is where every
preference the app honours is set — so a control that stores something the app
does not read, or reads something it does not store, is invisible from every
other surface. R519 found exactly that shape once (a goal preference that was
stored and never acted on) and R555 found `prefillSource` computed and never
read; Settings is where the reverse would hide. Contract: every control on the
screen writes a pref the app actually consumes, and every pref the app consumes
that a user can change has a control.

R562 — BUILD/REVIEW/SHIP on the pick logged above, and walking Settings found a
REGRESSION I SHIPPED IN R550. Every control on the screen writes a pref the app
actually reads, and every pref the app reads that a user can change has a
control — the correspondence is clean in both directions, and the two jump
fields are populated (45 lb, 5 reps) rather than empty, which is §4's rule. Then
I asked what each control is actually WORTH, and the plate-jump field is not
honoured. R550 stopped the plate buttons stranding a lifter off the grid by
rounding EVERY result, and that silently overrode a jump the lifter had set
themselves: `jump.lb` at 7 moved them 5, `jump.kg` at 3 moved 2.5. Ask for
seven, get five, with nothing said. Before R550 it was exact, so this is two
rounds old and mine. It is invisible from Settings, which stores the number
correctly, and invisible from the Now screen, which just moves by the wrong
amount — the only way to see it is to set the value and count. THE TWO GOALS
ONLY LOOKED OPPOSED. A weight already on the grid plus the lifter's own jump is
exactly what they asked for and needs no correction; a weight OFF the grid is
the case R550 existed for — 189.5 from a converted kilo session, where +45 gave
234.5 and every press kept the half. Snapping only the second honours both, and
it is the same rule R518 and R549 each reached from another side: their own
evidence outranks the default. REVIEW: suite 2090 pass / 0 fail (real count, up
7). Planted in BOTH directions, because this fix sits between two failures:
restore R550's snap-everything and the four custom-jump tests fail by name;
remove the snap entirely and five tests fail across two files, including R550's
own. Verified in the PRODUCT: set the jump to 7 in Settings, and the Now screen
button reads "Add 7 lb" and moves 175 to 182 — not 180. State restored, seed
regenerated, button back to "Add 45 lb". SHIP: `--check` current,
`link/build.cjs` dist/ ready. | next: this is the second time a fix of mine
introduced a defect two rounds later (R548's grid work forced the Settings copy
change, R550's snap broke the custom jump), and both were caught by walking a
DIFFERENT surface than the one I changed. That is worth more than the fix: the
rule is to re-walk the screens a change can reach, not just the one it was aimed
at. Four owner questions remain, and the tab bar has been the top item since
R523.

R563 — PICK (logged first): re-walk the surfaces R548-R550's weight work can
REACH, not the ones it was aimed at. Shortlist was (a) that, (b) the exercise
search/add path, (c) the skip-reasons filing. Picked (a) on this session's own
evidence: two of my fixes each caused a defect two rounds later — R548's grid
work made Settings' copy false, R550's snap broke the custom plate jump — and
BOTH were found by walking a different screen than the one I changed, by
accident rather than by method. The grid change touched a constant that four
surfaces read. Contract: enumerate what consumes WEIGHT_STEP and the plate jump,
check each one still says something true, and turn the sweep into a gate so the
next weight change has to answer for its blast radius rather than be caught by
luck two rounds on.

R563 — BUILD/REVIEW/SHIP on the pick logged above. Re-walked what R548-R550's
weight work can REACH rather than what it was aimed at, and the first thing the
sweep found was a DUPLICATE `grid:` key in the coach call — my R548 edit ran
twice, so the option was passed twice with the same value, and the second
occurrence also pushed R541's comment away from the line it describes, leaving
the `base` explanation sitting above `grid`. Behaviour identical, which is
exactly why it survived two rounds and every test. Nothing detects a change that
changes nothing. THE PROMISE IS THE THING WORTH GATING. The plate button is
labelled with the jump and its accessible name says "Add 7 lb", and for two
rounds it moved 5 — §16 asks that every number be checkable, and a control that
states its own effect is the easiest number in the app to check, because the
user presses it and watches. So the gate pairs the LABEL with the MOVEMENT
across seven jump values in both units: what the button prints, what VoiceOver
reads, and what the weight actually does, asserted together. Plus the one case
where they deliberately differ — an off-grid start, where landing on plates
beats honouring the jump exactly — stated rather than left as an exception
somebody has to rediscover. REVIEW: suite 2099 pass / 0 fail (real count, up 9).
Two plants: restore R550's snap-everything and the button's own label is caught
lying in both units; reintroduce the duplicate key and the call-site check
names it. Product verified — the button promising 45 moves 175 to 220 and back,
and the Now screen renders correctly after the key fix. SHIP: `--check` current,
`link/build.cjs` dist/ ready. | next: three rounds have now each found a defect
in my OWN recent work (R559's six seeds, R562's regression, R563's duplicate),
and none was found by the surface I was changing. If there is a rule here it is
that a change should be checked from where it is CONSUMED, not from where it is
written. The four owner questions still stand, tab bar first since R523.

R564 — PICK (logged first): the exercise PICKER and the add-a-custom-exercise
path. Shortlist was (a) that, (b) a duplicate-object-key scanner off R563's
find, (c) the skip-reasons filing. Picked (a): it is the last user flow never
walked — equipment, goals, settings, progress, recap, first run, restore and
erase have all had a pass — and it is the one place a user TYPES something the
app then stores forever under a name of their choosing. R446 already showed
custom exercises interact with erase in a way nobody had noticed. Ruled out (b)
as too broad for its evidence: one duplicate key is not a class until it happens
twice, and R563 already gates the site it happened at. Contract: a name the user
types is either accepted and findable afterwards, or rejected with a reason —
never silently dropped, and never creating a second entry for a lift they
already have.

R564 — BUILD/REVIEW/SHIP on the pick logged above. Walked the exercise picker
and the add-a-custom-exercise path, the last user flow never exercised, and it
is SOUND — the third surface in a row where the honest result is "nothing
broken". Blank names refused; duplicates resolved rather than duplicated, across
case, hyphens AND runs of spaces, so "  Bench   Press  " finds the builtin; a
96-letter name accepted and ellipsized cleanly at 375px with no horizontal
overflow, which `now-layout.test.ts` already guards with the definite-width fix
that makes ellipsis possible at all. Wrote nothing for any of that, because
duplicating coverage to make a round look productive is the opposite of the job.
ONE PATH HAD NOTHING ON IT and it is the one where a failure would be silent. A
name made entirely of characters the slug drops — "---" — slugifies to the
empty string, so the id falls through to a generated one built from
`Date.now()`, and two added in the same millisecond share a stem. Everywhere
else in this flow a collision would error on the primary key; here it would
quietly MERGE two of a lifter's own movements, with every set logged against
either landing on one. The behaviour is right — `freeSlug` de-duplicates against
the ids already taken, so seven punctuation-only names really are seven lifts,
each keeping the text that was typed — and nothing said so. Also pinned that the
generated id survives being used as an id: selectable, and a set can be logged
against it, because an id that only half works fails later and somewhere else.
REVIEW: suite 2103 pass / 0 fail (real count, up 4). Two plants: make `freeSlug`
skip its de-duplication and seven movements collapse into two, caught by name;
drop the whitespace collapse and a second Bench Press appears. Product verified
by adding a 96-letter movement through the real picker and reading the hero at
mobile width, then reseeding — the custom lift is gone and the app is back on
the seeded history. SHIP: `--check` current, `link/build.cjs` dist/ ready. |
next: every flow in the app has now been walked. Three consecutive rounds found
no defect in the product and two found defects in MY recent work, which is the
clearest signal yet about where the risk actually is. Four owner questions
remain, tab bar first since R523.

R565 — PICK (logged first): SPEED on a big history. Shortlist was (a) render/model
cost at 200+ sessions, (b) Dynamic Type at large font scales, (c) the

exist precisely because things were being recomputed), and unlike the last three
rounds it is about the product rather than my instruments. Contract: measure the
model's work at a realistic and an extreme history, in numbers, and gate
whatever is worth keeping.

R566 — Stage 0: OWNER.md still four blocked decisions. Picked auditing whether
the dev-only seed fixtures in public/ actually belong there, after checking (and
clearing) whether R565's own new seed had a gap in R559's tracking gate — it did
not, that scan is directory-derived. FOUND SOMETHING WORSE THAN A GAP: seven
fixture files written by seeds from THIS SESSION — big565.b64 through
pr539.b64, 1.5MB total — were TRACKED AND COMMITTED, because `.gitignore` named
four seeds one at a time (seed.b64, stress.b64, tabbar.b64, mixed.b64) and
nobody connected "writing a new seed tool" to "add it to the ignore list" for
the seven added since. Confirmed this is not theoretical: ran a REAL `expo
export --platform web` and every fixture came out the other side inside
`dist/`, the actual production artifact. `.gitignore` was not failing to
prevent a future risk; it had already failed to prevent a real one, twenty-some
git commits deep. Fixed with a wildcard, `public/*.b64`, rather than an eighth
name — the failure mode WAS the list falling behind, and a pattern cannot.
`sql-wasm.wasm` stays out of it on purpose: it is a real web dependency, not a
fixture, and a broader pattern would have swallowed it too. REVIEW, done
properly rather than assumed: planted a force-added fixture back and both
tracking tests named it; widened the pattern to `public/*` and the wasm-safety
test caught it. MADE A REAL MISTAKE MID-ROUND AND CAUGHT IT MYSELF: the first
`git rm --cached` sweep + commit left `pr539.b64` still tracked, because an
earlier `git add -f` / `git restore --staged` cycle (done to prove the plant
above) had put it in a different index state than the other six, and I trusted
the sweep instead of re-checking after commit. The suite caught it — still red
post-commit — rather than me declaring victory on a green run I had not
actually looked at. Second commit fixed the one file. Full suite: 2110 tests,
one unrelated flake (R565's own timing test, warned-of noise under full-suite
load, clean alone) resolved by rerunning in isolation — not silenced, checked.
`--check` current; no share code moved so `link/build.cjs` was not needed;
verified the dev server still serves the fixtures from disk. Committed as
9423b14 then c4fb917 (git is on for this repo; both commits are inside
fitness-app, never the parent). | next: worth a look at whether ANY other
gitignore pattern in this repo is a hand-list rather than derived — this was
the second time a list fell behind (R543's raw-history consumers was the
first), and the fix pattern is the same both times: find what defines the
population and match on that instead of enumerating it. Four owner questions
remain, tab bar first since R523.

R567 — PICK (logged first): sweep for OTHER hand-kept lists in the repo's own
tooling that could fall behind the way .gitignore did (R566) and raw-history-
consumers did (R543) — both real, both found by luck rather than by looking.
Shortlist was (a) that sweep, (b) the skip-reasons filing, (c) stop and wait on

R567 — Stage 0: OWNER.md still four blocked decisions. Followed up on my own

the two obvious candidates first and both were clean: `orphan-scan.cjs`'s DIRS
already includes src/data (fixed independently in R483, before this session);
field-scan.cjs's `ACKNOWLEDGED` exceptions are legitimately hand-kept by design,
not a population that should be derived. THE REAL GAP WAS THE SCAN'S OWN
POPULATION. `field-scan.cjs` targets multi-field shapes a model computes and a

protection at all. Ran the scan cold before deciding it belonged — it came back
CLEAN, every field read, so this is coverage gained rather than a bug found,
which is the more common and less exciting outcome and still worth locking in
so it cannot quietly drop back out unnoticed. REVIEW: suite 2111 pass / 0 fail
(real count, up 1 net — one new population-pin test). Two plants: a genuinely
dead field on SessionSummary is caught by name ("SessionSummary.weekOfYear");
removing SessionSummary from the scan's population fails the new pin test by
name. Verified in the PRODUCT — Progress renders the fields SessionSummary
carries correctly (title, sets, volume, per-lift bests) on the real seeded
history. `--check` current; no share code moved so link/build.cjs was not
needed. Confirmed no plant residue survived into the diff. Committed as 41e6186
inside fitness-app. | next: the remaining 27 unscanned interfaces are mostly

WeeklyComparison and a few others are worth a second look with the same

R568 — PICK (logged first): surface restore's skip REASONS to the user, not just
the count. Shortlist was (a) that, (b) another interface added to field-scan.cjs
(GoalDraft/Suggestion/WeeklyComparison), (c) wait idle. Picked (a) — I flagged

R568 — Stage 0: OWNER.md still four blocked decisions. Shipped the skip-reasons
gap flagged in R560 and deliberately deferred three rounds rather than file a
fifth question behind four unanswered ones — small, contained, product-facing,
no overlap with anything pending. `report.skipped` has always carried a REASON
string per row and only the COUNT reached the user: "3 skipped" with no way to
learn whether that meant nothing or something real. The design question was
noise, not plumbing: naming every skip on a badly mismatched file could print
hundreds of near-identical reasons on a status line, which is the wall of detail
§15 keeps this screen quiet against. Split on the one distinction that actually
matters — "already on this device" is the ORDINARY case, restoring the same file
twice or one already partly merged, and stays silent; the moment even one skip
is something else, the first REAL reason is named, so a lone genuine problem
cannot get buried under a pile of harmless duplicates. Kept the reason string
itself untranslated on purpose, the same choice `applyBackup` already makes for
parse errors — it is meant to be pasted into a support message as-is, and
translating it would mean support has to translate it back. REVIEW: suite 2116
pass / 0 fail (real count, up 5; one unrelated flake in R565's own timing test
under full-suite load, confirmed clean alone, not silenced). Two plants: revert
to count-only and three tests fail on the missing reason; always name a reason
even on an all-duplicate restore and the quiet-on-duplicate tests fail, catching
noise in the OTHER direction. Verified in the PRODUCT, not just the harness: hit
the real RESTORE button on the seeded app with a genuinely damaged file dropped
through it (an orphan set naming a session not in the file), and the screen
printed "Restored 0 sets, 0 sessions. 1 skipped (session ghost not in file)."
Reloaded afterward and the real history was untouched. `--check` current; no
share code moved so link/build.cjs was not needed. Committed as 9383166 inside
fitness-app, diff confirmed free of plant residue. | next: that closes every
filed non-owner item from this session. What remains with real product value is
entirely the four owner decisions — tab bar first, waiting since R523.

R569 — Stage 0: OWNER.md still four blocked decisions. With every self-directed
item closed, checked whether Dynamic Type — a real, heavily-fixed surface (R339,

Thirty-nine hand-placed fixes with nothing confirming the set stays complete is

IDENTICAL fitted value the resting \`<Text>\` three lines below correctly exempts

Type this is the R339 defect exactly, in the sibling control the original fix
never reached, because the two elements were added at different times and
nobody re-checked the first one's reasoning against the second. Fixed with the

R571 — Stage 0: OWNER.md still four blocked decisions. Went to stabilise
R565's timing test, flaky under full-suite load for three rounds running, and
the investigation found the original test's own claim was WRONG, not just
noisy. Re-planting R494's "actual defect" as R565 described it — a loop
inside \`goalProgress\` — never once affected the "eight times the history"
test, because that fixture has zero goals and \`goalHint()\` returns before
\`goalProgress\` is ever called; the round-565 log's claim of a reliable catch
was itself noise misread as signal, the exact failure this session has spent
many rounds warning against, this time in my own earlier work. Traced the REAL
regression to the call site — \`this.setsFor(goal.exerciseId)\` reverted to
\`this.repo.allSets()\` — and measured it properly: isolated, a stable 1.46x
against a clean 1.31-1.36x, a real ~10% gap with no overlap across five
separate runs. Tried to gate that gap directly and it BACKFIRED: tightening
the threshold to sit inside the isolated-measurement gap (1.42) made the test
flake on CLEAN code under full-suite load, because the app's own MAX_GOALS
cap (100) means the signal cannot be amplified past what contention noise can
swamp. WIDENING WAS THE HONEST FIX, NOT MORE PRECISION. Reverted the goals
threshold to 3x (R565's original) and the eight-times threshold to 10x — both
now catch only order-of-magnitude regressions reliably, and BOTH SAY SO
in their own comments rather than implying a precision they cannot deliver
under load. The specific 1.4x regression gets a DIFFERENT kind of backstop: a
new source-level test asserting \`goalHint\` still calls \`this.setsFor\`, not
\`this.repo.allSets()\` — cheap, sub-2ms, and unaffected by contention because
it reads a file rather than a clock. Caught the exact regression on all three
plant attempts, instantly, every time. A third test ("re-rendering... nearly
free") also flaked once during ten full-suite verification runs and got the
same honest treatment — widened from 2x to 4x margin with the reasoning
stated. REVIEW: ten consecutive full-suite runs (2123 tests each) with zero
failures, after multiple rounds of failing 1-2 times per 3 runs before the
fix. Three separate plants of the real regression, each caught reliably by
the new source check. Verified in the PRODUCT: Now screen renders normally on
the seeded history. \`--check\` current; no share code moved so
\`link/build.cjs\` was not needed. Committed as 7d1ecb6 inside fitness-app;
diff on now-model.ts and goals.ts is EMPTY — every plant during this
investigation was fully reverted, only the test file changed. | next: the
honest lesson is bigger than this one file — a timing-based test run inside a
large parallel suite cannot reliably gate a regression under roughly 2x the
size of normal run-to-run noise, no matter how the samples are massaged
(median, sum, more iterations all tried and all failed under real
contention). Where that precision matters, the fix is a structural source
check, not a faster stopwatch. Four owner questions remain, tab bar first
since R523.

R573 — Stage 0: OWNER.md still four blocked decisions. Ran \`npm run typecheck\`
directly rather than through \`npm test\`'s grep-filtered output, and found TWO
real type errors that had shipped and sat unnoticed. FIRST: \`now-model.ts\`
read \`exercises.get(this.exerciseId)?.equipment\` — but \`Exercise\` has never
had an \`equipment\` field (it lives on \`LoggedSet\`, per SET, not per
exercise). The expression type-checked as \`any\` and silently evaluated to
\`undefined\` on every call since R541 shipped, so \`?? 'barbell'\` always won:
the deload floor was always 45/20 regardless of what the lift actually was.
MEASURED THE REAL CONSEQUENCE rather than just the type error: a lifter
grinding at 40 lb on a weighted (bodyweight) pull-up, reps falling, was told
"hold here" when the correct floor (0, not 45) allows a real deload to 35 —
§8's protection silently disabled for every equipment but barbell. Fixed by
reading \`this.equipment\`, the model's own tracked field for the CURRENT lift,
which R541 could have used from the start. SECOND: \`NowScreen.tsx\` had
\`allowFontScaling={false}\` TWICE on one TextInput — my own R569 fix, which
added the prop without checking whether one already existed a few lines below.
A JSX duplicate attribute, which tsc flags immediately and nothing else does.
THE ROOT CAUSE IS MINE, NOT THE CODE'S. \`npm test\` already chains
\`tsc --noEmit\` as its last step and has all session — but every \`npm test\`
run this session was piped through a grep for the test runner's own lines
("^✖ ", "^ℹ (tests|pass|fail)"), and tsc's error output has a completely
different shape that never matches that pattern. A clean "ℹ fail 0" from the
grep was read as "everything passed" when the grep could only ever speak for
the test runner, not for tsc running after it — the same blind-instrument
shape as R539's backspace, R554's empty matcher, R565's misattributed plant,
now in my own terminal habit rather than in a test file. Closed the gap the
only way that survives a repeated habit: moved \`tsc --noEmit\` INSIDE the
suite as its own test, so a type error now fails as an ordinary "✖ <name>"
line — exactly the shape every grep pattern used all session already catches
and shows. REVIEW: fixing the duplicate-attribute bug shifted three EXISTING
tests' anchor windows (R563's coach-call check, two of R569's own gate) past
comments that had grown around the fix — not silently broken, LOUDLY broken,
each with a clear reason once read, each widened with the real measured
distance rather than a guess. Found and fixed a THIRD, unrelated bug in R569's
own scan while widening it: its closing-\`>\` search treated an arrow
function's \`=>\` as a tag close, which the original narrow window had never
been wide enough to reach. Planted all three original defects (equipment
lookup, duplicate attribute, and separately re-confirmed each existing test)
and every one is caught by name. Suite: 2126 pass / 0 fail, exit code checked
EXPLICITLY this time (0), not inferred from grep output. Verified in the
PRODUCT: seeded a lifter grinding at 40 lb on a bodyweight-equipment pull-up,
set the equipment through the real picker, and the screen read "40 is
grinding — back off to 35" — the exact number the fix predicts. \`--check\`
current; no share code moved so link/build.cjs was not needed; probe fixture
removed, app reseeded and confirmed clean. Committed as 852762f inside
fitness-app. | next: worth checking whether \`npm run check-deps\`, the OTHER
step \`npm test\` chains, has the same theoretical blind spot — it has never

R575 — Stage 0: OWNER.md still four blocked decisions. Investigated
\`noUncheckedIndexedAccess\`, a real tsc safety flag not covered by base
\`strict\` — worth checking because R548/R549/R550/R562/R573 all involved bugs
in exactly the shape it targets: indexing into a Record or array without
proving the key exists. Enabled it and ran a real compile: 508 errors, 81 in
\`src/\`, 1 in \`app/\`, the rest in \`test/\` and \`tools/\`. Sampled several of the
production hits before judging them — \`coach.ts\`'s repeated "'latest' is
possibly undefined" is \`sets[0]\` after \`sets.length >= MIN_SESSIONS\` is
already checked a few lines up; \`repo.ts\`'s is \`MIGRATIONS[v]\` inside a
\`v < MIGRATIONS.length\` loop. Both are real invariants the code already
enforces, just not ones array indexing lets TypeScript prove — the dominant
shape across the sample, unlike R573's equipment bug, which this flag would
NOT have caught (that was a field that plain doesn't exist on the type,
already covered by \`strict\`'s ordinary property checking). This round's own
contract said keep it only if what it finds is real and fixable at reasonable
cost, and 508 errors — mostly provable-safe patterns needing a large mechanical
\`!\`-assertion or restructuring pass across dozens of files, for a very low
hit rate on ACTUAL bugs in the one sample checked — is neither. Reverted
\`tsconfig.json\` to the exact byte it was; confirmed with a diff and a second
compile at exit 0. REVIEW: suite 2126 pass / 0 fail, unchanged; \`git status\`
confirms nothing was left touched. No SHIP step — nothing shipped. | next:
this closes the natural follow-up to R573/R574's typechecking work. The
finding is worth keeping even though nothing changed: a future session should
not re-attempt this flag expecting a quick win, and if it ever IS worth doing,

R581 — Stage 0: OWNER.md still four blocked decisions. Checked the two Goals
candidates I did NOT check in R580 — \`undo: {goals, label} | null\` (a full
snapshot of removed goals, to put back) and \`chosen\`. \`undo\`'s write/read
path is \`removeGoals\` -> \`restoreGoals\`, and \`restoreGoals\` is a PLAIN
UPSERT with no memory of why a goal it is handed no longer exists — it cannot
tell "wiped a second ago, undo makes sense" from "the device was erased on
purpose a minute ago, undo must not." Measured directly: wipe a goal, call
\`eraseAll()\` — the one action in this app that explicitly promises "this
cannot be undone" — then feed the stale \`undo\` snapshot to \`restoreGoals\`
anyway. It comes back. THIS IS REAL BUT NOT CURRENTLY REACHABLE, and finding
out why mattered as much as finding the defect: the only way off Goals is
\`router.back()\`, a POP, and popping destroys the component's local state —
so \`undo\` cannot survive a trip to Progress today, because reaching Progress
requires leaving Goals first. What makes this worth fixing NOW rather than
filing: it is directly and specifically tied to the open tab-bar decision
sitting in OWNER.md — a tab bar keeps every tab mounted rather than popping,
which would make exactly this reachable, landing on nobody's radar because
the code has looked safe for as long as the stack navigation made it safe.
Fixed by giving Goals the same shape NowScreen already has: a
\`useFocusEffect\` that clears \`editing\`, \`wiping\` and \`undo\` on arrival,
independent of whatever navigation model exists later. REVIEW: suite 2133
pass / 0 fail (real count, up 4 — one documenting \`restoreGoals\`'s honest
behavior with a builtin exercise so the test isolates the goal-row question
from a separate "the exercise itself is gone" question, and one pinning the
screen-level guard). Planted the fix's removal and the screen-level test
caught it by name; planted \`restoreGoals\` refusing everything and the
documentary test (plus three existing ones) caught that too, confirming it
tracks real behavior rather than a frozen assumption. Verified in the
PRODUCT: wiped the Squat goal on the real running app, confirmed "Squat goal
wiped. UNDO" appeared, popped back to Now, returned to Goals, and the undo
bar was GONE — "GOALS / DONE / Pick the lifts you want to move... / + ADD A
GOAL," no trace of the wipe. \`--check\` current; no share code moved so
link/build.cjs was not needed; app reseeded and confirmed clean. Committed as
a07b6bb inside fitness-app. | next: this closes the Goals side of R580's

document two real historical bugs (the position-decay mismatch and the
12-wide overflow pool re-sorting across different training days) with
measured day-counts for how bad each one got, and both fixes are exactly
right against their own reasoning. `occurrences()`'s identity+length memo is
sound because `Repo.allSets()` genuinely freezes its array (confirmed by
reading repo.ts:390-395, not assumed) and the length check is documented as
covering only the in-place-mutation case identity alone would miss.
One theoretical gap, filed rather than fixed: `rankExercises`'s
`positionSum / positionWeight` divides by a sum of `0.5 ^ (daysAgo/28)` terms,
which underflows to exactly 0.0 in IEEE double only past roughly 30,000 days
(~82 years) of daysAgo -- past that this produces NaN and would silently
corrupt sort order rather than crash. Confirmed the arithmetic by hand rather
than asserting it; not fixed, because no real training history can be 82
years old and a defensive branch for an unreachable input is exactly the kind
of complexity §12's spirit argues against paying for nothing. Documented here
so a future round does not rediscover the same arithmetic from scratch and
mistake it for live.

floor anyway: 2139 pass / 0 fail, unchanged.

R594 - Stage 0: OWNER.md unchanged since R586. IDEATE: continued R592/R593's
tracing method onto a different invariant that has bitten this app twice
before by its own admission -- pr.ts's own docstring says "convert a set's
weight into `unit` BEFORE combining it with anything else" broke this exact
module in two separate, undetected ways once already (a ~220 lb history read
as 100, producing a false PR). Traced every caller of `realLoad` for the same
convert-before-combine discipline `loadOf` (pr.ts:69) already follows.
FINDING, reported honestly rather than as a fix: `findPRs` (pr.ts:279) calls
`realLoad(set, measurements, unit)` for the `realWeight` field WITHOUT first
converting `set.weight` into `unit` the way `loadOf` does two lines above it
for the exact same set -- structurally the identical shape as the bug the
module's own comment describes having already fixed once. Before reporting it
as live, checked whether it is actually REACHABLE: `findPRs` has exactly two
callers (now-model.ts:1063, recap-model.ts:88), and both pass `session.unit`
as `unit` while iterating `sessionSets` -- sets that belong to THAT session by
construction. So `sessionUnits.get(set.sessionId)` for every set this loop
ever sees is always `session.unit`, which is always `unit` -- the missing
conversion is a no-op in both real call paths today. Confirmed by reading the
call sites directly, not assumed from the shape alone; the same discipline
that ruled out a false contrast-audit result in R591 and a false orphan-scan
result in R588 applies again.
DECIDED NOT TO EDIT: the inconsistency is real (this one call site does not
follow the pattern the rest of the file uses and could silently break if a
future caller ever passed a `unit` other than the session's own), but with no
live defect to plant-and-catch against, a source change here would be
housekeeping dressed as a fix -- risk for a cosmetic-only gain, and this
segment's own history (R565-R571) is a caution against treating "looks more
consistent" as equivalent to "verified different behavior." Left a decision
for a future round if a caller ever needs `unit` != `session.unit` here:
convert first, the same one-line pattern `loadOf` already demonstrates.
REVIEW: no code changed; suite unaffected, 2142 pass / 0 fail, unchanged.
SHIP: nothing to rebuild.
| next: three rounds running the same "trace a stated invariant to its other
call sites" method (R592 real fix, R593 filed gap, R594 verified-safe) --
worth keeping in rotation, but this round's more useful lesson is the second
half: finding a structural inconsistency is not the same as finding a bug,
and the checking step (does this actually run with mismatched inputs, ever)
is where the difference gets decided. Five owner decisions still wait, tab

BUILD/REVIEW (a reading audit): the dedup logic is sound and already
documents its own hard case -- "Hack-Squat" and "Hack Squat" both slugify to
`hack_squat`, and `freeSlug` exists specifically so the second one gets a
suffixed id instead of silently renaming the first via an upsert collision,
with a name-based case-insensitive check ahead of that to avoid creating a
near-duplicate in the first place. Collision handling degrades sanely past 99
suffixes to a timestamp-based id.
One real, minor gap found and weighed rather than fixed: `slugify` strips
everything outside `[a-z0-9]`, so a name typed in a non-Latin script (e.g. a
Japanese or Cyrillic movement name) reduces to an empty base and falls back to
an anonymous `ex_<timestamp>` id. Not a functional bug -- the app displays and
searches by NAME everywhere, never by id, and ids stay unique either way, so
nothing breaks or misbehaves. It is a readability-of-internal-ids issue only
(a Latin name gets `bulgarian_split_squat`; a non-Latin one gets `ex_m1a2b3`),
invisible to the user and only ever seen by someone reading the database
directly. Not filed as an owner decision -- there is no product-visible
consequence to rule on -- and not fixed, since the plausible fix (transliterate
or hash the actual name into the slug) is cosmetic effort for zero observable
benefit, exactly the kind of unrequested complexity §12's spirit warns against.
Noted here rather than silently dropped, in case it ever becomes visible
through some future feature (data export, debugging tools) that surfaces ids.

R603 - Stage 0: OWNER.md unchanged since R586. IDEATE: continuing the
domain-function reading audit onto measure.ts's `formatMeasure`, the shared
imperial-height formatter used by three real surfaces (measure.tsx's reading
list, measure-goal.ts's target/gap text, measure-model.ts's trend lines) --
never independently checked this segment.
BUILD/REVIEW: found and confirmed a real, reproducible rounding-carry bug.
`formatMeasure` splits an inches value into feet and a remainder, THEN rounds
the remainder to a tenth -- and a remainder just under a whole foot rounds up
to 12 itself: `formatMeasure(71.96, 'in')` printed `5'12"`, which is not a
height anyone has, rather than the correct `6'0"`. Confirmed with a direct
call before touching anything. Fixed with a carry check right after the
split: `if (inches >= 12) { feet += 1; inches = 0; }`. Added
test/format-measure-inches-carry.test.ts (the carry case at two different
whole-foot boundaries, plus a no-regression case for ordinary remainders
including the exact `5'11.9"` boundary one tenth below the bug). Planted the
bug back (removed the carry-check line) and the carry test failed by name
while the no-regression test kept passing; restored via Edit, confirmed
clean.
REVIEW: suite 2144 -> 2146 pass / 0 fail (real count, up 2).
Verified live in the PRODUCT: opened /measure, recorded a height of 71.96 in
through the real Settings-style sheet (dispatched PointerEvents, since a bare
click does not register on react-native-web Pressables -- HANDOFF trap 4),
and the HEIGHT row showed `6'0"`, not `5'12"`. Reset the demo database back
to the stock seed afterward so the touched state does not linger.
SHIP: `build-domain.cjs --check` reports current (measure.ts is domain code,
already rebuilt by this round's own `npm test` runs); no separate rebuild
needed.
| next: a genuine, previously-unknown display bug, found by reading a small

R604 - Stage 0: OWNER.md unchanged since R586. IDEATE: re-checked R603's own
claim rather than moving to new ground -- the fix comment asserted
`measure-goal.ts`'s `remaining` was a second reachable path into the carry
bug, and that claim was never actually tested, only asserted by analogy.
BUILD/REVIEW: WRONG, caught by testing it. `remaining` computes through
`Math.round(x * 10) / 10` (same as `convertMeasure`) BEFORE formatMeasure
ever sees it, and walked every hundredth from 71.90 to 72.04 through that
exact rounding directly: every result lands cleanly on a `.9` or a `.0`,
never a `.96`-style fraction, because a value already snapped to a tenth
splits into a remainder at that same resolution. The bug is real and the fix
is right (R603's live repro used a raw, hand-typed 71.96, not a computed
gap), but the comment's SECOND claimed path does not exist. Corrected the
comment in measure.ts to state what was actually verified: the only real
route in is `app/measure.tsx`'s own decimal-pad height input, which does not
restrict entry to one decimal place, feeding a raw `Measurement.value`
straight to `formatMeasure` with no rounding pass in between.
REVIEW: comment-only change; suite unaffected, 2146 pass / 0 fail, unchanged.
SHIP: nothing to rebuild.

BUILD/REVIEW: clean, with one apparent gap ruled out by checking the actual
storage layer rather than the caller's argument names. `eraseAll` clears
prefs via `DELETE FROM meta WHERE key LIKE 'pref.%'`, and callers set jump
amounts through `setPref('jump.lb', ...)` -- which LOOKS like it would store
under a bare `jump.lb` key, missing the `pref.` prefix the DELETE matches on.
Checked `getPref`/`setPref`/`clearPref` directly: all three prepend `pref.`
internally before touching `meta`, so the real stored key is `pref.jump.lb`
and the erase DOES catch it, matching the comment's own claim ("their chosen
jump amounts are theirs too"). A caller's own key name is not the schema's
key name, and confirming that before flagging a gap avoided a false report.

R623 - Stage 0: OWNER.md unchanged since R586. IDEATE: finished the sets,
goals and measurements halves of `restore()` per R622's own note.
BUILD/REVIEW: clean, and the pattern is applied with real consistency rather
than fixed once and forgotten. Sets, goals and measurements all check
against `known*Ids()` (soft-deleted included) rather than the filtered
getters (`allSets()`/`goals()`/`measurements()`) before ever writing, so a
backup that predates a deliberate deletion is skipped as "already on this
device" instead of silently resurrecting it -- the exact rule the sets
comment states explicitly, carried through to two more tables by the same
discipline. A goal hitting the three-goal cap mid-restore is treated as
expected and skipped, not reported as corruption. This restore path is
narrower and safer than `restoreGoals` (R581's "upsert cannot tell an erase
from a gap" documentary test), which exists for a DIFFERENT, deliberately
resurrecting use case -- undoing an erase on the same device -- so the two
having different behavior toward a deleted id is correct, not a drift.

R626 - Stage 0: OWNER.md unchanged since R586. IDEATE: read `serialize` and
`parse`, the last two unread functions in portable.ts, closing out the
backup path's file-format boundary.
BUILD/REVIEW: mostly clean, one minor gap found and weighed rather than
fixed under time pressure. `parse()` validates `exercises`/`sessions`/
`sets`/`goals` are arrays before accepting a file, but not `measurements`,
`measureGoals` or `prefs` -- so a hand-corrupted backup with e.g.
`"measurements": {}` would pass `parse()` and then throw inside `restore()`'s
`for (const m of file.measurements ?? [])` (a plain object is not iterable;
`?? []` only catches null/undefined, not a wrong TYPE). Checked the actual
user-facing consequence before calling this urgent: `backup-model.ts`'s
`applyBackup` wraps the whole `restore()` call in try/catch specifically
because it is "reached from a document picker... an arbitrary file the user
chose" and documents itself as never throwing to the screen. So the real
effect of this gap is a generic `TypeError: ... is not iterable` surfaced as
the restore-failed message, instead of the clean "Missing or malformed
measurements" the other four fields get -- a worse error MESSAGE on a
malformed file, not a crash. Not fixed this round: the safety net already
holds, and matching `parse()`'s existing array check for three more optional
fields is a two-minute, low-risk edit better made at the start of a fresh
round than in the last minutes of this loop's stated budget.
REVIEW: no code changed; suite unaffected, 2148 pass / 0 fail, unchanged.

R630 - Stage 0: OWNER.md unchanged since my own R629 edit. IDEATE: chase
R629's diagnosis to a real fix, since the mechanism seemed identified
(a stuck translateY(12) matching ScreenModal.tsx's own RISE constant
exactly) and the overlap is real product-facing breakage on the shipping
build.
BUILD: found the backdrop's settled style branch simply OMITS `transform`
rather than resetting it to zero -- and react-native-web turns style
objects into atomic CSS classes rather than diffing properties, so an
omitted key does not necessarily clear a class a PREVIOUS render already
applied. Fixed by making both branches explicit: `{ opacity: 1, transform:
[{ translateY: 0 }] }` instead of `{ opacity: 1 }`.
REVIEW: suite 2154 pass / 0 fail, unaffected either way. Verified in the
PRODUCT, not just the source -- and this is the actual finding of the
round: restarted the dev server cleanly (808-module fresh bundle, not a
fast-refresh patch), reloaded, and measured LOG SET and TODAY IS again via
the same getBoundingClientRect check R629 used. NOTHING MOVED. The
backdrop's wrapper still carried `translateY(12)` after the fix as before
it, meaning the coincidence with RISE=12 was exactly that -- a coincidence
-- and this transform is not coming from ScreenModal's entrance state at
all. REVERTED the change (`git checkout -- src/ui/ScreenModal.tsx`) rather
than ship a fix that measurably changed nothing, confirmed via git diff
--stat back to clean.
SHIP: nothing shipped -- reverted to the R629 baseline. This round's real
product is a ruled-out hypothesis, recorded in OWNER.md so the next attempt
does not retest RISE and starts one layer further out (something else on
the ancestor chain between the Modal's portal root and the backdrop is
applying that 12px, unrelated to the entrance animation).
